classes.name: Minn\Admin\ActivityChart
classes.doc:
The overview's activity chart: published posts and pages plus every
comment, counted per bar. A window over 45 days is drawn in weeks,
anything shorter in days; each bar carries the (from, to] GMT bounds
the drill-down asks for.

methods.name: bars
methods.doc: The bars for a window of days, counted from the database.
shapes: @return list<array{label: string, value: int, from: string, to: string}>

methods.name: bucket
methods.doc:
GMT stamps into bars, oldest first. Labels are site-local: the day
for daily bars, "Week of" the bar's first day for weekly ones.
shapes: @return list<array{label: string, value: int, from: string, to: string}>

classes.name: Minn\Admin\ActivityFeed
classes.doc:
What happened lately, as the overview and the bell tell it: the caller's
own recent posts and the latest comments, and the events behind one
chart bar. Also the visibility rule every comment row is put through.

methods.name: recent
methods.doc:
The overview's four most recent items, times already worded ("2 hours ago").

Oracle-caught quirk: the reference's recent-activity query runs with a
multi-type post_type plus perm=editable, and on that combination it
restricts EVERY status to post_author = caller, admins included,
published posts included. Authorless posts appear for nobody. The
engine reproduces the observed behavior, not the intent.

methods.name: between
methods.doc:
The events behind one chart bar, (from, to] GMT, newest first. Post
rows decode the RAW stored title; comment rows decode the texturized
one (the reference's asymmetry, kept).

methods.name: commentVisible
methods.doc: May this caller see a comment row that names its post?

methods.name: postTitle
methods.doc: A post's stored title, empty when the post is gone.

methods.name: displayName
methods.doc: A user's display name, empty when the user is gone.

methods.name: ownPosts
methods.doc: The caller's own posts, merged from a by-modified and a by-date window.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\AdminTypes

methods.name: commentsEnabled
methods.doc: Whether a UI post type still supports comments.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\App
classes.doc:
The Minn Admin app on disk: the symlinked dev copy the engine serves the
shell and assets from. Minn Admin is MIT, so reading its files is fine.

methods.name: switchedOff
methods.doc:
Whether the site has switched Minn Admin off: its plugin folder is in
wp-content/plugins (the record the reference keeps) and active_plugins
does not name it. A site that carries only the engine's bundle has no
such record and keeps its admin.

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: Where the bundle sits on disk.

methods.name: installed
methods.doc: Whether the bundle is on disk.

methods.name: version
methods.doc: The bundle's version from its plugin header.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: The absolute path of a readable file inside the app, or null.

methods.name: assetVersion
methods.doc: A self-busting asset version: app version plus file mtime.

methods.name: asset
methods.doc:
The absolute path and content type of an asset inside the app, or
null for anything missing or outside it.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\AppController
classes.doc:
Serves Minn Admin from the engine: the path-routed shell (every
sub-path renders the same page) and the app's assets. The nonce refresh
app.js asks admin-ajax.php for is the reference's own rest-nonce action
(Runtime\AjaxController).

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Admin\App $app, Minn\Admin\BootPayload $payload, Minn\Auth\Authenticator $authenticator, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, string $engineVersion, bool $off = false)

properties.name: off
properties.doc: the site has deactivated the Minn Admin plugin: the engine runs without an admin

methods.name: shell
methods.doc: Requires a signed-in user who can edit content; otherwise the login form.

methods.name: asset
methods.doc: One file of the app bundle, with its content type and caching headers.

methods.doc: The engine without an admin: the site keeps serving; the command that brings the admin back is named.

methods.doc:
The shell reproduces the structure of Minn Admin's own template.php
(an MIT file): pre-paint theme, inline window.MINN, mount point, app.js.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\Appearance
classes.doc:
A person's Minn Admin appearance: the colour scheme and its custom
token maps, stored where the app stores them (user meta
minn_admin_appearance, a serialized array) so the choice survives an
eject. The two WordPress-era switches, "Minn is the default admin" and
"Minn admin bar on the site", are always on here: there is no other
admin and no other bar, so the engine reports them true and ignores
writes to them.

constants.name: SLOTS
constants.doc: Scheme slots in the order the app lists them.

constants.name: BASE
constants.doc: The app's own Minn tokens, the fill for incomplete custom maps.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A user's saved appearance, normalised.
shapes: @return array{scheme: string, custom: array, defaultAdmin: bool, frontBar: bool, font: string}

methods.name: save
methods.doc: Merges the given keys over the stored map and writes it back; returns the normalised result.

methods.name: normalise
methods.doc: The appearance with every field valid and every missing one defaulted.

methods.name: hex
methods.doc: #rgb or #rrggbb to lowercase #rrggbb, or '' for anything else.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\BootPayload
classes.doc:
The window.MINN boot payload, assembled from the engine: the keys app.js
needs to boot and drive the wp/v2 surface, with capabilities from the
engine's own model.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, Minn\Admin\App $app, string $engineVersion, Minn\Admin\Appearance $appearance, Minn\Admin\HiddenIntegrations $hidden, Minn\Content\SiteIcon $icon, bool $blockTheme = false, ?Minn\Admin\Translations $translations = NULL)

constants.doc: Boot keys the plugin computes that point the app at wp-admin pages the engine does not serve.

methods.doc: The site's name, or Site when it has none.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: The window.MINN payload the app boots from, for one signed-in session.

methods.name: commerce
methods.doc:
Whether WooCommerce is running: the plugin's own answer when it gave one,
else whether the runtime loaded the class.

methods.name: caps
methods.doc:
What the app may show, each key a capability the reference gates the
same view on. The commerce caps mirror the plugin's own conditions:
WC loaded, the WC capability, and for coupons the store having them enabled.

methods.name: pluginPayload
methods.doc:
What Minn Admin's own boot_payload() computes when the plugin runs as
code on the runtime, so the app boots with the same keys on both
stacks (connectors, discussion defaults, roles, post formats, the
adapter flags). Engine-owned keys win; the withheld ones would send
the app to a wp-admin page the engine does not have.

methods.name: standHomeQuery
methods.doc:
The reference serves the app shell from the home query, so the global
post is the newest post while the payload is built; the comments
feature check reads it through the comments_open filter (a site that
closes comments on old posts reports the feature off when its newest
post is old).

methods.name: adapterSlices
methods.doc:
What Minn Admin's own adapters contribute when the plugin runs as code
on the runtime: plugin surfaces (Tools), editor panels, design
sources, editor commands, block forms. Absent, the app's fallbacks apply.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\HiddenIntegrations

(user meta minn_admin_hidden_integrations, "kind:id" => hidden-at) read
and written in the app's own shape so a choice made under WordPress
survives the swap and vice versa. The engine registers the core views
as hideable; plugin surfaces, editor panels, design sources, and slash
namespaces have no registry here, so hiding one is refused as
unregistered and a stored hide of one is simply not listed.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\LanguageChoices
classes.doc:
The language picker's markup. English always leads the list and carries the
empty value, because "no locale" and "American English" are the same choice.
When the picker also offers what could be downloaded, the two halves split
into named groups; otherwise every option sits in one flat list.

The attribute order is not tidy and is not ours to tidy: the English option
carries `data-installed` before `selected`, an installed translation carries
it after, and themes and plugins have been matching on that markup for
years.

methods.doc: The language select's HTML, installed languages first.
shapes: @param list<string> $installed locale codes the site already holds

offers, the core auto-update notice, and new registrations. Plugin and
theme update rows need an extension inventory the engine does not have
(a recorded gap); on the reference database those sections are empty,
so parity holds by construction.

while it is under two weeks old.

methods.name: translationCount

else the site's WPLANG, else en_US, exactly as the reference resolves it.
The app translates itself from a map of its source strings, read from the
JED catalogs Minn Admin's language packs install under
wp-content/languages/plugins (the bundle's own languages folder is the
fallback). Installing a pack fetches the release asset the bundle's
manifest names for that locale, checks its hash, and unpacks only that
locale's files, so an eject leaves the files WordPress would have written.

The boot burst of minn-admin/v1: the bell feed and its read marker, the
core status, and the one-round-trip boot-status the app starts from.
Every route sits behind the same capability floor (edit_posts) the
plugin declares.

methods.name: notifications
methods.doc: The bell feed.

methods.name: notificationsRead
methods.doc: Body {id} marks one read; {} marks all read.

methods.name: core
methods.doc: The core status.

methods.name: bootStatus
methods.doc:
The app's one-round-trip boot burst. Absent sections are the
contract's own fallback: the client loads a missing section
standalone. The engine serves what it can honestly answer and omits
the plugin-inventory sections it has no installation for.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\ApplicationPasswords
classes.doc:
Application passwords as the reference stores them: a serialized list in
the user's _application_passwords meta, each entry uuid, app_id, name,
password (a hash), created, last_used, last_ip. New passwords are 24
characters shown in groups of four; the stored hash is the reference's
own ($generic$, FastHash), so a password made on either stack works on
the other. Older hashes still verify, as the reference verifies them:
phpass (WordPress before 6.8, and the engine before this) and $wp$.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every application password of a user, as stored records without the hash's plain text.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: One record by uuid, or null.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Mints a password, stores its hash, and returns the record with the plain text once.
shapes: @return array{0: array<string, mixed>, 1: string} the stored record and the one-time plaintext

methods.name: rename
methods.doc: Renames one password; null when the uuid is unknown.

methods.name: touch
methods.doc: Records a use: the time and the address it came from.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes one password and returns its record; null when unknown.

methods.name: deleteAll
methods.doc: Removes every application password of a user and returns how many.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: The record a plaintext (spaces ignored) unlocks for the user, or null.

methods.name: generate
methods.doc: Twenty-four letters and digits.

methods.name: chunked
methods.doc: The plaintext as shown once: groups of four, space separated.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\AuthCookies
classes.doc:
The three cookies a sign-in sets: the auth cookie on the admin and
plugins paths (the secure variant over HTTPS, keyed off that scheme's
salt) and the logged_in cookie on the site root, which is the one REST
reads. Every value shares the username|expiration|token|hmac shape.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The hash suffixed onto every cookie name: md5 of the siteurl option.

methods.name: attach
methods.signature: attach(Minn\Http\Response $response, Minn\Content\UserRecord $user, int $expiration, string $token, bool $secure, bool $persistent = false): Minn\Http\Response
methods.doc: A non-persistent sign-in keeps the server expiry but sends session cookies the browser drops on close.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: The response with every sign-in cookie expired.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc: A cookie value under any scheme's salt (auth, secure_auth, logged_in).

classes.name: Minn\Auth\AuthFailure
classes.doc:
Why a request is not authenticated, as the reference's error code: a
missing or invalid cookie is rest_not_logged_in (the request is simply
anonymous); a good cookie with a bad nonce is rest_cookie_invalid_nonce.

methods.name: notLoggedIn
methods.doc: No usable session.

methods.name: invalidNonce
methods.doc: A session whose nonce did not verify.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Authenticated
classes.doc: A validated session: the user row and the raw session token behind it.

shapes: @param array<string, mixed>|null $applicationPassword the record that authenticated this call, when Basic auth did

params.name: applicationPassword
params.doc: the record that authenticated this call, when Basic auth did

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The signed-in user's id.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Authenticator
classes.doc:
Resolves the current user two ways. A page load carries the cookie alone;
a REST call must also carry a nonce bound to the same session.

constants.name: NOBODY
constants.doc: A real hash of a password nobody knows, checked against when the user does not exist so the answer takes as long either way.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: An authenticator over the shared database door.

methods.name: session
methods.doc: The session the cookie jar carries, or why there is none.

methods.name: rest
methods.doc: The session for a REST call: the cookie, then the nonce.

methods.name: restFromRequest
methods.doc:
A REST caller: the cookie session with its nonce first; failing that,
HTTP Basic credentials carrying an application password, which need no
nonce. A wrong Basic pair is reported as not logged in.

methods.name: applicationPassword
methods.doc: The user an Authorization: Basic header's application password unlocks, with the use recorded.

methods.name: basicCredentials
methods.doc: The login and password an Authorization: Basic header carries, or null.

methods.name: applicationPasswordsAvailable
methods.doc: Application passwords need HTTPS, unless plugin code says otherwise through the reference's filter.

methods.name: applicationPasswordsAvailableFor
methods.doc: Whether Basic auth may sign this user in; the runtime's filter has the last word.

methods.name: login
methods.doc: Username and password to a user row; no session is created here.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Capabilities
classes.doc:
The capability engine: a user's roles from {prefix}capabilities usermeta,
what those roles and the user's own capabilities grant, and the meta-capability mapping for
edit_post, delete_post, and read_post.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: The capability engine over the shared database door.

methods.name: roles
methods.doc: The role definitions.

methods.name: capsOf
methods.doc:
The capabilities stored on the user, as stored: role names and the
capabilities granted (or taken away) one by one.

methods.name: rolesOf
methods.doc:
The role slugs a user holds: each stored capability that names a
registered role, whatever it is set to (probe: the reference counts
'editor' => false as a role). One a plugin granted but never
registered does not count.

methods.name: allcapsOf
methods.doc:
Everything a user holds, as the reference's allcaps: each role's
capabilities in turn, then the user's own over them, role names
included, so a capability taken away one by one stays away and
current_user_can('administrator') is true for an administrator.
Values are as stored.

methods.name: can
methods.doc: Does the user hold every primitive the (possibly meta) capability maps to?

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The primitives a capability requires, all of which must be held.

methods.name: mapMore
methods.doc:
The rest of the reference's meta capabilities (captured with
map_meta_cap for an administrator, an editor and an author): each
names the primitive that decides it, refuses outright, or maps
through the object it is about. A name it does not know is its own
primitive.

methods.name: mapCommentCapability
methods.doc: A comment is edited as its post is (as editing posts, when the post is gone); a comment that does not exist, by no one. @return list<string>

methods.name: mapPostCapability
methods.doc:
A post's meta capability as the reference maps it (probe post-caps):
read_post needs read for a published post or one's own, the private
read for a private one, and what editing needs for anything else
(future, draft, pending, trash). Editing or deleting one's own post
needs the published capability while it is published or scheduled (or
was, before the trash), the plain one otherwise; someone else's, the
others capability, with the published one while it is published or
scheduled and the private one while it is private. The privacy policy
page needs manage_options as well.

methods.name: mapTermCapability
methods.doc:
A term capability on a plugin's taxonomy as the reference maps it
(probe rest-plugin-caps): the taxonomy's own name for it (edit_terms,
delete_terms, assign_terms), mapped in turn; nothing for a term that
does not exist or a default term's deletion. Null for the built-in
taxonomies, whose mapping is fixed.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Cookie
classes.doc:
The logged_in auth cookie: username|expiration|token|hmac, with
key  = HMAC-md5(username|fragment|expiration|token, logged_in salt)
hmac = HMAC-sha256(username|expiration|token, key)
and the session live in the user's session_tokens store.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: The cookie name this site uses: a hash of the siteurl option.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc: A sign-in cookie value for a user, expiry, and session token.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc: The session a cookie value proves, or null when any part fails.

methods.name: fromJar
methods.doc:
The logged_in cookie from a request's cookie jar: the canonical name
first, then any logged_in cookie, since tooling may send a name
derived from a different host.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\FastHash
classes.doc:
The reference's hash for high-entropy secrets ("$generic$", WordPress 6.8
and later): a 30-byte keyed BLAKE2b digest (sodium's generic hash, keyed
by the scheme's fixed label) in URL-safe base64 without padding. Reset
keys and application passwords are stored this way, so a secret minted
on either stack verifies on the other. Pinned against hashes the
reference made (tests/unit/auth-hashes.php). Without the sodium
extension nothing can be hashed or verified this way.

methods.name: available
methods.doc: Whether this PHP can make and check these hashes (the sodium extension).

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The "$generic$" hash of a secret.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a secret matches a "$generic$" hash; false for any other kind of hash.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\LoginThrottle
classes.doc:
Failed sign-ins per address, so a password guesser meets a wall: twenty
failures in fifteen minutes and the address waits out the window. The
counters live in the options table (autoload off), one row per address,
as "window start:count"; a successful sign-in clears the row.

methods.name: retryAfter
methods.doc: Seconds the address must wait, or null when it may try.

methods.name: recordFailure
methods.doc: Counts one failed sign-in from an address within the current window.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets an address's failures.

methods.name: read
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: int} window start and failure count

methods.name: prune
methods.doc: Rows whose window has passed are dead weight; drop them now and then.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Nonce
classes.doc:
The wp_rest nonce: ten characters of HMAC-md5(tick|wp_rest|uid|token)
under the nonce salt, accepted for the current tick and the one before.

methods.name: tick
methods.doc: The current half-life tick a nonce is bound to.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: A wp_rest nonce for a user and session token at the current tick.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a nonce is valid at this tick or the one before.

methods.name: at
methods.doc: The nonce for a given tick.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Password
classes.doc:
The stored password scheme. A modern "$wp$2y$..." value is bcrypt over
base64(HMAC-sha384(password, "wp-sha384")); a bare "$2y$" value is plain
bcrypt. Legacy phpass "$P$" hashes are not verified.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a stored hash of either scheme.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A stored hash in the modern scheme: "$wp" plus bcrypt over the pre-hash.

methods.name: fragment
methods.doc:
The four characters of the hash the cookie key is derived from: the
LAST four for a "$wp$" hash, offset 8 for legacy phpass. Getting this
wrong yields a cookie that verifies nowhere while every other check
passes, so both branches are pinned by the auth suite.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PasswordReset
classes.doc:
Password reset keys in the reference's storage shape: user_activation_key
holds "time:hash", the key itself travels in the email link and is good
for a day. The hash is the reference's own ($generic$, FastHash), so a
link either stack sent works on the other. Older shapes still verify: a
phpass hash (WordPress before 6.8) and the engine's former $minn$ HMAC.
A matching key stored without its time is expired, as the reference
treats it.

methods.name: issue
methods.doc: Mints a key, stores its hash, returns the key for the link.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc:
A new key and the value that stores it (the time it was issued and its
hash), for a caller that saves it itself.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: True when the key matches the stored hash and has not expired.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: "valid", "expired" (a matching key past its lifetime, a day unless given, or stored without a time), or "invalid".

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets a user's reset key.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The stored hash for a new key: the reference's own, or phpass (which it also reads) without sodium.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Phpass
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ($P$), from Openwall's public description of the
scheme: a log2 iteration count, an eight-character salt, and an iterated
MD5 in phpass's own base-64 alphabet. The reference still verifies these
for application passwords, which makes them the portable choice.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A portable phpass hash of a password.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a portable phpass hash.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc: phpass's base-64: 6 bits at a time, low bits first, no padding.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PortableHash
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ("$P$"), the shape the reference stores in
the post-password cookie: an iteration count character, an eight
character salt, and MD5 iterated over salt and password, encoded in
phpass's own base64 alphabet. Implemented from the published algorithm
so cookies are accepted in both directions.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The reference's cookies carry 2^13 iterations; it accepts nothing weaker.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a portable hash from the published algorithm.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\RegisteredCaps
classes.doc:
The capability names a plugin's post type or taxonomy registered, read
from the runtime's registry once plugins are loaded (probe
rest-plugin-caps): a type's cap object (create_posts, edit_posts,
publish_posts...) and whether it maps meta capabilities, a taxonomy's
term capabilities. Null for the built-in ones, whose names the engine
knows, and when no runtime is up.

methods.name: ofType
methods.doc: A plugin's post type, or null.

methods.name: ofTaxonomy
methods.doc: A plugin's taxonomy, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Roles
classes.doc:
Role definitions from the site's {prefix}user_roles option, parsed by a
bounded scan of the serialized blob, with the seeded contract copy as the
fallback for a fresh install.

methods.name: level
methods.doc: The wp_user_level stored beside the capabilities meta.

methods.name: serializeSingle
methods.doc: The {role: true} capabilities meta in its serialized form.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Drops the parsed map so the next read sees a rewritten option.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every role with its name and capabilities, from the option or the shipped defaults.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
Each role is a string key over a two-entry array of "name" and
"capabilities"; the capabilities map is {cap: bool}. Null when the
blob has another shape, so the caller can fall back.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Salts
classes.doc:
The site's own secret material, read from the constants wp-config.php
defines, so the engine keys off exactly what the install used.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: True when every key and salt is defined and none is the installer's placeholder.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The key and salt of a scheme joined, as the reference feeds them to its HMACs.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: HMAC-md5 under the scheme's salt: the primitive every cookie and nonce is built from.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Sessions
classes.doc:
The session_tokens usermeta store: {sha256(token): {expiration, ip, ua,
login}}. Read by a bounded scan of the serialized blob and written by
serializing it ourselves, so stored data is never executed.

methods.name: generateToken
methods.doc: A 43-character token; only sha256(token) is ever stored or compared.

methods.name: isLive
methods.doc: Whether a session token is still stored and unexpired for a user.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a session, pruning expired ones, and returns the raw token.

methods.name: destroyAll
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user (a password change).

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Removes one session; true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyKey
methods.doc: Removes the session stored under a key (the sha256 of its token); true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyOthers
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user except the one stored under the given key.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
Every stored session of a user, keyed by token hash. Each entry keeps
its stored text under raw, so writing the store back leaves sessions
this request did not make exactly as they were, including anything a
plugin attached to them.
shapes: @return array<string, array{expiration: int, ip: string, ua: string, login: int, raw: string}>

methods.name: serialize
methods.doc: The map in PHP's serialized form: stored entries as they were read, new ones key by key in the order given.

methods.name: entry
methods.doc: One new session: integers for the times, strings for the rest. @param array<string, int|string> $entry

classes.name: Minn\Auth\SignIn
classes.doc:
The door itself: what a sign-in surface needs beyond checking a
password. Sessions are minted here, the three cookies ride out on the
response, and the failure counter behind the throttle is kept in one
place with the session store and the cookie jar it protects.

methods.name: retryAfter
methods.doc: Seconds this address must wait before another attempt, or null when it may try now.

methods.name: recordFailure
methods.doc: Counts one failed attempt from an address.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The cookie-name hash the sign-in cookies, the postpass cookie, and the reset cookie share.

methods.name: establish
methods.doc: Signs a user in for two days: a new session, and the response with the cookies attached for the browser session.

methods.name: remember
methods.doc: Signs a user in for fourteen days, the cookies kept past the browser session: "remember me", and the one-time login link.

methods.name: end
methods.doc: Ends one session and clears the cookies from the response.

methods.name: endAll
methods.doc: Ends every session of a user (a password reset) and clears the cookies from the response.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: The response with the sign-in cookies cleared.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: A session longer than the two-day default is one to keep past the browser session, as the reference's remember-me does.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\TypeCapabilities
classes.doc:
The capability names a post type's permissions are built from. Posts and
pages own their families (edit_posts, edit_others_pages, ...). Navigation
menus fold every one of them onto edit_theme_options, which is why an
editor may read a menu and only an administrator may change one; the
reference's own registration says the same thing. A plugin's type
answers with the names it registered.

constants.name: FOLDED
constants.doc: Types whose whole cap family collapses to a single name.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: A cap name built from the post/page family, folded when the type folds, or the plugin type's own name for it (probe rest-plugin-caps).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: The capability creating a post of the type needs: the edit capability, or a plugin type's create_posts.

methods.name: plural
methods.doc: The capability stem of a type: pages for page, posts for everything else.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc: The edit capability of a type.

methods.name: editOthers
methods.doc: The edit-others capability of a type.

methods.name: publish
methods.doc: The publish capability of a type.

methods.name: readPrivate
methods.doc: The read-private capability of a type.

classes.name: Minn\Autoloader
classes.doc: PSR-4 for the Minn namespace: Minn\Http\Request lives at src/Minn/Http/Request.php.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers the PSR-4 loader for the Minn namespace.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Attributes
classes.doc:
The JSON object a block delimiter carries, read in place. Rewriting one
block's attributes must not disturb the rest of the markup, so callers
take the object's exact substring rather than reserializing the document.

methods.name: objectAt
methods.doc: The JSON object starting at $at, brace-matched through any strings; null when there is none.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Block
classes.doc:
One parsed block. A null name is freeform HTML between blocks. The
innerContent list holds the block's own HTML chunks in order, with a
null placeholder wherever an inner block sits.

methods.name: freeform
methods.doc: A block-less run of HTML, as the parser reads it.

methods.name: attr
methods.doc: One attribute, or the default.

methods.name: className
methods.doc: The class names declared on the block's own attributes (className).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\BlockName
classes.doc: The block name rules: a string, lower-case, `namespace/name`.

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: Why a block name is invalid, or null when it is fine.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Context
classes.doc:
What the template blocks render against: the resolution, the main
query's posts, and a stack of "current post" frames pushed by post
templates and comment templates as they loop.

shapes: @param list<PostRecord> $posts the main query's page of posts

params.name: posts
params.doc: the main query's page of posts

methods.name: forRest
methods.doc: A context for rendering outside a page: the home resolution and no posts.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The post being rendered, innermost first.

methods.name: pushPost
methods.doc: Enters a post's scope.

methods.name: popPost
methods.doc: Leaves the innermost post's scope.

methods.name: inLoop
methods.doc: Inside a post template loop (as opposed to the singular view).

methods.name: comment
methods.doc: The comment being rendered, if any.

methods.name: withComment
methods.doc: Enters or leaves a comment's scope.

methods.name: paged
methods.doc: The page number being rendered.

methods.name: totalPages
methods.doc: How many pages the listing makes.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Archives
classes.doc: core/archives: the months that have published posts, newest first, with their counts when asked (showPostCounts).

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Categories
classes.doc: core/categories: the non-empty categories as a list, by name.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Dates
classes.doc: Site-local dates the way the dynamic blocks print them.

methods.name: iso
methods.doc: ISO 8601 with the site's offset, from a site-local MySQL datetime.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The date_format option applied to a site-local MySQL datetime.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\LatestComments
classes.doc: core/latest-comments: the newest approved comments with avatar, meta, and a 20-word excerpt.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

methods.name: excerpt
methods.doc: The first twenty words, with an ellipsis when there were more.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\LatestPosts
classes.doc: core/latest-posts: the newest published posts as a list, optionally dated.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Search
classes.doc:
core/search: the site search form. The button sits outside or inside
the field and shows text or the search icon; the block's colour and
font presets land on the button (font family on the input too). The
input id comes from the shared request counter.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\SocialLinks
classes.doc:
core/social-links and core/social-link. The list keeps its stored
wrapper and gains the flex layout classes; each link renders from its
parent's icon colours and the service's icon. The icons are the
reference's rendered output captured as data (src/data/social-icons.json,
the upstream set is CC0); an unknown service gets the share icon.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers the block and its links with the renderer.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\SyncedPattern
classes.doc: core/block: a synced pattern, rendered from the wp_block post it references.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\TagCloud
classes.doc:
core/tag-cloud: non-empty tags by name, sized from 8pt to 22pt in
proportion to their counts (every tag at 8pt when the counts are equal).

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The block's HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\Comments
classes.doc: comments, comments-title, comment-template, the comment-* blocks, and the comment form.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers this family's blocks with the renderer.

methods.name: comments
methods.doc: Nothing at all when the post has no comments and takes none.

methods.name: list
methods.signature: list(array $all, int $parent, int $depth, Minn\Blocks\Block $block, Minn\Blocks\Renderer $renderer): string

methods.name: formWithPlugins
methods.doc:
With plugins loaded, the form is comment_form()'s, as the reference's
block renders it: the block theme's button in its defaults, the
block's classes on the respond wrapper, and every comment_form hook a
plugin uses to add its fields (a spam plugin's hidden check, a
consent box) fired on the way.

methods.name: visible
methods.doc:
The approved plain comments and the reader's own held ones, oldest
first: held comments by the signed-in account, by the email the
commenter cookie remembers, or by the email of the held comment a
link names with its moderation hash (wp_hash of its GMT date).

methods.name: linkedEmail
methods.doc: The author email of the held comment ?unapproved= names, when ?moderation-hash= proves the link came from posting it in the last ten minutes. @param array<string, mixed> $query

methods.name: approved
shapes: @return list<CommentRecord> approved plain comments, oldest first

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\Navigation
classes.doc:
navigation, navigation-link, page-list. A navigation block's items come
from its inner blocks, the wp_navigation post it references, the newest
published wp_navigation post, or (when none of those exist) the first
classic nav_menu; a responsive menu wraps them in the overlay markup
the reference emits.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers this family's blocks with the renderer.

methods.name: responsive
methods.signature: responsive(string $nav, string $label, string $list, int $id, bool $hasIcon, string $colors): string
methods.doc:
The overlay form of the menu: the open button, the modal container the
interactivity runtime drives, the close button, and the list inside.
Whitespace matches the reference's template byte for byte.

methods.name: items
methods.doc:
The menu's items. Link-shaped blocks render as their own list
items; any other block is wrapped in a plain item.

methods.name: presetClasses
shapes: @return list<string> the colour and font-size preset classes the block's attributes declare

methods.name: overlayColors
methods.doc: The overlay's colour classes, from the overlay* attributes.

methods.name: ancestorsOf
shapes: @return list<int> the ids of the current page's ancestors

methods.name: pageItems
methods.signature: pageItems(array $tree, int $parent, int $currentId, array $ancestors, string $submenuColors = ' has-text-color has-contrast-color has-background has-base-background-color'): string
methods.doc:
A page list dresses its items as navigation items only while it is
rendering inside a navigation block: submenu toggles, the item
classes, and the interactivity directives all belong to the nav. On
its own (wp/v2/navigation serves one that way) the reference emits
plain list items and a bare submenu list.

methods.name: navParent
methods.signature: navParent(array $page, string $marker, string $home, string $link, string $children): string

methods.name: enqueueView
methods.doc: Interactive navigation markup brings the block's view module with it, as on the reference.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\PostBlocks
classes.doc: The post-* blocks: they render the context's current post.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Layout
classes.doc:
The layout-support classes the reference adds at render time. Every
container carries is-layout-{type} and {block}-is-layout-{type}; flex and
grid layouts with rules of their own also carry a wp-container-* class
whose suffix names their generated stylesheet.

That suffix is a digest the engine cannot reproduce (its inputs are not
observable), so the engine derives its own deterministic suffix from the
layout attributes. Same shape, different value: recorded in the contract,
and the parity suites normalise it.

block is a freeform block that renders as-is.

galleries, style variations, and search inputs from ONE counter that runs
across every block rendered in the request (a list response keeps
counting from post to post), so the counter lives here, not on any block.
Leaf helpers with no renderer in hand reach it through current().

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\StyleEngine
classes.doc:
What a block's style object comes to, as the reference's style engine
reads it (probe style-engine): the declarations each style property
makes and the class names a preset or a set colour earns.

- Groups in the order background, colour, border, shadow, dimensions,
spacing, typography, and properties in their order within a group.
- A value goes into the declarations as given. Whether it makes CSS is
for the declarations holder to judge.
- A preset ("var:preset|color|base") becomes a custom property only
where the definition names one for its kind (a colour, a gradient,
spacing, a font size or family, a shadow, a dimension, a border radius,
a border side's colour). Elsewhere it makes nothing, and with presets
turned into class names it makes none anywhere.
- Sides and corners ("padding" => ["top" => ...]) name their own
properties in the order given. Border sides come after the whole
border.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Installer
classes.doc:
The swap, both ways. Install parks WordPress's own files beside the
webroot, lays the engine and its shape files down, and leaves
wp-config.php and wp-content untouched; eject puts every parked file
back and removes what install wrote. The install record at the webroot
(.minn-install.php) is what eject works from. Preflight says what the site will and
will not get before anything moves.

constants.name: RECORD
constants.doc:
The install record sits at the webroot, so every site keeps its own
(a symlinked minn/ is shared between sites) and an engine update
cannot take it. It is PHP that returns first, so a web request for it
prints nothing, and it names the webroot it belongs to.

constants.name: RECORD_HEAD
constants.value: '<?php return; // Minn Engine\'s install record: what `wp minn eject` puts back. ?> '

constants.name: LEGACY_RECORD
constants.doc: Where installs kept it before: read from a site's own minn/ copy, never through a shared symlink.

constants.name: CORE_ENTRIES
constants.doc: The files WordPress keeps at the webroot, moved aside as a set.

constants.name: WRITTEN_TREES
constants.doc: Webroot trees install writes (shape files + require placeholders) and eject deletes before restoring the park.

constants.name: LEGACY_PUBLISHED
constants.doc:
Leftover webroot copies from an earlier installer that published
assets outside minn/. Eject still deletes them.

constants.name: SKIP
constants.doc: Development-only trees inside the engine or the admin bundle that never ship.

## OPTIONS

[<theme>...]
: One or more themes to update.

[--all]
: If set, all themes that have updates will be updated.

[--exclude=<theme-names>]
: Comma separated list of theme names that should be excluded from updating.

[--minor]
: Only perform updates for minor releases.

[--patch]
: Only perform updates for patch releases.

[--format=<format>]
: Render output in a particular format.
---
default: table
options:
- table
- csv
- json
- summary
---

[--version=<version>]
: If set, the theme will be updated to the specified version.

[--dry-run]
: Preview which themes would be updated.

default: 1

[--field=<field>]

[--format=<format>]

---
default: table

---

character into its entity; staticize() turns each listed sequence in the
text (outside tags, and outside code and pre) into a CDN image, longest

classes.name: Minn\Content\Excerpt
classes.doc:
The reference's generated excerpt, as captured from probe posts: - Only text-bearing blocks contribute. Containers (group, columns, column, media-text) pass their allowed children through; anything not on the list vanishes with everything inside it (code, details, buttons, images, galleries, covers, dynamic blocks, and the nested list-item, so a modern list contributes nothing while a classic one does). - The text stops at the first (in a feed it runs on). - Block-level tags read as spaces; inline tags (and
) read as nothing. - Whitespace collapses, 55 words, an ellipsis when cut, wrapped in

, texturized (a feed texturizes first, so its inline code stays raw). A hand-written excerpt skips the block filter.

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
The more tag ends a listing's excerpt but not a feed's, and a feed
texturizes before the tags go (so inline code keeps straight quotes)
where a listing texturizes the finished text.

methods.name: forFeed
methods.doc:
The excerpt as a feed carries it: the whole content counts (no stop at
the more tag), texturize runs before the tags are stripped, and the
paragraph is not texturized again.

methods.name: source
methods.doc: The stored excerpt, or the content's allowed markup.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: The first 55 words with tags gone, an ellipsis when cut, empty for none.

methods.name: recordRendered
methods.doc:
A generated excerpt drops the disallowed blocks first and renders the
rest before trimming, so the allowed blocks count as rendered on the
page: the stylesheet prints their block styles even when nothing of
theirs survives the trim.

classes.name: Minn\Content\PostSlugs
classes.doc:
Which slug a live post may take beside the others, as the reference
settles it (probe insert-defaults). A flat type's slugs are its own: a
post, a page and a plugin's type may share one. A hierarchical type's
are its own and its attachments' under the same parent. An attachment's
are every post's. Never free: the feed names and embed; for a
hierarchical type, a number or a page number (2, page2); for posts, a
number a date archive would answer to: any number when the permalink
structure begins with the post name, a month (below 13) when the post
name follows the year, a day (below 32) when it follows the month. A post
keeps a number it already has. A taken slug gets the first free -2, -3
form, cut (and stripped of a trailing hyphen) to fit the column's 200
characters. The slug is taken as given, not sanitized.

Closes what markup leaves open and drops what it closes without opening, as the reference's force_balance_tags does, from its observed rules (contracts/runtime.md "The content filters"): tag names are lowercased; a void element is written self-closed (bare as
, with attributes as , one already self-closed as given); reopening the innermost open element closes it first unless it is one of the ten that may contain themselves; a closer shuts every element opened inside its own; a closer with nothing to close goes; what is still open at the end closes in reverse. Script and style text is left as it is, and a "<" not followed by a name is text.

classes.name: Minn\Context
classes.doc:
One request, as a value: the database door, who is asking, what they
may do, and where the site's files are. It is built once at the front
door and handed down, so nothing below has to reach for a global to
learn what request it is answering.

The reader is the one part that differs by surface (REST resolves it
from the nonce-bound caller, the front from the session cookie), so a
context is made with the reader its surface resolved.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, ?Minn\Http\Request $request, Minn\Content\Reader $reader, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, string $engineDir, string $absPath, string $version)

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: the minn/ folder: the engine's own files

properties.name: absPath
properties.doc: the site root with a trailing slash, as ABSPATH holds it

properties.name: version
properties.doc: the WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks

methods.name: withReader
methods.doc: The same context with another reader, for a surface that resolves one later.

methods.name: contentDir
methods.doc: wp-content under the site root.

methods.name: themesDir
methods.doc: The themes folder under wp-content.

methods.name: isSecure
methods.doc: Whether the request is over HTTPS.

classes.name: Minn\Cron\Cron
classes.doc:
The engine's scheduled work: scheduled posts go live when their time
comes, the cron option's due events fire, expired throttle rows and
transients are swept, and the daily auto-update check runs. Triggered
by wp-cron.php, `wp minn cron`, `minn cron`, or a front request that
finds something due (after its response is sent). One run at a time,
through a short-lived lock option.

Firing the cron option's due hooks needs the booted runtime and the
facade, so it arrives as a closure the caller supplies (from the front
pipeline, or the CLI once it has booted the runtime); with none, only
the engine's own scheduled posts and sweeps run.

shapes: @param ?Closure(): int $fireDueEvents fires the cron option's due hooks and returns how many ran

params.name: fireDueEvents
params.doc: fires the cron option's due hooks and returns how many ran

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, string $contentDir, string $homeUrl, string $version, ?Closure $fireDueEvents): self
methods.doc:
The one recipe every trigger builds from: the post writer, the
updater over the site's wp-content, and the runtime's firing closure.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs every due job; the report lists what happened. @return list<string>

methods.name: due
methods.doc: True when a scheduled post's time has come or the cron option holds a due event.

methods.name: fireEvents
methods.doc:
Fires the due events through the runtime. A callback that throws
ends the events step, as a fatal ends the reference's cron request;
the event was already rescheduled or removed, so it does not repeat
on the next trigger, and the sweeps still run.

methods.name: applyAutoUpdates
methods.doc:
The daily auto-update pass. The stamp is written before the pass so
a failing update is retried tomorrow, not on every trigger; what was
refused is reported by name.

methods.name: publishDue
methods.doc:
A scheduled post goes live as the reference publishes it: status only,
dates and modified untouched, term counts refreshed. With plugins
loaded it goes through check_and_publish_future_post, the reference's
own publish_future_post work, so they hear publish_post and the
transition; a plugin that throws on one post holds back no other.

classes.name: Minn\Db
classes.doc:
The one door to the database. Every query is a prepared statement; the
placeholder types are derived from the PHP values, so callers pass plain
arrays and never spell out "issd". A parameter that is a list stands for
a list of values: its "?" becomes as many placeholders as the list is
long, so "post_type IN (?)" takes the types themselves.

properties.name: inTransaction
properties.doc: Whether a transaction this door opened is still open, so a nested call joins it instead of starting another.

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
The connection the request being answered speaks through: its
runtime's own, so nothing deep in a render can reach a connection
belonging to another request. With no runtime (the command line, the
unit suite) it is the process's own connection.

This is the one place in the core that asks the runtime anything; the
alternative is a database door threaded through every renderer, and
the seam is here until that threading is done.

methods.name: shared
methods.doc: The one connection for this process, opened from wp-config's constants on first use.

methods.name: connection
methods.doc: The underlying mysqli handle, for the facade's wpdb.

methods.name: escape
methods.doc: A value escaped for direct interpolation into SQL, for callers that build their own statements.

methods.name: prefix
methods.doc: The table prefix from wp-config.

methods.name: table
methods.doc: `posts` becomes `wp_posts`; the prefix comes from wp-config.php.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc: Every row of a prepared query, as associative arrays.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: The first row of a prepared query, or null.

methods.name: value
methods.doc: The first column of the first row, or null when there is no row.

methods.name: execute
methods.doc: Runs a write and returns the affected row count.

methods.name: expand
methods.doc:
Rewrites every "?" whose parameter is a list into that many
placeholders, and flattens the values to match, so "IN (?)" becomes
"IN (?, ?, ?)". An empty list becomes NULL, which nothing is IN, so a
caller that means "everything" when the list is empty says so itself.

methods.name: transaction
methods.doc:
Runs a unit of work as one transaction: everything the closure writes
lands, or none of it does. The closure's return value is passed back.

A transaction already open is joined rather than nested, since the
storage engine has no nested transactions; the outermost call is the
one that commits. A table that cannot do transactions (MyISAM, which
no WordPress core table uses) silently keeps each write, which is the
behaviour there was before this existed.

methods.name: insertId
methods.doc: The id the last INSERT produced.

methods.name: option
methods.doc: One option's raw value, or null when it is unset.

methods.name: placeholders
methods.doc:
The statement split into placeholders and everything between them. A
"?" inside a quoted string is text, not a placeholder.

classes.name: Minn\Engine
classes.doc:
The engine's front door. An unmodified wp-config.php ends by requiring
wp-settings.php, which is the engine's own boot file; it hands off here.
REST is dispatched first (from the path or from ?rest_route=), then the
admin, the login endpoint, and finally the public site.

constants.name: WP_VERSION
constants.doc: The WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks; wp-includes/version.php says the same.

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: the minn/ folder: the engine's own files (assets, data, the admin bundle)

methods.name: serve
methods.doc:
The front door: answer the request that arrived and send it. This is
the only place the engine touches the world, so everything under it
is a function of a request, callable more than once in a process.

methods.name: answer
methods.doc:
The response for one request, whatever happens: a database that
cannot be reached, salts that are not set, or a failure anywhere
underneath, each answered in the language the request asked in.

methods.name: restRoute
methods.doc: The REST route a request names, in the path or in ?rest_route=, or null when it is not a REST request.

methods.name: bootRuntimeForRest
methods.doc:
The WordPress runtime for a REST request: the caller the REST layer
resolved is the reader, plugins load, and rest_api_init fires so
their routes answer after the engine's own.

methods.name: adoptSettledUser
methods.doc:
The user plugin code settled (determine_current_user) as the REST
caller, as the reference's cookie check leaves it: a request a
plugin signs in by its own token is that user; a sign-in cookie
vouches only for its own user (another one fails its nonce, and
without a nonce the request is nobody, plugin code included).

methods.name: handle
methods.doc: The response the request's own surface produces: REST, then the admin, the login endpoint, and the public site.

methods.name: frontPipeline
methods.signature: frontPipeline(Minn\Context $context, Minn\Http\Request $request, Minn\Runtime\Runtime $runtime, Minn\Content\Users $users, Minn\Auth\Sessions $sessions, Minn\Auth\Cookie $cookie, Minn\Auth\Authenticator $authenticator, Minn\Admin\App $app, mixed $session, Minn\Front\Resolver $resolver, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, ?Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, ?Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme $classicTheme): Minn\Http\Response
methods.doc: The themed front, admin app, and probe pipeline; split out so a mid-request ServeLogin signal can unwind it cleanly.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Extension
classes.doc:
What a Minn extension is: a class the engine constructs once per request
and asks to register what it provides. Everything it can touch is on the
Seams object; there is no global state to reach for.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers the extension's seams.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Extensions
classes.doc:
Where the engine looks for the seams an extension registered. The
request's runtime holds them, so nothing here keeps state of its own
and a request cannot inherit the extensions of the one before it.
Before the front has loaded any (REST and the command line never do)
there are none.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Installs the seams for this request.

methods.name: runner
methods.doc: The engine side of the seams, if any.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Loader
classes.doc:
Finds extensions under wp-content/plugins and wp-content/mu-plugins,
decides which are active, autoloads them, and asks each to register.
An extension that throws is logged and skipped; the page still renders.

methods.name: found
methods.doc: Every extension manifest on disk.

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Forgets the cached activation list after an option write.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The manifests that are active.
shapes: @return list<Manifest> the extensions this site has switched on

methods.name: declaredTypes
methods.doc: Extra post types declared by active extensions, keyed by slug.

methods.name: replacements
methods.doc: Which active WordPress plugin files an extension stands in for. @return array<string, string> plugin file => extension slug
shapes: @return array<string, string> plugin file => extension slug

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers every active extension's seams.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Manifest
classes.doc:
minn.json, read as data. A folder under wp-content/plugins (or
mu-plugins) with this file is an extension; the same folder may also be
a WordPress plugin, in which case the two share a name and a version.

{
"name": "Block Visibility for Minn",
"version": "1.0.0",
"license": "MIT",
"replaces": ["block-visibility/block-visibility.php"],
"autoload": {"Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\": "src/"},
"extension": "Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\Extension",
"shortcodes": ["example_tag"],
"blocks": ["vendor/block"],
"types": [{"slug": "zz_note", "name": "Notes", "rest_base": "zz-note"}]
}

"replaces" names the WordPress plugin files whose behaviour this
extension stands in for; the extension is active whenever one of them is
in active_plugins, or when its own folder is listed there, or when it is
named in the minn_active_extensions option. "shortcodes" and "blocks"
are the content tokens preflight treats as provided instead of missing.
"types" are extra post types the engine should serve on wp/v2.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $slug, string $dir, string $name, string $version, string $license, array $replaces, array $autoload, string $extension, string $covers = '', array $shortcodes = array ( ), array $blocks = array ( ), array $types = array ( ))

properties.name: covers
properties.doc: what of the replaced plugin this provides, when not all of it

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A folder's minn.json, or null when there is none.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Registrations
classes.doc: Everything the extensions registered for this request, handed from Seams to the runner once.

constructor.signature: __construct(array $blockGates, array $blockFilters, array $shortcodes, array $contentFilters, array $head, array $footer, array $bodyClasses, array $documentFilters, ?Closure $title)

classes.name: Minn\Extension\SeamRunner
classes.doc:
The engine's side of the seams: what the loader collected, called at the
right moment and in registration order. An extension never sees this
class; it sees Seams, which is only the eight registrations.

methods.name: allowsBlock
methods.doc: Whether every block gate lets a block render.

methods.name: filterBlock
methods.doc: A block's HTML through every block filter.

methods.name: filterContent
methods.doc:
Shortcodes, then the content filters, over rendered post content. An
extension's filter is promised the post as a row (contracts/extensions.md),
so a record is handed over as one.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: The document title through the title filter.

methods.name: head
methods.doc: What the extensions add to the head.

methods.name: footer
methods.doc: What the extensions add to the footer.

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc: The body classes the extensions add.

methods.name: filterDocument
methods.doc: The whole document through every document filter.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Seams
classes.doc:
Where an extension can take part in a request: eight typed registrations
and the request they run in. This is the whole surface an extension sees.
The engine calls what was registered through SeamRunner, at the right
moment and in registration order.

methods.name: gateBlocks
methods.doc: Decides whether a block renders at all; the first gate to answer false wins.

methods.name: filterBlocks
methods.doc: Rewrites a block's rendered markup.

methods.name: shortcode
methods.doc: Renders [tag attr="…"]content[/tag] wherever it appears in post content.

methods.name: filterContent
methods.doc: Rewrites rendered post content (after blocks and shortcodes).

methods.name: head
methods.doc: Markup for the document head (a style, a meta tag, a script).

methods.name: footer
methods.doc: Markup before </body>.

methods.name: bodyClass
methods.doc: Adds a body class.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: Replaces the document title; receives the engine's own.

methods.name: filterDocument
methods.doc: Rewrites the whole themed document before it is sent (what an output buffer did on the reference).

methods.name: registrations
methods.doc: What was registered, for the engine's runner. Extensions have no reason to call this.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Shortcodes
classes.doc:
The shortcode syntax in rendered content: [tag], [tag attr="v" flag],
[tag]inner[/tag], and [[tag]] as the escaped literal. Unregistered tags
stay as written, which is what the reference shows for a plugin that is
not installed.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Content with the registered shortcodes run.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: A shortcode's attributes parsed, curly quotes included.
shapes: @return array<string, string> named attributes; bare words keyed by position

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Charset
classes.doc:
A feed document as UTF-8. The encoding comes from a byte-order mark,
then the XML declaration, then the Content-Type charset, then UTF-8; a
document in another encoding is converted and its declaration rewritten,
so the parser only ever reads UTF-8.

methods.name: toUtf8
methods.doc: The document converted to UTF-8, with no byte-order mark.

methods.name: declared
methods.doc: The encoding the XML declaration names, if it names one.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Dates
classes.doc: Feed dates (RFC 822, W3C, and the looser forms feeds carry) as Unix timestamps; a date without a zone is UTC.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The timestamp, or null when the text names no date.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Document
classes.doc:
A parsed feed: the tree and the format it was recognized as (the
reference's type bits: RSS 0.90 1, the 0.9x versions 2 to 32, RSS 1.0 64,
RSS 2.0 128, Atom 0.3 256, Atom 1.0 512), with the lookups the feed
object is built on: the root's children, the channel's, the image's, and
the items of every format the document carries.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: A document read from bytes; the type is NONE when it parsed but is no feed.

methods.name: fromTree
methods.doc: A document over a tree already parsed (a cached feed), its type read from the root.

methods.name: root
methods.doc: The root element (rss, rdf:RDF or feed), or null.

methods.name: channel
methods.doc: The channel element: an RSS channel, or the Atom feed itself.

methods.name: image
methods.doc: The image element: inside an RSS 2.0 channel, beside an RSS 1.0 one.

methods.name: feedTags
methods.doc: Children of the root element by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: channelTags
methods.doc: Children of the channel by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: imageTags
methods.doc: Children of the image by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: items
methods.doc:
Every item node, in document order: Atom 1.0 and 0.3 entries, RSS 1.0
and 0.90 items beside the channel, RSS 2.0 items inside it.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\FeedError
classes.doc: A feed that could not be read: the message is the one the reference reports.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Iri
classes.doc:
URLs in feeds: a reference resolved against its base (RFC 3986), then
normalized the way the reference prints them: scheme and host in lower
case, the default port dropped, dot segments removed, and every byte a
URL may not carry (spaces, angle brackets, non-ASCII) percent-encoded.

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc: The reference resolved against the base and normalized; null when neither is absolute.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: An absolute URL normalized; anything else returned as given.

methods.name: split
shapes: @return array{scheme: ?string, authority: ?string, path: string, query: ?string, fragment: ?string}

methods.name: encode
methods.doc: Percent-encodes every byte outside the unreserved and sub-delimiter sets and the extra characters a component allows.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Locator
classes.doc:
Feed autodiscovery: the feeds an HTML page names in its
<link rel="alternate"> elements with a feed type, in page order, each
resolved against the page (or its <base href>).

methods.name: looksLikeFeed
methods.doc: Whether a response looks like a feed document rather than a page or text.

methods.name: alternates
methods.doc: The feed URLs a page names, resolved, in page order, each once.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Parts
classes.doc:
The repeating parts of a feed element read out of the tree as raw
values: links by relation, categories, and enclosures (Media RSS
contents, Atom enclosure links, RSS enclosures). The feed object
sanitizes and wraps them; each raw value travels with the node it came
from, so a relative URL resolves against that node's base.

methods.name: links
methods.doc:
Links by relation: Atom links (rel defaults to alternate, IANA names
answer to both spellings), then the RSS-style link elements and the
given extra alternates.
shapes: @param array<string, array<string, list<array<string, mixed>>>> $child the element's children
@param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $plain RSS-style link tags, by namespace and name
@param list<string> $more alternates already in their final form
@param Closure(string, array<string, mixed>): string $iri a URL as the feed hands it out, given its node

params.name: plain
params.doc: RSS-style link tags, by namespace and name

params.name: more
params.doc: alternates already in their final form

params.name: iri
params.doc: a URL as the feed hands it out, given its node

methods.name: categories
methods.doc:
Categories as raw text: Atom (term, scheme, label), RSS 2.0 (the text,
the domain as scheme), Dublin Core subjects.

methods.name: enclosures
methods.doc:
An item's enclosures as raw fields, Media RSS contents first (with the
item's thumbnails when a content has none of its own), then Atom
enclosure links, then RSS enclosures. "node" is where the URL came from.

methods.name: thumbnails
methods.doc: The media:thumbnail URLs directly under an element, each with its node.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Tree
classes.doc:
A feed document parsed into the nested arrays plugin code reads through
get_item_tags() and friends: each element is a node holding its own text
("data", whitespace between children included), its attributes grouped
by namespace, the xml:base and xml:lang in force, and its children by
namespace and local name. Two shapes differ from plain XML: an Atom text
construct of type "xhtml" keeps its markup as text, and an RSS title is
stored HTML-escaped. Named HTML references are read as characters unless
the document brings its own DOCTYPE.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The document's elements under a root holding only "child".

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: The document as the parser reads it: HTML references made numeric, the declaration on a line of its own.

methods.name: split
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} namespace and local name

classes.name: Minn\Front\AdminBar
classes.doc:
The Minn bar on the public site: the same server-rendered chrome the
app ships (assets/js/bar.js and assets/css/bar.css from the bundle),
built here for a signed-in reader who can edit. There is no other bar
and no other admin on the engine, so it is on for everyone who passes
the edit_posts gate; the app's per-person opt-in does not apply.

methods.doc: The bar for a signed-in editor, or null for anyone else.

methods.doc: The stylesheet link for the head.

methods.name: siteMenu
methods.doc: The site menu: the app's main views this user may open.

methods.doc: The status menu, only when the page carries a site status. @param array<string, mixed>|null $status

methods.doc: The create menu: a post, and a page for those who may edit them.

methods.doc: The notifications menu; bar.js fills the items.

methods.doc: The account menu: profile and sign out.

The status chip: the one thing the engine can say about site
visibility is whether search engines are asked to stay away.
shapes: @return array{tone: string, label: string, title: string, sub: string, fix: ?array}|null

classes.name: Minn\Front\Archives
classes.doc:

With plugins loaded, the reference's own submission and redirect
(contracts/runtime.md "The comment form"), so a spam plugin's checks,
the notifications and the commenter cookies are WordPress's: a refusal
with a status is the refusal page, one without is a blank page; else
set_comment_cookies, the comment's link (or redirect_to), the held

The site logo a theme prints, as get_custom_logo builds it (probe
plugin-helpers): the custom_logo theme mod's image at full size, never
lazy, its alt its own or else the site's name, linked home (marked the
current page on the front page). A theme that unlinks the home page logo
gets a plain span there, the image then decorative (an empty alt). The
image's attributes go through get_custom_logo_image_attributes and the
whole through get_custom_logo; no logo is an empty string, or in the
Customizer a hidden placeholder it can fill in.

The parts of a post's embed card the reference's embed template prints,
as markup: the featured image and its shape (the widest of the image's
sizes; wide enough and it sits above the title, else beside it, both by
filter), the site's name and icon, the comments and sharing buttons, and
the sharing dialog (its ids the post's and a random number, as on the
reference). The facade's template tags print them.

methods.doc:

embed_thumbnail_image_shape.

the query: a caller that does not say how long the thread is gets no
collapse at all under newest-first, because no page matches an unknown
last page.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Resolver
classes.doc:
Turns a public URL into a Resolution, following the reference's observed
rules:

- Unpaged content and archives without a trailing slash redirect to the
slashed form, as typed (case kept); paged views, search, and 404s do not.
- Query-var forms (?p=, ?page_id=, ?cat=, ?tag=, ?author=, ?m=, ?name=,
?pagename=) redirect to the pretty form when the target is public.
- Archive-shaped paths (category, tag, author, search, a four-digit year)
are strict: a mismatch is a 404 with no guessing.
- Plain-segment paths try the page hierarchy, then the post structure,
then redirect to the closest published page or post whose name starts
with the last segment, pages before posts, newest first.
- Empty term and date archives are 404; an author archive is 200 for any
name, even one that belongs to nobody.
- Non-public posts are 404 to anonymous readers and served to a reader
who can edit them.
