methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: An attribute value with its character references decoded.

methods.name: reference
methods.doc:
The character reference at $at in a context ("data" or "attribute"):
its text and how many bytes it spans, or null when none decodes there.

methods.name: char
methods.doc: The UTF-8 text for a code point, U+FFFD for one that cannot be a character, Windows-1252's for the C1 range.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Edits
classes.doc:
The edits pending on the current token: attribute sets and removals,
class additions and removals, and a text replacement, in call order.
They answer reads before they are written, and become the source
replacements the reader splices in when it moves on.

methods.name: validName
methods.doc: Whether an attribute name may be set at all, by the reference's rules.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.doc: Records a set; setting class outright forgets the class edits before it.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.doc: Records a removal of an attribute the source has.

methods.name: cancelAttribute
methods.doc: Forgets a pending set that never reached the source: cancelling an addition is not a removal.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The pending set or removal for a lowercase name, or null when there is none. @return array{name: string, value: string|true|null}|null

methods.name: addClass
methods.doc: Records a class to add; a later removal of the same class wins.

methods.name: removeClass
methods.doc: Records a class to remove; a later addition of the same class wins.

methods.name: hasClassEdits
methods.doc: Whether any class edit is pending.

methods.name: hasTagEdits
methods.doc: Whether any attribute or class edit is pending.

methods.name: classesAfter
methods.doc:
The class list after the pending edits: additions appended once,
removals gone.

methods.name: setTextFor
methods.doc:
Records a text replacement for a token of a kind that takes one: text
(escaped), an ordinary HTML comment, or a raw-text element's body
(script and style bodies get their closers escaped). False when the
kind takes none, or the text would end the element early.

params.name: tagName
params.doc: the lowercase tag name of an opening tag, null for anything else

methods.name: takeText
methods.doc: The pending text replacement, taken: it is cleared on read.

methods.name: takeReplacements
methods.doc:
The source replacements the attribute and class edits amount to, and
forgets them: a changed attribute is rewritten in place (its duplicates
removed), a removed one is cut, a new one is inserted after the tag name.
shapes: @param list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string}> $attributes the tag's own
@return list<array{int, int, string}> start, end, text

params.name: attributes
params.shape: list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string}>

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets everything pending.

methods.name: splice
methods.signature: splice(string $html, array $replacements, array $bookmarks, int $tokenStart, int $tokenEnd): array
methods.doc:
Splices replacements into the source, ascending, and moves the bookmarks
and the cursor by what the token at [$tokenStart, $tokenEnd] gained or lost.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: array<string, array{0: int, 1: int}>, 2: int} the source, the bookmarks, the cursor

methods.name: classValue
methods.doc: The class attribute's decoded value before class edits: a pending set, else the source's; null when there is none.

methods.name: classList
methods.doc: The class names before class edits.

methods.name: rebuiltClassValue
methods.doc: The class attribute after edits: source order and inner whitespace kept, removed classes gone with the space before them, additions appended.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Scanner
classes.doc:
Reads one token's shape out of raw HTML at an offset: a tag with its
name and attributes, a comment of one of the reference's kinds, a
doctype, or a processing instruction. Pure and stateless; null means the
input ends before the token does, which is where a streaming reader pauses.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc:
A tag starting at $at, its name from $nameStart (one byte in for an
opener, two for a closer): the name, where it ends, the end offset,
the attributes with their source offsets, and the self-closing flag.
shapes: @return array{name: string, nameEnd: int, end: int, attributes: list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string, quoted: bool}>, selfClosing: bool}|null

methods.name: rawText
methods.doc:
A raw-text element's body (script, style, textarea, ...): from $from to
its closing tag, or null when the closer never comes.
shapes: @return array{textStart: int, textLength: int, end: int}|null

methods.name: markupDeclaration
methods.doc:
What "<!" opens at $at: an HTML comment (abruptly closed or not), a
doctype, a CDATA lookalike, or a bogus comment.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, commentType?: string, fullStart?: int, fullLength?: int}|null

methods.name: question
methods.doc:
What "<?" opens at $at: a processing instruction when an ASCII
alphanumeric target (not "xml") is followed by space, "?" or ">"
(its text after the space, up to "?>" or ">"); a PI lookalike comment
for another XML name closed by "?>"; otherwise an invalid comment.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, target?: string, commentType?: string, fullStart?: int, fullLength?: int}|null

methods.name: attributeValue
methods.doc: A source attribute's decoded value (true when it has none), or null when the tag lacks it.

methods.name: opensMarkup
methods.doc: Whether the "<" at $at opens markup: a tag, a closer, "<!" or "<?".

methods.name: textEnd
methods.doc: Where text starting at $at ends: at the next "<" that opens markup, before a "<" ending the input, or at the end.

methods.name: cdata
methods.doc: A CDATA section in foreign content, "<![CDATA[" to "]]>"; null when it does not close.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int}|null

methods.name: doctype
methods.doc: A doctype's body split into its name and public and system identifiers.

methods.name: isSpace
methods.doc: Whether a byte is HTML whitespace.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc:
One attribute from $i: its name (a leading "=" is part of it), then an
optional quoted or bare value. Null when the input ends first.
shapes: @return array{int, string, int, int, ?string, bool}|null offset after, name, start, end, value, quoted

methods.name: comment
methods.signature: comment(int $start, int $end, int $textStart, int $textLength, string $type, int $fullStart, int $fullLength): array
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, commentType: string, fullStart: int, fullLength: int}

classes.name: Minn\Html\TagQuery
classes.doc:
A tag processor's next_tag() query: a tag name (any case), a class, the
nth match to stop at, and whether closers count.

methods.name: from
methods.doc: The query read from the array a caller passes.
shapes: @param array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string} $query

params.name: query
params.shape: array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string}

methods.name: matches
methods.doc: Whether a tag (by name, closer or not, and a class test) matches, before the offset is counted.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tags
classes.doc:
A streaming HTML tokenizer with in-place edits: tags, text, comments,
doctypes, and processing instructions in document order, attribute reads
with character references decoded, attribute and class edits applied to
the source without reserialising anything else, bookmarks to seek back to.
Behaviour pinned by the html-tag-processor probe fixture.

constants.name: RAW_TEXT
constants.doc: Elements whose body is raw text up to the closer.

properties.name: afterPre
properties.doc: Whether a text token here drops one leading line break (it follows a PRE or LISTING opener).

methods.name: nextToken
methods.doc: Advances to the next token; false at the end or at an incomplete one.

methods.name: nextTag
methods.doc: Advances to the next tag matching the query; false when none.
shapes: @param array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string} $query

params.name: query
params.shape: array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string}

methods.name: pausedAtIncompleteToken
methods.doc: Whether the scan stopped inside an unfinished token.

methods.name: tokenType
methods.doc: The current token's kind.

methods.name: tokenName
methods.doc: The current token's name.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: The current tag name, upper-cased; a processing instruction's target, or a PI lookalike's, as written.

methods.name: isCloser
methods.doc: Whether the current tag is a closer.

methods.name: selfClosing
methods.doc: Whether the current tag has the self-closing flag.

methods.name: commentType
methods.doc: The current comment's kind.

methods.name: fullCommentText
methods.doc: The current comment's whole text (a funky comment's is its text).

methods.name: modifiableText
methods.doc: The current token's text as a reader sees it.

methods.name: doctype
methods.doc: Doctype pieces, or null when the token is not a doctype. @return array{name: ?string, public: ?string, system: ?string}|null

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The decoded value, true for a bare attribute, null when absent; a pending edit answers first.

methods.name: attributeNames
methods.doc: The current tag's attribute names with a prefix, lower-cased.
shapes: @return list<string>|null lowercase names, in source order, null off a tag

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The current tag's classes.
shapes: @return list<string> distinct class names after pending edits

methods.name: hasClass
methods.doc: Whether the current tag has a class.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.doc: Sets an attribute on the current tag.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.doc: Removes an attribute from the current tag.

methods.name: addClass
methods.doc: Adds a class to the current tag.

methods.name: removeClass
methods.doc: Removes a class from the current tag.

methods.name: setModifiableText
methods.doc: Replaces the current token's text, when its kind allows it.

methods.name: setBookmark
methods.doc: Names the current token's position.

methods.name: releaseBookmark
methods.doc: Forgets a bookmark.

methods.name: hasBookmark
methods.doc: Whether a bookmark exists.

methods.name: seek
methods.doc: Moves to a bookmark.

methods.name: parseAs
methods.doc:
Reads what follows as content of a namespace: outside HTML "<![CDATA["
opens a CDATA section. Tag bodies are read as HTML ("html": SCRIPT,
STYLE and the other raw text elements take their text whole) unless
the start tags here are foreign content ("foreign").

methods.name: allowBookmarks
methods.doc: Raises how many bookmarks may be held at once.

methods.name: rewind
methods.doc: Back to the start of the document, with every update written in and the bookmarks kept.

methods.name: tokenSpan
methods.doc: Where the current token sits in the document: [start, end].

methods.name: textSpan
methods.doc: Where the current text token's text sits: [start, length].

methods.name: source
methods.doc: The source between two offsets, updates written in.

methods.name: bookmarkStart
methods.doc: Where a bookmark starts, or null when there is none of that name.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: The document with every update written in.

methods.name: setToken
methods.signature: setToken(string $type, string $name, int $start, int $end, int $textStart, int $textLength): void

methods.name: takeTag
methods.doc: A tag the scanner read at $at becomes the current token; a raw-text element carries its body to its closer.

methods.name: take
methods.doc: A comment, doctype, or processing instruction the scanner read becomes the current token; null pauses.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc: Writes every pending update into the source, keeping bookmarks and the current token aligned.

methods.name: rescanCurrent
methods.doc: Re-reads the current token so attribute offsets match the new source.

classes.name: Minn\Html\TokenMap
classes.doc:
A map from words to replacements that reads the longest word at a place
in a text (as character reference names are read): words shorter than
the key length stand alone, the others are grouped by their first bytes,
longest first.

methods.name: keyLength
methods.doc: How many leading bytes group the words.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Whether the word is in the map ("case-sensitive" or "ascii-case-insensitive").

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The replacement for the longest word at $offset, and the word's length; null when none starts there.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: Every word and its replacement: the short words first, then each group longest first.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\BodyRules
classes.doc:
The "in body" insertion mode, with select handled in body as the current
spec does (no "in select" mode). The adoption agency runs its simple
cases (the formatting element is closed with nothing special inside it);
the reference stops on the others, and on an end tag for a formatting
element that is not active.

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes one token in the "in body" insertion mode.

methods.name: isSpecial
methods.doc: Whether the node is in the spec's "special" category.

methods.name: adoptionAgency
methods.doc: The adoption agency algorithm in the cases the reference runs: the formatting element closes with nothing special opened inside it.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Builder
classes.doc:
The HTML tree construction algorithm over the engine's tokenizer, as the
reference's HTML processor runs it: tokens go through the insertion
modes (HeadRules, BodyRules, TableRules) or the foreign content rules,
and every node opened or closed becomes an Event with its breadcrumbs.
Text is read one kind at a time (NUL bytes, white space, the rest). At
the end of the input every open element closes; nothing implied is
added. Where the reference does not build a tree (Unsupported), the walk
stops with that error.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Back to the state before the first token.

methods.name: next
methods.doc: The next opened or closed node, or null at the end, at an incomplete token, or once unsupported markup stopped the walk.

methods.name: halt
methods.doc: Stops the walk for good (a failed seek leaves the processor like this).

methods.name: error
methods.doc: Why the walk stopped early, if it did.

methods.name: breadcrumbs
methods.doc: The breadcrumbs of the open elements now.

methods.name: token
methods.doc: The token being processed.

methods.name: stack
methods.doc: The stack of open elements.

methods.name: formatting
methods.doc: The list of active formatting elements.

methods.name: isFragment
methods.doc: Whether this builder parses a fragment (in a BODY context) rather than a document.

methods.name: mode
methods.doc: The insertion mode.

methods.name: switchTo
methods.doc: Switches the insertion mode.

methods.name: reprocessIn
methods.doc: Switches the insertion mode and processes the current token again under it.

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes a token under the current insertion mode, or the foreign content rules when they apply.

methods.name: processIn
methods.doc: Processes a token using the rules of an insertion mode other than the current one.

methods.name: framesetOk
methods.doc: Whether the frameset-ok flag is still set.

methods.name: framesetNotOk
methods.doc: Clears the frameset-ok flag.

methods.name: compat
methods.doc: The document's compatibility mode ("no-quirks", "limited-quirks", "quirks").

methods.name: setCompat
methods.doc: Sets the compatibility mode the doctype indicated.

methods.name: headPointer
methods.doc: The head element pointer.

methods.name: formPointer
methods.doc: The form element pointer.

methods.name: setFormPointer
methods.doc: Sets (or clears) the form element pointer.

methods.name: templateModes
methods.doc: The stack of template insertion modes.

methods.name: pushTemplateMode
methods.doc: Pushes a template insertion mode.

methods.name: popTemplateMode
methods.doc: Pops the current template insertion mode.

methods.name: adjustedCurrent
methods.doc: The adjusted current node: the context element when only the fragment's root is open.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: Inserts an element for the current start tag, real, in the namespace.

methods.name: insertImplied
methods.doc: Inserts an element the markup implied.

methods.name: insertLeafElement
methods.doc: Inserts and at once closes an element for the current start tag: a void element, one read whole, or self-closed foreign content.

methods.name: insertLeaf
methods.doc: Inserts a leaf (text, comment, CDATA, processing instruction) for the current token, in the namespace.

methods.name: insertDocumentLeaf
methods.doc: Inserts a leaf at the top of the document (a doctype or a comment before or around the html element).

methods.name: pop
methods.doc: Closes the current node as implied.

methods.name: popUntil
methods.doc: Pops until an HTML element of one of the names closes; when the current end tag names it, that last close is real.

methods.name: popUntilNode
methods.doc: Pops until this very node closes.

methods.name: generateImpliedEndTags
methods.doc: Generates implied end tags, leaving an element of the name open.

methods.name: generateAllImpliedEndTags
methods.doc: Generates all implied end tags thoroughly (table parts as well).

methods.name: closeP
methods.doc: Closes a P element: implied end tags but P's, then pops through the P.

methods.name: closePInButtonScope
methods.doc: Closes a P element when one is in button scope.

methods.name: reconstructFormatting
methods.doc: Reconstructs the active formatting elements; the reference stops when any would have to be reopened.

methods.name: skipNextNewline
methods.doc: Asks the parser to drop one leading line feed from the next token (after PRE, LISTING).

methods.name: resetInsertionMode
methods.doc: Resets the insertion mode from the stack of open elements.

methods.name: unsupported
methods.doc: Stops: the reference's processor does not build a tree for this markup.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The current tag's attribute, decoded; null when absent.

methods.name: doctype
methods.doc: The doctype's name and identifiers, for the compatibility mode. @return array{name: ?string, public: ?string, system: ?string}

methods.name: read
shapes: @return list<Token> the next token from the tokenizer (text in runs), an end-of-input token, or nothing when paused

methods.name: finish
methods.doc: Closes everything still open at the end of the input; nothing implied is added.

methods.name: keptAttributes
methods.doc: The attributes an element keeps for later comparison: all of a formatting element's (Noah's Ark), and encoding on MathML annotation-xml.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Compat

The compatibility mode a doctype indicates, by the identifier lists in
the HTML standard: quirks for legacy and missing doctypes, limited
quirks for the XHTML 1.0 transitional and frameset ones (and HTML 4.01's
with a system identifier), no quirks otherwise.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The mode ("no-quirks", "limited-quirks", "quirks") for a doctype's pieces.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
A whole doctype token read: its name (lower-cased), identifiers and
mode; a malformed one is quirks. Null when the text is not one doctype.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Event
classes.doc:
One step of the walk the HTML processor reports: a node opened (pushed)
or closed (popped), the breadcrumbs at that moment, and the offset of
the token behind it when the document wrote it (null when implied).

methods.name: isCloser
methods.doc: Whether this event closes its node.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\ForeignRules
classes.doc:
The rules for content in SVG and MathML: text and comments stay in the
foreign namespace, an HTML-only start tag (or a font with color, face or
size) breaks out back to HTML, other start tags open elements in the
current foreign namespace, and an end tag closes the nearest element of
its name or falls through to the HTML rules.

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes one token by the rules for foreign content.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Formatting
classes.doc:
The list of active formatting elements, with its markers (null): the
formatting elements opened since the last marker that may need
reopening, three of a kind at most (the "Noah's Ark" clause).

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Adds a formatting element, dropping the earliest of three identical ones since the last marker.

methods.name: insertMarker
methods.doc: Adds a marker (a cell, caption, template, applet, marquee or object opened).

methods.name: clearToLastMarker
methods.doc: Drops entries back to and including the last marker.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Drops one element from the list.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Whether this very element is in the list.

methods.name: lastNamed
methods.doc: The last HTML element of the name since the last marker.

methods.name: needsReconstruction
methods.doc: Whether reopening would be needed: the last entry is an element no longer open.

methods.name: names
methods.doc: The entries' names, markers left out.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\HeadRules
classes.doc:
The insertion modes around the body: initial (doctype and the
compatibility mode it indicates), before html, before head, in head, in
head noscript, after head, in template, after body, the frameset modes,
and after after body (where a comment would land outside the html
element, which the reference does not support).

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes one token in one of these insertion modes.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Node
classes.doc:
A node the tree builder places: an element (named as the HTML API
reports it, upper-cased, with its namespace) or a text, comment, doctype
or other leaf. Real when a token in the document made it (its offset is
where that token starts), virtual when the parser implied it.

constants.name: ATOMIC
constants.doc: Elements whose body the tokenizer reads whole, so they never take a closer.

methods.name: element
methods.doc: An element; the attributes kept are the ones the builder compares.

methods.name: leaf
methods.doc: A leaf: text, a comment, a doctype, a CDATA section, a processing instruction.

methods.name: selfClosed
methods.doc: The same element, marked as written with "/>".

methods.name: isSelfClosing
methods.doc: Whether the element was written with "/>".

methods.name: text
methods.doc: A leaf's text.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: The attributes kept for comparison.

methods.name: isHtml
methods.doc: Whether this is an HTML element with one of the names.

methods.name: isIn
methods.doc: Whether this is an element of the namespace with one of the names.

methods.name: expectsCloser
methods.doc: Whether the element is closed by a closer of its own: not a leaf, not void, not read whole, not self-closed foreign content.

methods.name: isHtmlIntegrationPoint
methods.doc: Whether this element is an HTML integration point (SVG foreignObject, desc, title; MathML annotation-xml for HTML).

methods.name: isMathTextIntegrationPoint
methods.doc: Whether this element is a MathML text integration point.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\OpenElements
classes.doc:
The stack of open elements and the spec's scope tests over it: an
element is in scope when it is reached walking down from the current
node before any of the scope's boundary elements.

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Puts a node on top.

methods.name: pop
methods.doc: Takes the current node off, or null when the stack is empty.

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The current (bottom-most open) node.

methods.name: at
methods.doc: The node at a position, 0 being the root.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: How many nodes are open.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every open node, root first.

methods.name: containsNode
methods.doc: Whether this very node is open.

methods.name: hasHtml
methods.doc: Whether an HTML element of the name is open anywhere.

methods.name: inScope
methods.doc: Whether one of the HTML elements is in the default scope.

methods.name: inListItemScope
methods.doc: Whether the HTML element is in list item scope (the default plus OL and UL).

methods.name: inButtonScope
methods.doc: Whether the HTML element is in button scope (the default plus BUTTON).

methods.name: inTableScope

classes.name: Minn\Http
classes.doc:
Outgoing HTTP, called straight from anywhere with no import:

$data = Minn\Http::get('https://api.example.com/status')->json();
Minn\Http::post($url, json: ['email' => $email], timeout: 10)->throw();

Every verb answers with an Exchange (->ok(), ->failed(), ->json(),
->header(), ->cookie(), ->throw(), ->code, ->body) and takes the same
named arguments, each optional:

- `query`: array added to the URL's query string
- `headers`: `name => value` (a list value repeats the header), or "Name: value" lines
- `json`, `form`, `body` (post, put, patch): an array sent as JSON, an array
form-encoded, or a string sent as it is; one of the three, and the first
two set the Content-Type
- `timeout`: seconds for the whole exchange, 5 by default
- `redirects`: how many to follow, 5 by default; 0 hands back the 3xx
- `hosts`: URL prefixes every hop must start with (`['https://api.wordpress.org/']`)
- `private`: hosts allowed to reach a private address. Loopback, LAN,
link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused otherwise, at every
hop and after DNS, so a URL someone typed is safe to fetch
- `maxBytes`: the largest body accepted; a longer one fails the exchange
- `userAgent`: Minn/{version} by default

A misspelt argument is an error at the line that has it. Credentials
(Authorization, Cookie) are dropped when a redirect leaves the origin.

methods.doc:
Sends exactly what the Outbound says, with none of the verbs' rules
about where a request may go: the door WordPress's own HTTP API comes
through after applying its rules, and the one a fake answers at.

methods.name: fake
methods.doc:
Answers requests from $answers instead of the network until
restore(), for tests. Keys are URL patterns (* matches anything; the
scheme and query may be left off); values are an array (sent as JSON),
a string (the body), a status code, an Exchange from reply(), or a
closure taking the Outbound and returning one of those. A request no
pattern matches fails as if nothing were listening. The fake answers
wp_remote_*() too, and refuses to start outside the command line.

methods.name: restore
methods.doc: Puts the network back after fake().

methods.doc: A response made by hand, for a fake to answer with. An array body is sent as JSON.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Access
classes.doc:
Who a route is for. The six answers every route gives, so the
authorization surface of the engine reads as a list of these.

cases.name: Public
cases.doc: Anyone, signed in or not; the caller is never resolved.

cases.name: SignedIn
cases.doc: A signed-in caller, whoever they are.

cases.name: Cap
cases.doc: A signed-in caller holding the named capability (and every extra one).

cases.name: Floor
cases.doc: The Minn Admin floor: signed in, may edit posts, and holds every extra capability named; refused as rest_forbidden.

cases.name: Own
cases.doc: A signed-in caller holding a capability on the object a pattern capture names.

cases.name: Type
cases.doc: Any caller, on a route whose {base} capture must name a declared post type; the route declines otherwise and the handler judges the rest.

cases.name: Taxonomy
cases.doc: Any caller, on a route whose {base} capture must name a taxonomy plugin code registered to show in REST; the route declines otherwise and the handler judges the rest.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Args
classes.doc:
The parameters a route accepts, as the reference describes them in the
REST index: name => {description, type, ...}. The descriptions, types,
enums and bounds were captured from the reference, so a client that
reads either index is told the same thing, and the router refuses a
value the way the reference refuses it, before it judges the caller.

A route declares only what it really reads. An argument published here
that the handler ignores would be worse than none at all, because a
client reading the index would build a request around it, so each set
below names the code that consumes it. The sets keep the reference's
order, because a refusal lists the invalid parameters in that order.
`_fields` and `_embed` are read everywhere and declared nowhere, as the
reference lists neither and validates neither.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Policy
classes.doc:
What a route requires of its caller, as data on the route: the router
enforces it before the handler runs, so a grep over the attributes is
the authorization surface. The two refusals are the reference's: a
caller who is not signed in gets the sign-in code (401), a signed-in
caller who lacks the capability gets the refusal code (403); how a bad
nonce is answered belongs to whoever judges the policy. A policy that
names a subject has the record looked up first, and answers the
record's 404 before either refusal, which is the reference's order.

argument allows: `policy: new Policy(Access::Cap, 'upload_files',
refuse: 'rest_cannot_create', message: '...')`.

params.doc: where the parameters come from when they depend on the path

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The row for one attribute on one handler method; the name defaults to the handler.

methods.name: argsFor
methods.doc:
The parameters as the index publishes them for one concrete route the
pattern takes (a {base} route's parameters are that base's).

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: The row as data, for the JSON catalogue. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: summary
methods.doc: The first sentence of a docblock, the way the API docs read it.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Router
classes.doc:
Matches a request to a #[Route] on one of the registered handler
objects, has the check refuse a bad argument, has the gate judge the
route's policy, and invokes the method with the request plus the named
pattern captures. That order is the reference's: an invalid parameter is
answered before the caller is looked at. The gate is the one
thing a router cannot be built without: a policy nobody judges is a
route nobody may call.

shapes: @param Closure(Policy $policy, Request $request, array<string, string> $captures): void $gate throws when the policy refuses the caller
@param Closure(Route $route, Request $request): void|null $check throws when a declared argument is missing or invalid; judged before the gate

params.name: envelope
params.doc: what runs around a matched route instead of the router throwing its refusals itself

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers every #[Route] method of the given handlers; returns the router for chaining.

methods.name: routes
methods.doc: The routes that list in an index: pattern => methods. @return array<string, list<string>>

methods.name: table
methods.doc:
Every registered route as a row: what it is, who it is for, what it
takes. The same rows Rest\Catalogue reads from the classes alone.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
The methods the caller may use on this path, for the Allow header:
every route matching the path (a route with no captures that names
the path exactly claims it alone), its policy judged for the caller
without dispatching. A route that states no policy counts for GET
only, until it states one. Empty when nothing matched or nothing
is allowed, and the header is then left out, as the reference does.

methods.name: matching
methods.doc:
The routes a request's method and path match, policies unjudged, in
the order dispatch tries them, with their captures: what a batch
reads to tell a route that does not take part from no route at all.

methods.name: dispatch
methods.doc: Null when nothing matched, so the caller can fall through.

methods.name: arguments
methods.doc:
The captures a handler takes, by parameter name; a capture spelled as
the reference spells it (user_id) binds to its camelCase parameter.

methods.name: enveloped
methodsOf
methods.doc:
The methods one handler answers on one pattern alongside the request's,
grouped as the reference registers them: reading alone, deleting
alone, and creating or editing together (POST, PUT, PATCH).

methods.name: literal
methods.doc: The one path a route spells, a capture it fixes ({base:media}) read as its word; null for a route with a real capture.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Subject
classes.doc:
The record a route capture names, so a policy can have it looked up
before the caller is judged: the reference answers "no such post" ahead
of "you may not", and the 404 it sends is the record's own. A kind that
reads its post type or taxonomy from the {base} capture says so.

cases.name: Post
cases.doc: A post of the type the {base} capture names (posts, pages, blocks, media, navigation, menu-items); a post when there is none.

cases.name: PostParent
cases.doc: The same lookup, refused as an invalid parent (revisions and autosaves).

cases.name: GlobalStylesParent
cases.doc: A global styles post, refused as an invalid parent (its revisions).

cases.name: Term
cases.doc: A term of the taxonomy the {base} capture names (categories, tags, wp_pattern_category).

cases.name: User
cases.doc: A user by id, or "me" for the caller, who must then be signed in.

methods.name: missingCode
methods.doc: The reference's error code for a record that does not exist.

methods.name: missingMessage
methods.doc: The reference's message for a record that does not exist.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Transport
classes.doc:
The engine's outgoing HTTP transport over curl: it sends exactly what an
Outbound says and nothing else decides. Redirects are followed by curl, so
the header lines of every hop arrive in order; only the last response's
block is kept, the way plugin code expects to read it. Code calling out
goes through Minn\Http, which owns the rules about where a request may go.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: Performs one outgoing request over curl and returns the exchange, a transport error included.

methods.name: options
methods.doc: The curl options every request carries, the header lines collected into $lines as they arrive.

methods.name: limit
methods.doc:
Stops a body that grows past $maxBytes: curl refuses up front when the
length is announced, and the progress callback aborts when it is not.

methods.name: lastHead
methods.doc: The last response's status line and header lines, line endings removed.

classes.name: Minn\Http\TrustedProxies
classes.doc:
Which addresses in front of the engine may speak for the client.

By default none do: a forwarded header is a request header, and a request
header is the client's word. Behind a proxy or CDN that terminates TLS,
`REMOTE_ADDR` is then the proxy's, which makes every visitor look like one
address (the sign-in throttle would lock them all out together) and every
request look insecure (the auth cookie would lose its Secure flag).

A site says who to believe in `wp-config.php`:

define('MINN_TRUSTED_PROXIES', '10.0.0.0/8, 2400:cb00::/32');
define('MINN_TRUSTED_PROXIES', '*');   // any: only when nothing but the proxy can reach PHP

The client is then the right-most address in `X-Forwarded-For` that is not
itself trusted, which is what a proxy chain appends, so a client that sends
its own `X-Forwarded-For` cannot put an address the engine believes to the
right of the proxy's.

shapes: @param list<string> $ranges addresses or CIDR ranges, or ['*'] for any

params.name: ranges
params.doc: addresses or CIDR ranges, or ['*'] for any

methods.name: none
methods.doc: Nobody in front of the engine speaks for the client.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: What the site declared in wp-config.php, or nobody.

methods.name: trusts
methods.doc: Whether the engine believes what this address says about the client.

methods.name: clientAddress
methods.doc:
The client's address, given who connected and what was forwarded: the
right-most forwarded address that is not itself a trusted proxy.

methods.name: forwardedSecure
methods.doc: Whether a forwarded scheme may be believed, and says https.

methods.name: bare
methods.doc: An address with a port or brackets stripped, as a forwarded list may carry them.

methods.name: covers
methods.doc: Whether a CIDR range or a plain address covers the address given.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\Catalog
classes.doc:
One translation file's contents: its headers as written, its messages
keyed the gettext way (the context, a 0x04 byte, then the original; the
original alone without a context), each with its translated forms and,
where the file says, the original plural, and the file's plural rule.
An empty translation counts as none.

methods.name: from
methods.doc: A catalog from headers and entries, its plural rule taken from the headers.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: The lookup key for an original in a context; an empty or missing context is no context.

methods.name: headerValue
methods.doc: A header's value, its name matched without case.

methods.name: translate
methods.doc: The translation of a message, or null when the file has none.

methods.name: translatePlural
methods.doc: The form of a message a count takes under this file's rule, or null when the file has none.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether the file holds a translation for the message.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\LocaleStack
classes.doc:
The locales a request switched into, innermost last, each with the user
whose locale it is (false when a locale was named outright). Empty means
the request speaks its own locale.

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Enters a locale, a user's or one named outright.

methods.name: pop
methods.doc: Leaves the innermost locale; the one now in force, or null when none is switched.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Leaves every switched locale.

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The innermost switched locale, or null.

methods.name: currentUser
methods.doc: The user whose locale is innermost, or false (none switched, or a locale named outright).

methods.name: switched
methods.doc: Whether any locale is switched in.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\MoFile
classes.doc:
The GNU gettext binary catalog (.mo), read and written. The file opens
with a magic number that also says its byte order, then a revision, the
message count, and the offsets of two tables of (length, offset) pairs:
the originals, then the translations. The entry with an empty original
carries the headers; a plural original is "singular NUL plural" and its
translations are NUL-separated; a context precedes the original with a
0x04 byte.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The catalog in a .mo file's bytes, or null when they are not one.

methods.name: write
methods.doc:
A .mo file's bytes for headers and entries, little-endian, entries in
the sorted order gettext expects.

methods.name: byteOrder
methods.doc: "V" for a little-endian file, "N" for a big-endian one, null for anything else.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PhpFile
classes.doc:
The PHP translation file (.l10n.php): a file that returns an array of its
lower-cased headers and a "messages" map from the gettext key to the
translation, plural forms joined by NUL bytes. It is the site's own data,
read the way the reference reads it, by including it.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The catalog a .l10n.php file returns, or null when it returns no messages.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PluralExpression
classes.doc:
The C subset a Plural-Forms header writes its rule in: the number n,
integer literals, parentheses, ! and unary minus, * / %, + -, the four
comparisons, == and !=, && and ||, and the ternary, with C's precedence
and the ternary binding to the right. Parsed into a small tree once and
evaluated per number; nothing is ever handed to PHP to run.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The expression as a tree, or null when it is not a whole expression.

methods.name: evaluate
methods.doc: The value of a parsed expression for one number; true is 1 and false 0.

methods.name: binaryLevel
methods.doc: One level of left-associative binary operators, and every tighter level under it.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PluralRule
classes.doc:
A language's plural rule from its Plural-Forms header: how many forms it
has and which form a number takes. A file without the header follows
English (two forms, n != 1); an expression that does not parse sends
every number to the first form, as the reference does.

methods.name: english
methods.doc: English: one form for 1, the other for everything else.

methods.name: fromHeader
methods.doc: The rule a Plural-Forms header states.

methods.name: fromExpression
methods.doc: A rule from a form count and an expression in n.

methods.name: index
methods.doc: The form a number takes.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\ScriptTranslations
classes.doc:
Where a script's JSON translations are found, and how they reach the
page. A script is placed by its URL: inside a plugin or a theme, its path
there; elsewhere on the site, its path from the site root; off the site,
nowhere. The JSON files are named by the md5 of that path (with ".min.js"
read as ".js"), or by the script's handle in a folder a plugin names.

methods.name: place
methods.doc:
A script's path inside its plugin, theme or site, and the languages
subfolder for it ("plugins", "themes", or "" for the site); the path
is false for a script off the site.

methods.name: absolute
methods.doc: The script made absolute the way place() reads it, for the filter that may move it.

methods.name: fileHash
methods.doc: The md5 a translation file is named by: a minified script shares its source's file.

methods.name: prefix
methods.doc: The start of a translation file's name: the core domain goes by locale alone.

methods.name: block
methods.doc: The inline script that hands a script's translations to wp.i18n before the script runs.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\TextDomains
classes.doc:
The text domains this request knows: each domain's files in the order they
were loaded, and the domains looked for and not found (known, with no
files), all in the order they first appeared, which is the order a locale
switch reloads them in. A lookup asks a domain's files in load order and
the first one with a translation answers, each under its own plural rule.
The registry also remembers the folder a plugin or theme named for its
domain (and how files there are named), and the domains unloaded for good.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: Adds a loaded file to a domain; a file already loaded there is not added twice.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether any file is loaded for the domain.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc: Forgets a domain and its files; true when it had any.

methods.name: markKnown
methods.doc: Records that a domain was asked for, so it is looked for once and reloaded on a switch.

methods.name: known
methods.doc: Whether the domain was loaded or looked for.

methods.name: knownDomains
methods.doc: Every known domain, in the order it first appeared.

methods.name: unloadFile
methods.doc: Drops one file from a domain; true when it was loaded.

methods.name: catalogs
methods.doc: The domain's files and catalogs, first loaded first.

methods.name: translate
methods.doc: The first loaded translation of a key in the domain, or null.

methods.name: translatePlural
methods.doc: The first loaded plural form of a key for a count, or null.

methods.name: rememberFolder
methods.doc: Records the folder a plugin or theme named for its domain; files there are "{domain}-{locale}".

methods.name: rememberThemeFolder
methods.doc: Records the active theme's own language folder; files there are named by locale alone.

methods.name: folderFile
methods.doc: The .mo path a domain's named folder would hold for a locale, if a folder was named.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: Keeps an unloaded domain from loading again on its own.

methods.name: closed
methods.doc: Whether the domain was unloaded for good.

methods.name: domains
methods.doc: The domains with files loaded.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\TranslationFiles
classes.doc:
Which file a request for a .mo path reads, and reading it. Asked for
"x.mo", the reference reads "x.l10n.php" when the format is php and that
file is there, and the .mo only otherwise; asked for the mo format, only
the .mo.

methods.name: candidates
methods.doc: The files to try for a requested .mo path, in order.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A translation file's catalog by its extension, or null when it cannot be read as one.

classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginController
classes.doc:
Signing in. The page people see is /minn-admin/login: the form, the
lost-password and reset flows, and logout all live there and link there.
/wp-login.php stays as the address tooling knows (one-time login links,
uptime probes, scripted sign-ins) and answers in place with the same
shapes; a bare GET of it sends a browser to the clean page. Sessions
and cookies validate on the engine AND on WordPress either way.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Auth\Authenticator $authenticator, Minn\Auth\SignIn $signIn, Minn\Content\Users $users, Minn\Auth\PasswordReset $reset, Minn\Mail\Mailer $mailer)

constants.name: SEGMENTS
constants.doc: Clean path segment => the action wp-login.php spells with ?action=.

methods.doc: The sign-in, lost-password, reset, and logout pages.

methods.name: signIn
methods.doc: Handles the posted form for each of those pages.

methods.doc: The check-your-email page's word, as the reference's: the confirmation link is on its way, or the registration is done.

methods.name: signInNotices
methods.doc: A sign-in page's notices after wp_login_errors, handed where a sign-in would land (the admin, unless the page names a landing).

methods.name: lostPassword
methods.doc: POST lostpassword mints a key and mails the link; POST resetpass saves the new password. Null for other actions.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc:
A reset asked for with plugins loaded, as the reference asks for it
(retrieve_password, its hooks and mail): the page again with the
refusal in its words, or on to "check your email". An unknown
account still counts against the address's attempts.

methods.name: openResetLink
methods.doc:
The link from the email: the key moves into a cookie scoped to
wp-login.php and the browser lands on the form without the key in
its address bar, as on the reference.

methods.name: resetSession
methods.doc: The user and key from the reset cookie, when the key is still good. @return array{0: ?array, 1: string}

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
Registration, when the site allows it (else off to the sign-in page
saying so): the form (its landing as registration_redirect says), or
a POST through register_new_user, landing where the form said (else
on the sign-in page, to check the email), or back on the form with
every refusal in its words.

methods.name: validateReset
methods.doc:
A new password judged as the reference judges it: the mismatch, then
whatever validate_password_reset adds.

methods.name: parts
methods.signature: parts(string $action, string $title, string $siteName, ?Minn\Content\UserRecord $user = NULL, ?Minn\Login\LoginNotices $notices = NULL): array
methods.doc:
What plugins put on one of the sign-in pages (LoginHooks::page()), for
a page titled $title, with its notices printed; without plugins, the
notices alone. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: tokenLogin
methods.doc:
The one-time login link `wp user login` prints (the captaincore
helper's contract): the token in user meta must match, be under
fifteen minutes old, and is spent on use. Any failure reads the same
so ids cannot be probed.

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc:
Only this site's own URLs are sign-in destinations: a path, or an
absolute URL on the home host. Anything else lands in the admin.

methods.name: logout
methods.doc:
Logging out ends the server-side session as well as the cookies, and
needs the session's own nonce so a stray link cannot do it; without
the nonce the reader is asked first.

methods.name: action
methods.doc:
The action asked for: a clean path segment (/minn-admin/login/reset)
or wp-login.php's ?action=. The reset flow's two halves share the
"reset" segment; a POST there saves the password.

methods.name: actionUrl
methods.doc: An action's address on the page this request came in on: a path under the clean page, a query on wp-login.php.

methods.name: base
methods.doc: The sign-in page this request arrived at: the clean page, or wp-login.php for the tooling that still names it.

methods.name: tooManyAttempts
methods.doc: A guessed-at address waits out the window; the page says so and the status lets tooling see it.

methods.doc: The sign-in page, its notices through wp_login_errors first.

classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginHooks
classes.doc:
The sign-in as plugins see it, when they are loaded. The credentials go
through the reference's authenticate chain, so a plugin may refuse a
sign-in (a breached password, a second factor, a locked account) or
accept one the password alone would not; wp_login_failed is the chain's
own report. wp_login follows a good sign-in and wp_logout a sign-out.
The refusal is shown as the page's notices (LoginNotices): the chain's
own as one vague sentence, a plugin's in its own words.

methods.name: available
methods.doc: Whether the chain can be asked: only with plugins loaded.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc:
The credentials through wp_authenticate and the authenticate filters,
as the reference's sign-in runs them: the user, or the refusal (a
WP_Error, or null when the chain gave none).

methods.name: signedIn
methods.doc:
After a good sign-in. The chain read the user through the runtime,
which cached their meta before the new session was written, so the
cache is let go first: a plugin reading session_tokens on wp_login
(CleanTalk keeps the first session's address) must see the new one.

methods.name: enter
methods.doc: A sign-in page request arriving, as wp-login.php announces it: login_init, then login_form_{action}.

methods.name: page
methods.signature: page(string $action, string $title, string $siteName, string $homeUrl, ?Minn\Content\UserRecord $user = NULL, ?Minn\Login\LoginNotices $notices = NULL): array
methods.doc:
What plugins put on the sign-in page, where the reference's page puts
it: the title (login_title), the head (login_enqueue_scripts, then
login_head, which prints the styles and scripts), the body classes
(login_body_class), the header's link and words (login_headerurl,
login_headertext), the message above the form (login_message), the
page's notices (login_errors, login_messages), the fields inside the
form (login_form, lostpassword_form or resetpass_form, as the page
is), and the footer (login_footer).
shapes: @return array{title: string, head: string, bodyClass: string, headerUrl: string, headerText: string, message: string, errors?: string, messages?: string, form: string, footer: string}|array{}

methods.name: landing
methods.doc: Where a good sign-in lands, as login_redirect says (the requested address and the user beside it).

methods.name: leaving
methods.doc: Where a sign-out lands, as logout_redirect says.

methods.name: signedOut
methods.doc: After a sign-out ended the session.

classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginNotices
classes.doc:
What a sign-in page tells the reader, held as the reference's pages hold
it: notices by code, each an error or (severity "message") a message,
their words as HTML. Printed, the errors are one paragraph, or a list
when there are several, and the messages a paragraph each; with plugins
loaded the sign-in page hands them through wp_login_errors first, and
every page prints them through login_errors and login_messages. The
authenticate chain's own refusals read as the engine's one sentence, so
a page never says which half of a sign-in was wrong.

shapes: @param list<array{0: string, 1: string, 2: string}> $notices code, HTML, severity ('' or 'message')

constants.name: REFUSALS
constants.doc: The chain's own refusals, which the page words as one.

constants.name: REFUSED
constants.value: 'Error: The username or password you entered is incorrect.'
constants.doc: The one sentence for any of them.

methods.name: none
methods.doc: No notices.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: The engine's own plain words as one notice; an "Error:" lead takes the reference's strong label.

methods.name: refused
methods.doc: A sign-in refused: the chain's refusal, or (none given, or not one) the engine's one sentence.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The notices a WP_Error holds (a plugin may have handed back something else: then none).

methods.name: with
methods.doc: These notices and one more.

methods.name: isEmpty
methods.doc: Whether there are none.

methods.name: wpError
methods.doc: As the WP_Error plugins are handed.

methods.name: forSignIn
methods.doc:
The sign-in page's notices after wp_login_errors, which is handed
where a sign-in would land; without plugins, as they are.

methods.name: areas
methods.doc:
The error and message areas' HTML ('' for an area with none),
through login_errors and login_messages with plugins loaded.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: Plain words as notice HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Login\ServeLogin
classes.doc:
Thrown by the wp-login.php shape file when plugin code require's it
mid-request (a hide-login plugin serving its own sign-in URL, the
perfmatters pattern). Engine::respond() catches it and answers the
current request with the sign-in surface.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\AddressRules
classes.doc:
Email addresses: the checks a mailer can apply (PHP's filter, the
RFC 5322 grammar with comments, quoted local parts and domain literals,
the HTML5 form rule), parsing an address list, and the domain of an
address in ASCII.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc: Whether the address passes the named check ("php", "pcre", "pcre8", "html5", "noregex").

methods.name: parseList
methods.doc:
The addresses in a comma-separated list, each with its display name
(encoded words decoded into $charset); entries that are not valid
addresses are left out.

methods.name: asciiDomain
methods.doc: The address with its domain in ASCII (IDNA), the domain read from $charset first; unchanged when it cannot be.

methods.name: quoted
methods.doc: The text as an RFC 822 quoted string when it holds a character that needs one.

methods.name: rfc5322
methods.doc: RFC 5322 addr-spec with comments and folding white space, a quoted local part or a domain literal; local part 64, label 63 characters.

methods.name: splitList
shapes: @return list<string> the list split at commas outside quotes and angle brackets

classes.name: Minn\Mail\ChangeNotices
classes.doc:
The notices the reference mails a user when their password or email
address changes, as templates: plugins filter them (password_change_email,
email_change_email) with the placeholders still in them and the site name
still a %s in the subject, and fill() finishes them after.

methods.name: password
methods.doc: The password notice: subject and message, placeholders unfilled. @return array{subject: string, message: string}

methods.name: email
methods.doc: The email-address notice, sent to the address being left: subject and message, placeholders unfilled. @return array{subject: string, message: string}

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: A template's placeholders filled with their values. @param array<string, string> $values placeholder name (USERNAME, ...) => value

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Composer
classes.doc:
A message as the reference's mailer writes it: the header block (Date,
the address lines, Subject, Message-ID, X-Mailer, custom headers,
MIME-Version), the MIME header for its type, and the body, multipart
when it has an alternative, inline parts or attachments. Boundaries are
"b1=_{id}" to "b3=_{id}"; a 7-bit-clean body declared 8bit goes out as
7bit us-ascii, and a body with a line past 998 characters as
quoted-printable.

methods.name: body
methods.doc: The body and the encoding a single-part message declares.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: The header block, MIME-Version and the MIME header included.

methods.name: mimeHeaders
methods.doc: The MIME header for the message's type: the content type (with its boundary) and the transfer encoding.

methods.name: mailOnlyHeaders
methods.doc: The To and Subject lines PHP's mail() takes as arguments, written after the headers in the sent copy.

methods.name: addressLine
methods.doc: "Name: a, b" for a list of [address, name] pairs.

methods.name: address
methods.doc: One address as a header writes it: the address alone, or the name (as a phrase) and the address in angle brackets.

methods.name: secure
methods.doc: Header text with any line break taken out.

methods.name: messageId
methods.doc: The message id given when it is well formed, else one made from the id and the host name.

methods.name: encodingFor
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} the encoding and charset a body part declares

methods.name: partHead
methods.signature: partHead(Minn\Mail\Draft $d, string $boundary, string $charset, string $contentType, string $encoding): string

methods.name: calendar
methods.doc:
A text/calendar part when the message carries one, followed by $after;
its method is the calendar's own (upper-cased) when it is a known one.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: The date given when it reads as a moment already past, else now; either way as RFC 5322 writes it.

methods.name: attachAll
methods.doc: Every attachment of one disposition as parts of the boundary, then the boundary's end; an identical one, or a repeated inline id, goes once.

methods.name: extraLines
shapes: @return list<string> X-Priority, X-Mailer, Disposition-Notification-To and the custom headers

classes.name: Minn\Mail\DataLines
classes.doc:
A message cut into the lines SMTP DATA sends. Any line break (CRLF, CR
or LF) ends a line. A line longer than 998 characters is cut at its last
space within the first 998 (the space dropped), or at 997 when there is
none; in the header block (when the first line reads "Name: ..." with no
space in the name, up to the first empty line) each continuation starts
with a tab. Dot stuffing is the sender's job, after the cut.

methods.name: split
methods.doc: The lines to send, without their line endings.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\DebugOutput
classes.doc:
Where a mailer's debug text goes, as its Debugoutput setting names it: "echo" (a timestamp and a tab, continuation lines indented under the text), "html" (entity-escaped, line breaks dropped, ending in
), "error_log", a PSR-3 logger's debug(), or any other callable, which gets the text and its level. The two printed forms come back as text for the caller to print; the others are delivered here and return null.

methods.name: smtp
methods.doc: Debug text from the SMTP client: the text to print, or null once delivered; its html form carries a timestamp.

methods.name: mailer
methods.doc: Debug text from the mailer itself: the text to print, or null once delivered; its html form has no timestamp.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Dkim
classes.doc:
DKIM signatures (RFC 6376) as the reference's mailer writes them:
rsa-sha256, relaxed header and simple body canonicalization, the
standard headers signed in the order they appear (plus any extra ones
the caller names), an optional identity, the signed headers copied into
z= when asked, and the signature folded in 73-character pieces.

methods.name: copyingHeaders
methods.doc: The same signer, copying the signed headers into z= as well.

methods.name: quotedPrintable
methods.doc: Text with everything outside the DKIM-safe printable set written as =XX.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: Relaxed header canonicalization: unfolded, names lower-cased, runs of space collapsed, values trimmed.

methods.name: body
methods.doc: Simple body canonicalization: CRLF line endings and exactly one at the end.

methods.name: sign
methods.doc: The base64 RSA-SHA256 signature of the text, or null when the key cannot be read.

methods.name: signatureHeader
methods.signature: signatureHeader(string $headerBlock, string $subject, string $body, int $time, array $extra, string $eol): ?string
methods.doc: The DKIM-Signature header for a message, signed at $time.
shapes: @param list<string> $extra lower-case names of further headers to sign

params.name: extra
params.doc: lower-case names of further headers to sign

methods.name: signedHeaders
shapes: @return array{0: list<string>, 1: list<string>, 2: list<string>} names, header lines and z= copies

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Draft
classes.doc:
Everything a message is composed from: the transport it goes out on
(which decides the line ending, the header line length, and where To,
Subject and Bcc are written), the envelope, the content, the headers,
and the attachments as [path or data, file name, name, encoding, type,
is data, disposition, content id]. $toHeader is "list" (To, or
undisclosed-recipients when there is neither To nor Cc) or "omit" (one
message per recipient, the address given to each send instead).

constructor.signature: __construct(string $mailer, string $eol, string $charset, string $contentType, string $encoding, string $subject, string $body, string $altBody, string $ical, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, array $cc, array $bcc, array $replyTo, string $messageId, string $messageDate, ?int $priority, string $xMailer, string $confirmReadingTo, array $customHeaders, array $attachments, string $toHeader = 'list')
shapes: @param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $to address and name pairs, as are $cc, $bcc and $replyTo
@param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $customHeaders name and value pairs

params.name: to
params.doc: address and name pairs, as are $cc, $bcc and $replyTo

methods.name: lineLength
methods.doc: The longest header line the transport takes before it must fold.

methods.name: encodeHeader
methods.doc: Header text encoded for this message's charset and transport.

methods.name: messageType
methods.doc: Which parts the message has: plain, or "alt", "inline", "attach" joined by "_".

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HeaderWords
classes.doc:
Header text as mail carries it (RFC 2047): left alone when it is plain
and short enough, quoted when a phrase needs it, otherwise encoded words
in Q (mostly ASCII) or B (mostly not), folded to the line length the
transport allows: 63 for PHP's mail(), 998 otherwise. Plain text only
becomes an encoded word to be folded when it is too long for one line.

methods.name: encode
methods.signature: encode(string $text, string $position, string $charset, int $lineLength, string $eol): string
methods.doc: The header text encoded for its position ("text", "phrase" or "comment").

methods.name: q
methods.doc: RFC 2047 "Q" encoding for a position: spaces as "_", and the characters the position cannot carry as =XX.

methods.name: base64Lines
methods.doc:
Base64 lines of at most 63 characters cut at whole characters, so a
multibyte character is never split across encoded words.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: Encoded words decoded (adjacent ones joined) and converted into $charset; other text passes through.

methods.name: specials
methods.doc: How many characters the position counts as needing encoding.

methods.name: qLines
methods.signature: qLines(string $text, string $position, string $charset, int $width, string $eol): array

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HostEntry
classes.doc:
One entry of a mailer's Host setting ("host", "host:port",
"ssl://host:465", "tls://host"; entries are separated by semicolons):
the security prefix, the host and the port. Only ssl:// and tls:// are
prefixes; anything else stays part of the host and fails the host check.

methods.name: parseAll
methods.doc: The entries of a Host setting, null where one cannot be read.
shapes: @return list<array{0: string, 1: self|null}> the trimmed entry text and its reading

methods.name: validHost
methods.doc: Whether a host name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address is well formed.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HtmlMessage
classes.doc:
What a mailer reads out of an HTML message: the images it can carry
inline (a src or background naming a file under the base directory, or
a data: URI of a raster image), the content id each one gets (the first
32 hex digits of a SHA-256 of the URL, or of a data URI's bytes, at
"phpmailer.0"), and the plain-text version (head, style and script
dropped, tags stripped, entities decoded into the charset).

constants.name: NO_TEXT
constants.value: 'This is an HTML-only message. To view it, activate HTML in your email application.'

methods.name: images
methods.doc: Every quoted src or background value, in document order.

methods.name: dataImage
methods.doc: A data: URI's bytes and type when it is a raster image, else null.

methods.name: localPath
methods.doc: A relative path with no scheme and no step up out of the base directory, or null.

methods.name: cid
methods.doc: The content id the mailer gives an image.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The plain-text version of an HTML message.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailHeaders
classes.doc:
The headers argument of wp_mail() read the way the reference reads it:
a string split into lines (CRLF or LF) or a list of lines; a line
without a colon is skipped. From gives an address and a name (quotes
dropped); Cc, Bcc and Reply-To add comma-separated entries (a comma
inside quotes still splits); Content-Type gives a type and either a
charset or a boundary (a boundary leaves the charset empty); every
other header is kept by name, the last of a name winning.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The headers argument, as a string of lines or a list of them.

methods.name: recipient
methods.doc: One recipient entry as [address, name]: "Name <address>" (the name as written) or a bare address.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailLog
classes.doc:
The engine's development transport: each message as one JSON line
(time, from, to, subject, body) appended to wp-content/minn-mail.log,
nothing sent.

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The site's log file.

methods.name: write
methods.signature: write(string $file, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, string $subject, string $body): bool
methods.doc: Appends one message; false when the file cannot be written.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailSettings
classes.doc:
How mail leaves the site, from the minn_mail option (JSON or a serialized
array): the PHP mail
function by default, SMTP when configured, or a log file for development.
The sender defaults to the site name at a no-reply address on the home host.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $transport = 'mail', string $host = '', int $port = 587, string $encryption = 'tls', string $username = '', string $password = '', string $fromEmail = '', string $fromName = '')

methods.name: stored
methods.doc:
What the minn_mail option holds, without defaults: empty when the site
has not configured mail.

methods.name: fromSite
methods.doc: The site's mail settings from its minn_mail option, or the defaults.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: The option's JSON, secrets included, for the settings surface.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Mailer
classes.doc:
Sends a Message through the configured transport. Failures are logged
and reported as false; nothing here throws into a request.

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: A mailer using the site's own settings.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
The one-line send: a recipient, a subject, a body, through the site's
transport and sender, with nothing to construct at the call site.

methods.name: noticesFor
methods.doc: The engine's own notices, worded once, from this site's name and address.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
Sends one message; false on failure. With WordPress's mail function
loaded the message goes through wp_mail(), so its filters and the
phpmailer_init hook (an SMTP plugin's way in) apply as they do on the
reference; otherwise through the configured transport directly.

methods.name: draft
methods.signature: draft(string $mailer, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, Minn\Mail\Message $message): Minn\Mail\Draft

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailerStrings
classes.doc:
The mailer's English messages, keyed as plugins look them up
("authenticate", "provide_address", ...): the base set, and the set
WordPress's own mailer subclass loads, which words four of them
differently. Captured from the reference into data/mailer-strings.json.

methods.name: base
methods.doc: The base mailer's messages.

methods.name: wordpress
methods.doc: The messages WordPress's mailer subclass loads.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Message
classes.doc: One outgoing plain-text email.

methods.name: to
methods.doc: One recipient or several, and the two things every mail has.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MimeTypes
classes.doc:
The MIME type a mailer gives an attachment by its file extension (the
table the reference's mailer answers with); anything else is
application/octet-stream.

methods.name: forExtension
methods.doc: The type for an extension, in any case.

methods.name: forFilename
methods.doc: The type for a file name or path: its last extension (a query string ignored).

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Notices
classes.doc:
The messages the engine itself sends, worded as the reference words them
and built in one place, so a controller and a CLI verb that announce the
same thing say the same thing.

methods.name: loginDetails
methods.doc: A new account's login details, with a link to choose a password.

methods.name: passwordReset
methods.doc: The password reset link, with the requester's address as the reference prints it.

methods.name: moderation
methods.doc: A comment waiting in the queue, announced to the site's address.

methods.name: newComment
methods.signature: newComment(string $authorEmail, string $postTitle, string $author, string $comment, string $link): Minn\Mail\Message
methods.doc: An approved comment on a post, announced to the post's author.

methods.name: subject
methods.doc: Every notice the reference sends carries the site's name in brackets.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\PathParts
classes.doc:
A path's parts the way a mailer names attachments, safe for multibyte
names: the directory ('' when there is none), the last segment, its
extension (after the last dot, so ".hidden" is all extension) and the
name before it. Either slash separates; trailing ones are ignored.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The path's four parts.
shapes: @return array{dirname: string, basename: string, extension: string, filename: string}

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Smime
classes.doc:
S/MIME signing of a composed MIME entity with a certificate and key on
disk: the entity goes through OpenSSL as a detached signature and comes
back as new MIME headers (multipart/signed) and the signed body.

methods.name: sign
methods.doc: The signed entity's MIME headers and body, or null when signing fails.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Smtp
classes.doc:
Delivery over SMTP for the engine's own mail when WordPress's mail
function is not loaded: the site's server, SSL or STARTTLS, a sign-in
when a user name is set, one message per connection, through the same
SmtpSession the PHPMailer SMTP class speaks with.

methods.name: sendRaw
methods.doc:
Sends one composed message (headers, a blank line, the body) to the
envelope recipients; false on any refusal.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\SmtpSession
classes.doc:
One SMTP conversation as the reference's client holds it: the socket,
the last reply, the server's extensions from EHLO, and the last error as
{error, detail, smtp_code, smtp_code_ex}. Every command names itself in
its error ("RCPT TO command failed"); a command sent before connecting
fails as "Called X without being connected". Debug text goes to the
given closure with its level: 1 client lines, 2 server replies, 3
connection events, 4 raw inbound lines. Credentials never reach it.

methods.name: limits
methods.doc: How long one read may wait and how long a whole reply may take, in seconds.

methods.name: connect
methods.doc: Opens the connection and reads the greeting.

methods.name: startTls
methods.doc: Asks for TLS and turns it on.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc:
Signs in with the named mechanism, or the strongest the server offers
when it is empty or not offered.

params.name: oauth
params.doc: a ready XOAUTH2 token, base64, when there is one

methods.name: connected
methods.doc: Whether the connection is open; a socket closed at the far end is closed here too.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: Closes the socket and forgets the server's greeting and extensions; the last error stays.

methods.name: data
hello
methods.doc: EHLO, falling back to HELO; the extensions come from the EHLO reply.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc: MAIL FROM, with the given parameters (" XVERP", " SMTPUTF8") after the address.

methods.name: quit
methods.doc: QUIT; the connection closes when it succeeds, or anyway unless told to keep it.

methods.name: recipient
methods.doc: RCPT TO, with the delivery notifications asked for (NEVER, SUCCESS, FAILURE, DELAY).

methods.name: xclient
methods.doc: XCLIENT with the named attributes that are in $allowed; others are dropped.

methods.name: turn
methods.doc: TURN is refused here, as the reference refuses it.

methods.name: command
methods.doc:
Sends one command and reads the reply; a reply outside $expect fails
with "{name} command failed" and the reply's detail and codes.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: Writes raw text to the server; credential commands show as hidden in the debug text.

methods.name: error
methods.doc: The last error; every field is empty after a command that succeeded.
shapes: @return array{error: string, detail: string, smtp_code: int|string, smtp_code_ex: string}

methods.name: extensions
methods.doc: The extensions from the last EHLO (or the HELO greeting), null before one.

methods.name: extension
methods.doc: One extension's value: true for a bare one, a string or list for one with arguments, false when absent, null before EHLO.

methods.name: lastReply
methods.doc: The server's last reply, every line.

methods.name: transactionId
methods.doc: The queue id the server gave the last message: null before one was sent, false when none was recognised.

methods.name: parseReply
methods.doc: The reply's code, enhanced code (when present) and the text after them.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\TextWrap
classes.doc:
Word wrapping for mail text. Lines break at spaces once they would pass
the length; existing line breaks stay; a word longer than the line stays
whole in plain text, and in quoted-printable text is cut into pieces
ending in a soft break ("="), never inside an =XX escape or (for UTF-8)
inside an encoded character. A line broken at a space keeps the space
and, in quoted-printable text, a soft break after it.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: Plain text wrapped to the length, every line ending in $eol.

methods.name: quotedPrintable
methods.doc: Quoted-printable text wrapped to the length with soft breaks, every line ending in $eol.

methods.name: utf8Boundary
methods.doc:
Where to cut quoted-printable UTF-8 text at or before $max without
splitting an encoded character.

methods.name: wrapWith
methods.signature: wrapWith(string $text, int $length, string $softBreak, string $charset, string $eol): string

methods.name: line
methods.signature: line(string $line, int $length, string $softBreak, string $charset, string $eol): string

methods.name: closeLine
methods.signature: closeLine(string $word, string $out, string $buffer, int $length, string $softBreak, string $charset, string $eol): array
methods.doc:
Ends the line before a long word: with as much of the word as fits
when more than twenty characters are left, else with a soft break.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} the output and what is left of the word

methods.name: pieces
methods.signature: pieces(string $word, string $out, int $length, string $charset, string $eol): array
methods.doc: A long word in line-length pieces, each but the last ending in a soft break.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} the output and the last piece, which starts the next line

methods.name: cut
methods.doc: How much of the word to take: at most $max, never inside an escape.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Transfer
classes.doc:
Body text in a content transfer encoding, and the line-ending helpers
mail composition leans on.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
The text in an encoding: 7bit, 8bit and binary keep the text (the first
two with normalized line breaks and a final one), base64 in 76-column
lines, quoted-printable by PHP's encoder.

methods.name: quotedPrintable
methods.doc: Quoted-printable text with the encoder's line breaks normalized.

methods.name: normalizeBreaks
methods.doc: Every CRLF, CR or LF as $eol.

methods.name: stripTrailingSpace
methods.doc: The text without trailing spaces, tabs and line breaks.

methods.name: stripTrailingBreaks
methods.doc: The text without trailing line breaks.

methods.name: has8bit
methods.doc: Whether any byte is outside 7-bit ASCII.

methods.name: hasLongLine
methods.doc: Whether any line runs past the 998 characters SMTP allows.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Canvas
classes.doc:
One GD bitmap and the operations the media layer needs on it. Every
operation returns a new canvas; alpha is preserved throughout, which is
what makes PNG and WebP sub-sizes match the reference's.

methods.name: open
methods.doc:
A canvas from an image file, or null when it cannot be decoded or
would not fit in memory. The header names the dimensions before a
pixel is decoded, so a small file that claims a huge canvas is
refused instead of taking the request down.

methods.name: resample
methods.doc: Resamples a source box onto a destination box.
shapes: @param array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int} $box dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h (the GD argument order)

params.name: box
params.shape: array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int}
params.doc: dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h (the GD argument order)

methods.name: crop
methods.signature: crop(int $x, int $y, int $width, int $height, ?int $targetWidth = NULL, ?int $targetHeight = NULL): self
methods.doc: A canvas cut to a rectangle, resized to a target when given.

methods.name: rotate
methods.doc: A canvas turned by an angle, or null when GD refuses.

methods.name: flipVertical
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored on either axis.

methods.name: flipHorizontal
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored left to right.

methods.name: copy
methods.doc: An untouched copy of the canvas.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Writes the bitmap in the given format; the directory is created when missing.

methods.name: progressive
methods.doc: The bitmap written progressively from now on (an interlaced JPEG).

methods.name: baseline
methods.doc: The bitmap written line by line from now on, as it is by default.

methods.name: stream
methods.doc: Writes the image to the output in a format, at a quality.

methods.name: affordable
methods.doc:
Whether a bitmap of these dimensions fits the memory left to this
request: five bytes a pixel for the decoded image (GD keeps four and

it was made), then EXIF for what IPTC left empty (a short description as
