classes.name: Minn\Ops\Packages
classes.doc:
Putting themes and extensions on disk. Themes come from wordpress.org
(block themes render on the engine) or an uploaded zip; extensions come
from an uploaded zip or a URL, and must carry a minn.json: a WordPress
plugin would install but never run, so it is refused with the reason.
Every archive is unpacked through one guarded routine: exactly one
top-level folder that is a plain name (never "." or ".."), no absolute
or dotted paths, no symbolic links, bounded entry count and size, the
folder's identity checked and its destination proven to be a direct
child of the kind's directory before it is moved into place. Removal
proves the same containment before anything is deleted.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Updates
classes.doc:
Update offers from wordpress.org for the site's plugins and themes: the
directory's update-check endpoints asked with the installed headers, the
answer kept in the minn_updates option (JSON) for twelve hours, and the
offers applied by downloading the release archive through the one
package unpacker. A plugin or theme the directory does not know keeps
its folder untouched and is never offered anything. The per-item
auto-update lists are the site's own auto_update_plugins and
auto_update_themes options, in the shape the app already reads.

The directory is not the only source. A plugin that hosts itself answers
for its own version through the update transient's filter, which is where
WordPress reads it too, so Runtime\PluginUpdates asks the runtime the same
question and its answer is merged in. Applying such an offer goes through
the publisher: a package outside the directory is unpacked only when
`upgrader_pre_download` hands back a copy it verified.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: The stored answer, refreshed when older than the TTL or absent.

methods.doc: Asks wordpress.org now, whatever the cache says, and keeps the answer.

methods.doc: Asks the directory now and stores the answer.

Fetches and unpacks an offer's package. A directory package is
downloaded here, every redirect hop staying on the wordpress.org
download host; anything else has to come from its publisher, verified.
The archive's SHA-256 is kept under "archives" in the state either

word: the reference asks `upgrader_pre_download` before every
download, and a plugin that hosts itself answers there with the copy
it fetched and checked against the hash it publishes. No answer means
nobody vouched for the archive, and the engine will not unpack code
over a folder on nobody's word.

search string split into terms (quoted phrases kept whole, single letters
and stopwords dropped, ten or more terms or none left searched as one

classes.name: Minn\Rest\AbilitiesController
classes.doc:
wp-abilities/v1: what this site can be asked to do, and the doing of it.

An ability is a named unit of work with an input schema, an output
schema, and a permission callback, registered by core or by a plugin.
The catalogue is what an agent reads first, so the shapes here are the
reference's, captured; the engine's own registry answers them.

Reading the catalogue needs only a session. Running one is the ability's
own decision, through its permission callback, and a read-only ability
runs on GET, since running it changes nothing.

ability's own permission callback decides who may.

takes it; the runtime's table is never consulted. This is what the

declines cannot bounce between the two. $as is the caller's own

what answers OPTIONS on the reference).

order, or a namespace's share, for anyone who can edit a type shown in
REST. Each carries its registration (attributes, supports, selectors,
contexts, asset handles and the first of each as the old single field)
with its styles (its own, then those registered for it) and its
variations as built when asked; a dynamic block links to its renderer.
Served with plugins loaded, since a plugin's blocks come from its code.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: Every block type, or those of one namespace (?namespace=).

methods.name: inNamespace
methods.doc: One namespace's block types.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One block type.

methods.name: requireViewer
methods.doc: Only someone who edits a type shown in REST may read block types; the runtime holds them.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\BlocksController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/blocks: synced patterns and reusable blocks, stored as wp_block
posts. The reading and writing is the posts machinery with the post
type's own capabilities; what is this type's alone is the reading gate:
without edit_posts the list is empty and a single block is refused,
published or not.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The blocks the caller may edit; an empty list for anyone else.

methods.name: single
methods.doc:
One block. Editing context is the posts machinery's own gate
(rest_forbidden_context); a view is refused to anyone who cannot edit
posts, and a trashed or unknown block is not found rather than refused.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a block: a pattern's create_posts is publish_posts.

routes: POST /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a block.

routes: DELETE /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap delete_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trashes or deletes a block.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Caller
classes.doc:
Who is making this REST call. Resolved once from the cookie and nonce;
an anonymous or failed caller has id 0 and every capability check fails.

methods.name: resolveAs
methods.doc:
Settles the caller as a session already proven elsewhere: an
in-process request a plugin makes through rest_do_request() carries
no nonce, so it runs as whoever the outer request resolved.

methods.name: resolveAnonymous
methods.doc: Settles the caller as nobody: plugin code (determine_current_user) signed the request out.

methods.name: cookieBound
methods.doc:
Whether a sign-in cookie vouches for this caller (or failed to, for
want of its nonce): a cookie's nonce vouches for its own user only.

methods.name: resolveInvalidNonce
methods.doc: Settles the caller as one whose cookie's nonce does not vouch for the user plugin code named.

methods.name: session
methods.doc: The session, or null for an anonymous or refused caller.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The caller's user id, 0 when anonymous.

methods.name: can
methods.doc:
Whether the caller holds a capability, on a post when given. With
plugins loaded the answer is WordPress's: the same mapping, then
map_meta_cap and user_has_cap, where role editors and lock plugins
have their say.

methods.name: editsAnyRestType
methods.doc:
Whether the caller can edit posts of some type shown in REST: what
the reference asks before showing statuses, block types and the
active theme. A plugin's types count once plugins are loaded.

methods.name: capabilities
methods.doc: The capability engine.

methods.name: require
methods.signature: require(string $code = 'rest_not_logged_in', string $message = 'You are not currently logged in.', int $status = 401): Minn\Auth\Authenticated
methods.doc:
The session, or the reference's refusal: a bad nonce is always 403
rest_cookie_invalid_nonce; no identity is the caller-supplied error.

methods.name: requireFloor
methods.doc:
The floor every Minn Admin route shares: a signed-in caller who can
edit posts, plus any further capability named, all refused with the
same rest_forbidden the reference uses. Returns the caller's id.

methods.name: requireCap
methods.doc: 403 rest_forbidden unless the caller holds every capability named.

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: 401 for an anonymous caller, 403 for one who is signed in but refused.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Catalogue
classes.doc:
The route table read from the classes alone: every #[Route] under
src/Minn, as rows, with no request, database, or site behind it. This is
what contracts/api/routes.json is written from, so an agent can read
which routes exist, who may call them, and what they take, without
booting the engine. The per-request router builds the same rows for the
handlers it actually registered, which is what the live index serves.

methods.name: scan
methods.doc:
Every route declared by a class under the source directory, in file
order, then declaration order.

methods.name: document
methods.doc: The rows as the JSON catalogue: a version line and one entry per route.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc:
The fully qualified names of the classes under the directory, from
their paths (PSR-4: Minn\A\B is A/B.php), sorted.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentListArgs
classes.doc:
The WP_Comment_Query arguments a comment list request makes, as the
reference makes them before rest_comment_query (probe
rest-comment-lists): each declared parameter the request carries under
its query name, an empty email and search when none is given, the
orderby name mapped to the query's, the found rows counted, the posts
loaded, the date bounds as one clause, the offset the page makes when
none is given, and ids alone for a HEAD request.

methods.name: of
methods.doc:
The arguments before plugins see them: a parameter maps when the
collection (as rest_comment_collection_params left it) still has it.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2 comment object; edit context adds the moderation-desk fields.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: A comment in the context asked for, through rest_prepare_comment when a plugin hooks it.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: The REST URL builder.

methods.name: buildFields
methods.doc: The wp/v2 comment shape, with the edit-context fields when asked.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/comments: the status tabs with pagination headers, single,
signed-in replies, moderation updates, trash, and force delete.

methods.name: list
methods.doc:
The comments list as the reference serves it: the request's
WP_Comment_Query through rest_comment_query, its totals (counted again
when a page comes back empty), and the comments the caller may read.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One comment, if the caller may read it.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: A signed-in reply; the author fields come from the user.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Status flips and content or author edits, for moderators.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trash remembers where the comment came from; force removes it outright.

methods.name: totals
methods.doc:
The total and the page count: the query's own, or, when it found
nothing (a page past the end), a count without the page.

methods.name: events
methods.doc: Tells plugins about the writes, through the runtime's comment functions.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
What this caller may ask the list for: the edit context and other
statuses are for moderators and editors; comments without a post
belong to moderators, an unreadable post's to those who may read it
(or who give its password); type, author, author_exclude and
author_email to anyone who can edit posts (the email judged as sent,
before sanitizing empties a bad one).

methods.name: readablePost
methods.doc: A post whose comments this caller may read: one it may read, unlocked or opened with its password.

methods.name: readable
methods.doc: A listed comment this caller may read: a moderator any, its author their own, anyone an approved one on a post they may read.

methods.name: plainComment
methods.doc: A comment row of the plain kind, or the reference's invalid-id error.

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
The fields a request sends, as the reference's controller prepares
them for the runtime: the content, the author fields, the address (a
moderator may name one) and the browser.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Context
classes.doc:
The view a REST caller asked for. View is the public shape, edit adds the
raw halves and the caller's own action links, embed is the reduced shape
a linked resource carries when it rides inside another response.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The context a request names, view when it names none or names one the route does not serve.

methods.name: isEdit
methods.doc: Whether this is the edit context.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\DeclaredPostsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/{rest_base} for extra post types declared by an active extension.
Registered last so core collections (users, comments, menus, ...) match
first; an unknown base is declined, so a plugin's own route under wp/v2
(answered by the runtime after the engine's routes) is not shadowed.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A declared type's list.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A declared type's single post.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a post of a declared type.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a post of a declared type.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trashes or deletes a post of a declared type.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\DeclaredTermsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/{rest_base} for the taxonomies plugin code registers to show in
REST (probe rest-plugin-types), answered as the core taxonomies are.
Registered after the declared post types; a base no such taxonomy names
declines, so a plugin's own route under wp/v2 is not shadowed.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A registered taxonomy's terms.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One term of a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a term in a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a term of a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Deletes a term of a registered taxonomy.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Embed
classes.doc:
The _embed decoration and the embed context. Every embeddable link in an
object's _links is answered in-process as the same caller with
context=embed and placed under _embedded[rel]; a rel whose every embed
came back empty or as an error is left out, while an empty list beside a
full one stays (wp:term keeps its empty tags list next to the categories).
Lists have _fields applied per item before the links are read, so a
_fields value without _links embeds nothing there; a single object embeds
first and is filtered afterwards. The embed context is the view object
cut to the reference's key set for that kind of item.

constants.name: KEYS
constants.value: array (   'post' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'date',     2 => 'slug',     3 => 'type',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'title',     6 => 'excerpt',     7 => 'author',     8 => 'featured_media',     9 => '_links',   ),   'media' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'date',     2 => 'slug',     3 => 'type',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'title',     6 => 'author',     7 => 'featured_media',     8 => 'caption',     9 => 'alt_text',     10 => 'media_type',     11 => 'mime_type',     12 => 'media_details',     13 => 'source_url',     14 => '_links',   ),   'user' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'name',     2 => 'url',     3 => 'description',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'slug',     6 => 'avatar_urls',     7 => '_links',   ),   'term' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'link',     2 => 'name',     3 => 'slug',     4 => 'taxonomy',     5 => '_links',   ),   'comment' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'parent',     2 => 'author',     3 => 'author_name',     4 => 'author_url',     5 => 'date',     6 => 'content',     7 => 'link',     8 => 'type',     9 => 'author_avatar_urls',     10 => '_links',   ), )

methods.name: requested
methods.doc: Null when _embed is absent; [] for every rel; otherwise the rels asked for. @return ?list<string>

methods.name: decorate
methods.doc: Decorates a finished response: the embed context, then _embedded, then the deferred _fields.

methods.name: shape
methods.doc: An item cut to the embed shape of its object type (a post type, a taxonomy, attachment, user or comment); any other kept whole. @param array<string, mixed> $item @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: answer
methods.doc: The linked object in embed context, or null when the link answers with an error.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: A REST href in either URL form, as the route path and its query. @return array{0: string, 1: array<string, string>}

methods.name: kind
methods.doc: Which key set a route's objects take in embed context; null for routes without one.

methods.name: context
methods.doc: The embed shape, with the fields plugin code registered for the item's type to show in embed.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\EngineRoutes
classes.doc:
The engine's own REST routes in the reference's regex form, for the
index and for the runtime's server, whose route table plugin code reads
to learn what the site answers (a missing /wp/v2/comments there reads as
"comments are off").

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The router's routes as route => methods, the way the index lists them.
shapes: @param list<string> $declaredBases the rest_base of every declared type

params.name: declaredBases
params.doc: the rest_base of every declared type

methods.name: forms
methods.doc:
A route attribute pattern as the reference writes routes: `{id:\d+}`
becomes `(?P<id>\d+)`, a bare capture matches one segment, a `{rest*}`
capture the remainder, and a literal constraint (`{base:posts}`, or
the alternation `{base:posts|pages}`) expands to one route per
literal. The declared-type routes are written once as a `{base:[...]}`
catch-all; they list per declared type under its rest_base (as the
reference lists a registered type) and not at all when no type is
declared, so nothing listed answers no-route.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Fields
classes.doc:
The _fields response filter. Dot paths descend ("title.rendered"); the
object's own key order is kept. Applied per item on list responses and to
the whole payload otherwise, which is why _fields on the associative
types response strips every key and yields [] over HTTP, a reference
quirk the engine reproduces by construction.

constructor.doc: embedded first and filtered by Embed afterwards

params.name: deferred
params.doc: true when _embed rides along: a single object is

methods.name: fromQuery
methods.doc: The _fields selection a query carries, or null for everything.

methods.name: withLinksForEmbedded
methods.doc: The same paths plus _links whenever _embedded is among them: the reference's single-object rule under _embed.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: The object with only the selected fields.

methods.name: select
methods.doc:
The fields a response keeps when a caller names some: known fields as
given, dotted paths whose root is known, and `id` whenever it exists.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\GlobalStylesController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/global-styles: the site editor's saved styles (one post per
theme, read and written by id, with its revisions) and the active
theme's own styles and variations. There is no collection, no create
and no delete; the post is made on first use, as on the reference.

constants.name: CANNOT_EDIT
constants.value: 'Sorry, you are not allowed to edit this global style.'

constants.name: CANNOT_READ_REVISIONS
constants.value: 'Sorry, you are not allowed to view revisions of this post.'

methods.name: single
methods.doc: The saved styles by id: anyone who edits posts may read them, editing context needs the theme.

routes: POST /wp/v2/global-styles/{id:[\/\d+]+} (cap edit_theme_options; global styles {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/global-styles/{id:[\/\d+]+} (cap edit_theme_options; global styles {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/global-styles/{id:[\/\d+]+} (cap edit_theme_options; global styles {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: Replaces the title, settings, or styles the body names; what it leaves out stays.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc: The style variations the active theme ships; listed ahead of the theme's own route, whose pattern would take this path too.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The active theme's settings and styles, the engine's defaults underneath.

routes: GET /wp/v2/global-styles/{parent:[\d]+}/revisions (cap edit_theme_options; global styles parent {parent} must exist)
methods.name: revisions
methods.doc: The revisions of the saved styles, newest first; all of them unless per_page pages them.

routes: GET /wp/v2/global-styles/{parent:[\d]+}/revisions/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_theme_options; global styles parent {parent} must exist)
methods.name: revision
methods.doc: One revision of the saved styles.

methods.name: requireTheme
methods.doc: The theme routes answer only for the active stylesheet, and only to those who edit posts.

methods.name: requireParent
methods.doc: Revisions are for those who edit the theme, of a parent that is a global-styles post.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: A title arrives as a string or as {raw}; anything else is ignored.

methods.name: node
methods.doc: settings and styles are objects when present; a scalar is the reference's type error, null is ignored.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\GlobalStylesObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2/global-styles item, theme, and revision shapes.

methods.name: item
methods.doc:
The saved styles: the title both ways, settings by origin, styles
with their presets resolved, the links; in editing context the
app's lock fields too, which a global-styles post never carries.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The active theme's own styles as the themes/{stylesheet} route answers them.

methods.name: revision
methods.doc:
One revision row: both nodes when the body holds anything at all,
neither when it is blank, then the row's own facts; no links.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: Writing methods appear for a theme editor; the CSS action for whoever may write CSS.

methods.name: node
methods.doc: An empty node is an object on the wire, never a list.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\IndexController
classes.doc:
The API index at /wp-json/: the site facts monitors read (name, url,
home, namespaces) and the routes this engine serves, described from its
own router rather than the reference's full schema; and the index of one
namespace at /wp-json/{namespace}, the same routes narrowed.

methods.name: index
methods.doc: The REST index: namespaces, routes, and the site's description.

methods.name: namespaceIndex
methods.doc:
One namespace's index, as the reference answers /wp-json/wp/v2 (or oembed/1.0): the
namespace, its routes (the namespace root among them), and the link
up to the root index. A namespace the engine does not serve is left
to the runtime, whose plugins may own it.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\InstalledThemesController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/themes as the reference answers it (probe rest-themes): the
installed themes, or only those with a status (active, inactive), each
with its style.css headers raw and rendered, where it lives, and whether
it is a block theme. The active theme also carries its supports as the
editor reads them, the template types and part areas it may define, and
a link to the theme export; any theme with user styles links to them. Anyone who can edit
a type shown in REST may read the active theme; listing the others takes
switch_themes. Each theme goes through rest_prepare_theme. Served with
plugins loaded, since a theme's supports come from its own code.

constants.name: STATUS
constants.value: array (   'status' =>    array (     'type' => 'array',     'items' =>      array (       'type' => 'string',       'enum' =>        array (         0 => 'active',         1 => 'inactive',       ),     ),     'description' => 'Limit result set to themes assigned one or more statuses.',     'required' => false,   ), )

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The installed themes the caller may see.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One theme by its stylesheet.

methods.name: viewsThemes
methods.doc: May list the installed themes.

methods.name: viewsActive
methods.doc: May read the active theme: anyone who lists themes, or edits a type shown in REST.

methods.name: requireRuntime
methods.doc: A theme's supports come from its own code: without the runtime there is no answer to give.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Links
classes.doc: Response link relations compacted through CURIEs: a rel that matches a CURIE's template becomes `name:suffix`, and the used CURIEs ride along.

methods.name: item
methods.doc:
One link as a response serves it: its attributes, then its href; a
self link's target hints after the href, where the reference adds them.

methods.name: compact
methods.doc: Links with their curies applied, as the reference compacts them.
shapes: @param list<array{name: string, href: string, templated?: bool}> $curies

params.name: curies
params.shape: list<array{name: string, href: string, templated?: bool}>

classes.name: Minn\Rest\LiveSettings
classes.doc:
wp/v2/settings with plugins loaded, served from the registered settings
as the reference serves it (probe rest-settings): every setting shown in
REST, core's and a plugin's alike, under its REST name. A read asks
rest_pre_get_setting first, then get_option with the schema's default,
and a value its schema refuses reads as null. A write takes the body's
values its schema accepts (null always), offers each to
rest_pre_update_setting, deletes the option for null (refused when what
is stored does not fit the schema, since null could not restore it) and
otherwise hands it to update_option.

methods.name: shown
methods.doc: The settings shown in REST, by REST name, with the arguments the filters are handed.
shapes: @return array<string, array{name: string, schema: array<string, mixed>, option_name: string}>

methods.name: payload
methods.doc: Every shown setting's value. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: store
methods.doc: Writes the shown settings a body names, after refusing the values their schemas refuse.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\MediaController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/media: list, single, upload on both transports (multipart field
"file", or a raw body with Content-Disposition), field edits, and force
delete with the files.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The media list: the post lists' own path for attachments (probe rest-media-lists), each item in the media shape.

routes: GET /wp/v2/media/{id:[\d]+} (public; attachment {id} must exist; edit context: cap edit_post on {id})
methods.name: single
methods.doc: One attachment.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Uploads a file and creates its attachment.

routes: POST /wp/v2/media/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; attachment {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/media/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; attachment {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/media/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; attachment {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: The editable fields the app uses.

routes: DELETE /wp/v2/media/{id:[\d]+} (cap delete_post on {id}; attachment {id} must exist)
methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Attachments cannot be trashed; force removes the row, its meta, and its files.

methods.name: storeWithPlugins
methods.doc:
With plugins loaded, the file goes through the runtime's
wp_handle_sideload (a raw body) or wp_handle_upload (a form field),
as the reference's REST upload sends it: their prefilters, the allowed
types (upload_mimes), the content check, the name, the move and
wp_handle_upload, where SVG and security plugins work. A refusal is the
engine's REST error with the runtime's words.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} the path relative to the uploads folder, and the type

methods.name: insertedWithPlugins
methods.doc:
With plugins loaded, the attachment saved as the reference's controller
saves it (probe rest-media-save): the photo's own title and caption
(wp_read_image_metadata) unless the request names them, the prepared
attachment through rest_pre_insert_attachment, the file's name as the
title when none is left, then wp_insert_attachment, the REST actions
(the alt text between them), wp_after_insert_post, and the sizes.

methods.name: preparedAttachment
methods.doc:
rest_pre_insert_attachment over the prepared attachment, then the
caption and description the request sends.

methods.name: finishedWithPlugins
methods.doc:
After rest_insert_attachment: the alt text, rest_after_insert_attachment
and wp_after_insert_post, in the reference's order.

methods.name: params
methods.doc:
The fields a media request sends, wherever it sends them: the query, a
form, or a JSON body.

methods.name: inserted
methods.doc: The attachment's row written and the reference's actions told, for a file already stored.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\MediaObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2 media object, view and edit context.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: An attachment in the context asked for, through rest_prepare_attachment when a plugin hooks it.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: The REST URL builder.

methods.name: buildFields

methods.name: details
methods.doc: media_details: dims, file, filesize, and the sizes with URLs.

methods.name: descriptionHtml
methods.doc: The attachment-page image HTML that description.rendered carries.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\MenuItemObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2/menu-items resource.

methods.name: view
methods.doc: The wp/v2 menu-item shape.

methods.doc: The wp/v2 menu shape.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\MenusController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/menus, menu-items, and menu-locations. Viewing needs edit_posts;
writes need edit_theme_options. Anonymous callers get 401.

methods.name: listMenus
methods.doc: Every classic menu.

methods.name: singleMenu
methods.doc: One menu.

methods.name: createMenu
methods.doc: Creates a menu.

methods.name: updateMenu
methods.doc: Renames or re-describes a menu.

methods.doc: Deletes a menu and its items.

methods.doc: The items of a menu.

methods.name: singleItem

methods.doc: Creates a menu item.

PUT /wp/v2/menu-items/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_theme_options; menu item {id} must exist)

classes.name: Minn\Rest\NavigationController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/navigation: the block theme's navigation menus, stored as
wp_navigation posts. The reading and writing is the posts machinery with
this type's own capabilities (every one of them edit_theme_options), so
only the routes live here.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The navigation posts.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One navigation post.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\OEmbedController
classes.doc:
oembed/1.0 as the reference answers it (probe oembed). embed is the
provider side: one of the site's own addresses as embed data (the post
through url_to_postid and oembed_request_post_id), "Not Found" for
anything else; format=xml is served as XML on the way out
(RuntimeRoutes::serve). proxy is the editor's consumer side, for anyone
who can edit posts: the site's own addresses answered locally, anything
else fetched through WP_oEmbed with the editor's size, its markup
through oembed_result, and kept in a transient for a day
(rest_oembed_ttl) under the request's arguments.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PolicyGate
classes.doc:
Judges a route's policy against the caller, with the reference's
refusals: a caller who is not signed in gets the policy's sign-in code
at 401, a bad nonce is always 403 rest_cookie_invalid_nonce, and a
signed-in caller who lacks a capability gets the refusal code at 403.
A subject the policy names is looked up first and answers its 404
before any of those. The edit-context policy is judged as well when
the request asks for it.

methods.name: closure
methods.doc: The judge as the router takes it.

methods.name: judge
methods.doc: Throws the refusal the policy names, or returns.

methods.name: subject
methods.doc:
The record's 404 when it does not exist. "me" names the caller, who
must then be signed in; the reference answers that with its plain
sign-in refusal whatever the route's own code is.

methods.name: type
methods.doc:
A {base} that names no declared type declines the route, so the next
one may take it. A write is judged with the type's own capabilities
(probe rest-plugin-caps): a missing post first (404), then the
caller (401 signed out, 403 refused).

methods.name: taxonomy
methods.doc:
A {base} that names no registered taxonomy declines the route. A
write is judged with the taxonomy's own capabilities (probe
rest-plugin-caps): a missing term first (404), then the caller.

statuses (every registered one, and any), each REST taxonomy's term
filter (a list, or a query with children for a hierarchical one and an
operator for the include side) under a relation, stickies for posts, and
formats for a type with post formats. Plugins change them through
rest_{type}_collection_params, asked once a request.

The WP_Query arguments a post list request makes, as the reference makes

per_page, stickies (only them, or none of them), an exact search, each
taxonomy's include and exclude under the request's relation, formats

mapped to the query's, and stickies left where they fall unless asked.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostObject
classes.doc:
Builds the wp/v2 post and page objects in the reference's shape: the
view context, the edit context (raw+rendered dual fields, editor-only
fields, and cap-gated wp:action-* links), and their _links blocks.

constants.name: NAVIGATION
constants.doc: The one post type whose REST shape is not post-shaped.

constants.name: BLOCK
constants.doc: The other: a pattern carries its content raw, its category, and its sync status.

methods.name: view
methods.doc: The view-context object, through rest_prepare_{type} when a plugin hooks it.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc: The edit-context object, through rest_prepare_{type} when a plugin hooks it.

methods.name: permalink
methods.doc: A post's permalink as of now: pretty once live with a slug, ?p= (or ?page_id=) before.

methods.name: restBase
methods.doc: The rest_base of a type.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: The _links of a post in the view context.

methods.name: permalinkTemplate
methods.doc:
The editor's sample permalink: the structure with the name token left
in place (pages: the parent path plus %pagename%), or the query form
when permalinks are plain.

methods.name: modifiedUnsaved
methods.doc: Whether a live post carries an autosave newer than its saved revision.

methods.name: lockHolder
methods.doc: The OTHER user holding a live _edit_lock (150 second window), or null.

methods.name: editLinks
methods.doc: The view links plus the caller's verbs and cap-gated wp:action-* entries.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: A MySQL datetime in the reference's ISO form.

methods.name: meta
methods.doc:
The meta field: the keys registered to show in REST (probe rest-meta),
or the footnotes alone without the runtime.

methods.name: navigationView
methods.doc:
A navigation menu is a post with almost nothing on it: no author, no
excerpt, no featured image, no comments, no taxonomies, and so no
class list either. What it does carry is a template field and the
rendered menu.

methods.name: blockView
methods.doc:
A pattern (wp_block) is read by editors only, so its title and
content come raw even in view context: no rendered title, no rendered
content. It carries an excerpt, the footnotes meta, its pattern
categories, and the sync status core registers beside meta.

methods.name: viewFields
methods.doc: The view-context object: the shared fields, then the type's own, then class_list and _links.

methods.name: viewTerms
methods.doc:
The taxonomies a non-page carries, each as [term_id, slug] pairs; the
format terms only for posts.

methods.name: typeFields
methods.doc:
Pages carry parent and menu_order first; posts carry their term ids,
and only the post type has sticky and format, among the shared fields.

methods.name: classList
methods.doc:
The reference's class_list order: identity, type, status, format (posts
only), password, thumbnail, hentry, then one class per term.

methods.name: termLinks
methods.doc: The taxonomy links a type carries: posts their categories and tags, patterns their pattern categories, pages and menus none.

methods.name: editFields
methods.doc:
The edit-context object for a given caller: raw+rendered dual fields,
password, permalink_template, generated_slug, block_version, Minn
Admin's registered list fields, and the cap-gated action links.

methods.name: allow
methods.doc:
What the caller may do to this post, which the reference reports in
every context: a reader sees GET, an editor of the post sees the
write verbs, and DELETE only when they may delete it too.

methods.name: gmt
methods.doc:
A gmt timestamp for the wire: the stored one, or, when it is the
draft zero, the local time converted through the site's offset, the
way the reference derives it.

rest-post-lists): the caller and the statuses judged, the request's
parameters sanitized, the query arguments through rest_{type}_query
and rest_query_var-*, a WP_Query (so pre_get_posts and every query
filter run), then each post the caller may read (or edit, in the edit
context) shaped (by $shape when the type has its own object, as
media does). The totals are the query's, counted again without the
page when a later page came back empty. A media search also matches
file names, as the reference's does.

the last is refused.

Writes a new post's row as the insert does: its guid becomes the
permalink as of now (pretty only when live). The default category
follows, and the body's own terms come after rest_insert_{type}, so

Moves a post to the trash through the runtime's wp_trash_post, which
tells plugins and keeps what the way back needs; without plugins
loaded, the same rows by hand.

methods.doc:
After a save: a published post (not a page) that moved keeps its old
slug on record, and one that stayed published keeps its old date; one
brought back from the trash has its wanted slug back and stops waiting
for it.

methods.doc:
A draft that was never given a date (its GMT date is zero) has a
floating one: every save moves it to now, and the GMT date stays zero
until the post leaves draft or pending, as on the reference.

methods.doc: A date in the future turns a publish into a schedule, whether the status was sent or kept.

methods.doc:

by edit_others_*), the two flags, password, the page attributes, the

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RegisteredFields
classes.doc:
The fields plugin code adds to an object type with register_rest_field,
as the reference serves them (probe rest-fields). A get callback's value
follows the item's own fields, before its links. It is handed the item
so far (without links, cut to the fields asked for, id kept), the
field's name, the request and the object type. A field is left out when
_fields does not name it or its schema's context does not include the
request's. A write runs the update callbacks for the fields its body
names, with the saved object, before rest_after_insert; an error one
returns is the write's answer.

reference's controllers set it: a write and a delete answer in edit
(a term's delete in view); a read in the one asked for, or view.

them. Without plugins they are Minn's own render. With plugins loaded

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RestMeta
classes.doc:
An object's meta field over REST, from the keys registered to show
there (probe rest-meta). Each key answers under its REST name (its own,
or show_in_rest's name): those for every subtype, then the object's
subtype's, left out of a context their schema does not name. A single
key reads its first stored value (its default, or its type's empty value,
when none), a multiple key each one; each value is checked against the
key's schema (null when it does not fit, the empty value of a scalar
type for '') and cast, or handed to the key's prepare callback. A write
goes key by key in registration order: null (or an empty list) deletes,
a value its schema refuses is a 400, and a key the user may not edit is
a 403 (an unchanged single value is left alone first). The errors are
gathered; the first is the answer, with the others beside it.

methods.doc: The meta field of an object in a context (the one the request answers in, when none is named), keyed by REST name. @return array<string, mixed>

The keys registered to show in REST for an object type and subtype,
each with its REST name, whether it is single, its schema (a multiple
key's an array of its own) and its prepare callback; keys of a type

The REST server's filters around one of Minn's own routes, as the
reference runs them around every route (contracts/runtime.md, "The REST
server's envelope"): rest_request_before_callbacks is handed the argument
check's error or null and may refuse; the route's permission is the
next refusal; rest_dispatch_request may answer in place of the route;
rest_request_after_callbacks sees whatever came of it and may change it.
A value other than an error from the first filter does not answer: the
route still runs. With nothing hooked on any of the three, the route
answers as it would without plugins, unconverted; and before the runtime
boots (the API is built first) there are no plugins to ask.

output schema (ability_invalid_output), and wp_after_execute_ability.

methods.name: input
methods.doc: True, or why the input does not fit.

methods.name: execute
methods.doc: The ability's answer, or the error that stopped it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AccountFlows
classes.doc:
The account functions a sign-in page and plugins call, with the
reference's checks, words, hooks and mail (probe account-flows): asking
for a password reset (retrieve_password), resetting one
(reset_password), registering (register_new_user), and telling the site
and the new user about a registration (wp_new_user_notification).

constants.name: NO_ACCOUNT
constants.value: 'Error: There is no account with that username or email address.'

methods.name: retrievePassword
methods.doc:
A reset link mailed to the account a login or email names: true, or
the refusal (no name, no such account, a plugin's error, reset not
allowed, or the mail failing).

methods.name: resetPassword
methods.doc: A new password for a user, announced before (password_reset) and after (after_password_reset).

methods.name: registerNewUser
methods.doc:
A new account for a login and an email, with a generated password and
the nag to change it: its id, or every refusal at once (the name
empty, illegal, taken or barred; the email empty, malformed or taken;
whatever register_post and registration_errors add).

methods.name: newUserNotification
methods.doc:
A new account announced: to the site's address (unless only the user
is told), then to the user with a link to set their password (unless
only the site is, or the old call shape asks for nobody).

methods.name: resetLink
methods.doc: The link that opens the password form for a user's key.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AjaxController
classes.doc:
admin-ajax.php, the endpoint plugins post their front-end work to: a form
submitted without a reload, a spam check, a background job. The action a
request names runs the handlers registered as wp_ajax_{action} for a
signed-in visitor and wp_ajax_nopriv_{action} for anyone else, answered as
the reference answers them (contracts/runtime.md "admin-ajax.php").

It is an admin request: is_admin() is true while the plugins load and
admin_init fires before the handler. A handler usually ends the request
itself (wp_send_json, wp_die, exit), so the endpoint's headers go out
before it runs; one that returns is followed by the reference's "0".

constants.name: CORE
constants.doc: The core actions the endpoint answers itself, under the prefix for who is asking: the action => the handler.

constants.name: ADMIN_FILTERS
constants.doc: The filters the reference's admin includes add once plugins have loaded: the hook, the callback.

methods.name: claims
methods.doc: Whether a request is for the endpoint, which the runtime boots as an admin request.

methods.name: dispatch
methods.doc: Runs the handlers registered for the action the request names.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: The action the request names, the posted field over the query's, or null when there is none to run.

methods.name: allowedOrigin
methods.doc: The two cross-origin headers, for an Origin that is this site's own address; empty for any other.

methods.name: registerCore
methods.doc: The reference registers its own actions after admin_init, only those for who is asking, ahead of a plugin's.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AllowedOptions
classes.doc:
The settings-page allowlist plugins extend: option group => the option
names a settings form in that group may save. The engine renders no
settings pages, so the list is only recorded, never enforced.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
The allowlist with each new name appended to its group once, groups
created as needed. A group handed as anything but a list adds nothing.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ApplicationPasswordEvents
classes.doc:
Application password changes made over REST, as the reference makes them
(probe rest-application-password-hooks): the prepared item (the name,
and an app id a new one is given) through
rest_pre_insert_application_password, then WP_Application_Passwords
(which tells plugins through wp_create_, wp_update_ and
wp_delete_application_password), then rest_after_insert_application_password.

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
A new password: its record and its plain text in groups of four, or
the reference's refusal.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A password renamed (when the body names it): its record as it stands.

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc: The item the request prepares (its name; a new one's app id), through rest_pre_insert_application_password. @param array<string, mixed> $fields

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ApplicationPasswordSignIn
classes.doc:
wp_authenticate_application_password as the reference answers it (probe
application-passwords-api): a user found already stands; outside an API
request (application_password_is_api_request) nothing is tried; then the
user by login or email, the feature's availability (for the site, for
the user), and each of the user's passwords, a match passing through
wp_authenticate_application_password_errors, recorded, and announced
(application_password_did_authenticate); every refusal announced
through application_password_failed_authentication.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc: The signed-in user, the input unchanged, or the refusal.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
determine_current_user's application password step: an earlier
answer stands; else the user the REST request's application password
signed in (the engine checked the password before plugins loaded),
heard again as the reference hears it: the feature's availability,
wp_authenticate_application_password_errors, then
application_password_did_authenticate; a refusal is announced and
leaves the request signed out.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: Why the user may not sign in by application password, or null when they may.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Assets
classes.doc:
The registry behind wp_register_/wp_enqueue_ for scripts and styles:
handles, sources, dependencies, versions, inline additions, localized
data, and the head/footer split. Printing follows the reference's tag
shapes as far as captured; see contracts/runtime.md.

methods.name: watch
methods.doc: A listener called after every change, so a plugin-facing view can stay current.

methods.name: setQueue
methods.doc: The queue as a plugin left it after editing the view directly.

methods.name: register
methods.signature: register(string $handle, string|false $src, array $deps, string|bool|null $ver, mixed $extra): bool
methods.doc: Registers an asset under a handle.

methods.name: externalHosts
methods.doc: The hosts the queued assets load from, other than the site's own.
shapes: @return list<string> hosts of enqueued sources (dependencies first) away from the given host, for dns-prefetch hints

methods.name: deregister
methods.doc: Forgets an asset.

methods.name: enqueue
methods.doc:
Queues an asset for printing (probe placeholders-admin). One that is
neither registered nor among the reference's own handles waits, and
joins the queue when it is registered; one of the reference's own the
engine ships no file for is queued as the reference would queue it.

methods.name: dequeue
methods.doc: Removes an asset from the queue, or from the handles waiting for registration.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: Whether a handle is registered, by the site or as one the reference registers itself (data/default-assets.json).

methods.name: enqueued
methods.doc:
Queued directly, or pulled in as the dependency of something queued,
however deep. The reference answers the same way, and plugin code
leans on it: WooCommerce only attaches its settings blob when it
finds `wc-settings` "enqueued", and nothing queues that handle by
name, it only ever rides in as a dependency.

methods.name: doneList
methods.doc: The handles printed so far.

methods.name: setDone
methods.doc: The printed handles as a plugin left them after editing the view directly.

methods.name: done
methods.doc: Whether a handle has been printed.

methods.name: addInline
methods.doc: Attaches inline code to an asset.

methods.name: addData
methods.doc: Attaches a data key to an asset.

methods.name: setTranslations
methods.doc: Names the text domain and folder a script's translations come from, and makes the script depend on wp-i18n.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: A data key of an asset, or false.

methods.name: localize
methods.doc: Attaches a localized object to a script.

methods.name: toPrint
methods.doc: Every queued handle not yet printed, dependencies first, filtered to the group (footer or not).

methods.name: toPrintHandles
methods.doc:
Named handles and everything they depend on, in printing order, whether
or not they were queued; what already printed is left out.

methods.name: withPath
methods.doc:
Enqueued handles that name a file on disk, mapped to that path. A style
registered with a `path` datum is saying it can be inlined; whether it
is small enough to be worth inlining is the caller's decision.

methods.name: unsource
methods.doc: Drops a handle's source so it prints as markup rather than a link.

methods.name: markDone
methods.doc: Records a handle as printed.

methods.name: item
methods.doc: One registered asset, or null.

methods.name: items
methods.doc: Every registered asset.

methods.name: queue
methods.doc: The handles queued.

methods.name: kind
methods.doc: Whether these are scripts or styles.

methods.name: depsOf
methods.doc: A handle's dependencies: as registered, or as the reference registers it. @return list<string>

methods.name: held
methods.doc:
Whether a handle is an item to attach to: one registered here, or a
stylesheet the reference registers itself, held from then on with no
file (the engine ships none of those) so what a plugin attaches to it
still prints. A core script is not held: its inline code without the
library would only fail in the browser.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Avatar
classes.doc: Avatars the way get_avatar_data and get_avatar decide them: the argument defaults, the email an id, user, post, or comment names, the Gravatar URL, and the attributes. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

methods.name: dataArgs
methods.doc: The data arguments normalised: sizes to integers, the default token, the rating lowercased.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The Gravatar hash an email yields; '' for no email.

methods.name: hashFromAddress
methods.doc: A hash given as an md5.gravatar.com address, else null.

methods.name: urlArgs
methods.doc: The Gravatar URL's query arguments for the data arguments. @return array<string, string|int|false>

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The classes: the size class, a default marker, the caller's own. @return list

methods.name: extraAttributes
methods.doc: The extra attribute string with loading and decoding added when the caller did not set them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockFilters
classes.doc:
The block-level filters plugin code hooks (pre_render_block,
render_block_data, render_block, render_block_{name}), applied around the
engine's own renderer so a plugin sees every block the page renders, not
only the ones it registered.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: Whether any block filter is registered.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: A block as the parsed array plugins receive.
shapes: @return array<string, mixed> the parsed-array shape plugin code reads

methods.name: fromArray
methods.doc: A block from the parsed array plugins hand back.

methods.name: before
methods.doc: A short-circuit from pre_render_block, or the block as render_block_data left it.

methods.name: after
methods.doc: A rendered block through render_block and its per-name filter.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockHooks
classes.doc:
The Block Hooks API on the engine's own front end: a plugin asks for its
block to be inserted next to an anchor block in a template part or a
pattern (WooCommerce puts the mini-cart after the navigation in a
header), and the markup the renderer reads carries those insertions.

The facade owns the traversal (wp-api/blocks.php); this is the seam the
theme blocks call, and it stays inert until a plugin actually hooks
something, so a site without such a plugin parses nothing extra.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: Whether block hooks are registered and the runtime is up.

methods.name: forPart
methods.doc:
A template part's markup with its hooked blocks inserted. The context
is the part itself: a plugin reads its area to tell a header from a
footer, and its content to see whether its block is already there.

methods.name: registeredPattern
methods.doc:
A plugin-registered pattern's content, hooks already applied by the
registry, for a slug the theme does not carry. Null when the runtime
is not up or nothing registered that name.

methods.name: forPattern
methods.doc:
A theme pattern's markup with its hooked blocks inserted, with the
pattern array as the context (blockTypes and categories are how a
plugin recognises a header pattern).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockMetadata
classes.doc:
block.json to the settings a block type registers with: the property
renames, the script and style handles (registered through the closures,
one per entry), the view script modules, the block hooks positions, and
the render template as a callback. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/blocks.json.

methods.name: settings
methods.signature: settings(array $metadata, Closure $scriptHandle, Closure $styleHandle, Closure $moduleId, Closure $render): array
methods.doc: Block settings from a block.json, the way the reference maps its properties.
shapes: @param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $scriptHandle registers one script entry, answering its handle
@param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $styleHandle registers one style entry
@param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $moduleId registers one view script module entry
@param Closure(string): ?Closure $render the render callback for a template path, or null when the file is missing

params.name: scriptHandle
params.doc: registers one script entry, answering its handle

params.name: moduleId
params.doc: registers one view script module entry

params.name: render
params.doc: the render callback for a template path, or null when the file is missing

methods.name: assetHandle
methods.doc: The script or style handle a block.json field registers under; core blocks keep the `wp-block-` spelling.

methods.name: handles
methods.doc: The registered handles for one asset field: every entry when the field lists several; null when the field is absent. @return list<string>|null

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockTemplates
classes.doc:
Block templates plugins register at runtime, by their namespaced name
("plugin//slug"). A theme file or a saved template of the same slug
wins; otherwise the registered content renders for that slug.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: The registered row, or the refusal code the reference reports.

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Forgets a registered template; the row, or null.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every registered template.
shapes: @return array<string, array<string, mixed>> by registered name

methods.name: get
methods.doc: One registered template, or null.

methods.name: bySlug
methods.doc: A registered template by slug, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockWidget
classes.doc:
A block widget's legacy class name. Every widget the block editor saves
is one block of markup, and a classic theme styles it by the widget
class the equivalent legacy widget used, so the wrapper carries a
second class named after the FIRST block in the content. A block with
no legacy equivalent adds nothing.

constants.name: LEGACY_CLASSES
constants.doc: First block name => the legacy widget class a theme styles.

methods.name: classNameFor
methods.doc: The legacy widget class a block widget maps to.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentCloser
classes.doc:
The Discussion setting that closes comments on old posts. Observed on the
reference: only the "post" type closes (the types filter changes nothing),
status is not consulted, the age is whole days on post_date_gmt and must
exceed the setting (a fifteen-day-old post stays open at fifteen), and zero
days switches the rule off.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: Whether comments stay open on a post under the close-after-days setting.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentEvents
classes.doc:
What the reference's REST comments controller tells plugins, for the
engine's own: with plugins loaded every change goes through the
runtime's comment functions (wp_insert_comment, wp_update_comment,
wp_set_comment_status, wp_trash_comment, wp_delete_comment), which fire
the reference's actions in its order, and the REST actions follow.
Without a booted runtime the rows are written as before and nothing is
told.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Whether plugins are loaded to be told anything.

methods.name: allow
methods.doc: The check a new comment passes on the reference before it is written: check_comment_flood, with the address, the email and the GMT date.

methods.name: restCreate
methods.doc:
A comment created over REST with plugins loaded, as the reference's
controller creates one (probe rest-comment-save): the request's
fields through rest_preprocess_comment, the signed-in author filled
in, the content check (allow_empty_comment), the date, the length
check, wp_allow_comment (a duplicate is a 409, a flood a 400),
rest_pre_insert_comment, then wp_insert_comment over
wp_filter_comment; a refusal is its REST error.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $prepared the request's fields as the controller prepares them

params.name: prepared
params.doc: the request's fields as the controller prepares them

methods.name: restUpdate
methods.doc:
A comment changed over REST with plugins loaded: the request's fields
through rest_preprocess_comment, the content and length checks,
wp_update_comment, then the status, as the reference's controller
changes one.

methods.name: changeStatus
methods.doc:
A REST status asked for, as the reference's controller changes it:
nothing when it is already so; approve and hold through
wp_set_comment_status with that word, spam, unspam, trash and untrash
through their own functions.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: Writes a new comment and returns its id; an approved one is counted on its post. @param array<string, mixed> $columns

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
An edit through REST: the fields, as wp_update_comment writes them
(which tells plugins even when nothing changed), then the status
through wp_set_comment_status when it moves.

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: Moves a comment to the trash, keeping its status and the time for the way back.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes a comment for good.

methods.name: restSaved
methods.doc: rest_insert_comment, then rest_after_insert_comment, with the comment as it stands and the request; no $before is a new comment.

methods.name: restDeleted
methods.doc: rest_delete_comment, after a trash or a delete, with the comment as it was and the response. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: preprocessed
methods.doc: rest_preprocess_comment over the prepared comment.

methods.name: requireContent
methods.doc:
The reference's content check: allow_empty_comment, handed the comment
with the author, parent, post and user filled in; empty content is a 400.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: A plugin's error as REST serves it: its own status, or 500.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentFeedQuery
classes.doc:
The comments a comments feed's main query carries, as the reference
finds them (probe comment-feed-query). For a listing (the site's, an
archive's, a search's) they come before its posts, which are then
narrowed to the posts those comments are on; for a single post they come
after it. Either way the comment_feed_* filters shape the query (handed
the WP_Query), only approved comments that are not notes count, newest
first, as many as a feed carries.

methods.name: listing
methods.doc: A listing's comments, then its posts narrowed to theirs: the posts query's join and where as they stand after posts_join.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A single post's comments, once the query has found the post.

methods.name: request
methods.signature: request(WP_Query $query, string $join, string $where, string $groupby, string $select): string
methods.doc: The request, its pieces through the comment_feed_* filters.

methods.name: keep
shapes: @param list<mixed> $rows rows or ids, each made a WP_Comment

params.name: rows
params.doc: rows or ids, each made a WP_Comment

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentForm
classes.doc:
The comment form's submission with plugins loaded
(wp_handle_comment_submission), in the order the reference runs it
(contracts/runtime.md "The comment form"): a reply to a comment still
held is refused; the post is looked at, each refusal with its action
(comment_id_not_found, comment_closed, comment_on_trash, comment_on_draft,
comment_on_password_protected) and pre_comment_on_post when it takes
comments; the signed-in user's own name and addresses replace the form's,
or a site that requires sign-in refuses; the required fields, an empty
comment (allow_empty_comment) and the column lengths are checked; then
wp_new_comment stores it, where preprocess_comment, the duplicate and
flood checks and pre_comment_approved have their say. A refusal is a
WP_Error whose data is the status the form answers with; none means a
blank page.

methods.name: submit
methods.doc: The stored comment, or the refusal the form answers with.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $form the posted fields, unslashed

methods.name: store
methods.doc: The comment checked for content and length, then stored through wp_new_comment. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: postRefusal
methods.doc: Why the post takes no comment, or null after pre_comment_on_post when it does.

methods.name: fieldRefusal
methods.doc: A signed-out commenter's name and email, when the site requires them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentPages
classes.doc:
Which page of a post's comments a comment falls on, and the link that
opens it there, as the reference works them out (probe comment-pages):
the page size from the arguments, the comments_per_page query variable
or the option (no pages at all when comments are not paged); a reply
takes its top-level comment's page while comments are threaded; a page
is the count of older top-level comments over the page size. The
default page loses its number when the oldest comments come first.

methods.name: pageOf
methods.doc:
The page a comment is on, through get_page_of_comment (handed the
arguments as settled and as given); a threaded reply answers with
its top-level comment's page. Null for a comment that is not there.

methods.name: linkPage
methods.doc:
The page a comment's link names (before get_comment_link): the one
asked for, the loop's, or the comment's own; '' for the default page
when the oldest comments come first.

methods.name: link
methods.doc: A post's link opened at a page of its comments, as pretty or plain links write it.

methods.name: olderQuery
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args the count of the top-level comments older than this one, through get_page_of_comment_query_args

params.name: args
params.doc: the count of the top-level comments older than this one, through get_page_of_comment_query_args

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQuery
classes.doc: The approval breakdown wp_count_comments reports (comment lists run through WP_Comment_Query and Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryRunner).

methods.name: breakdown
methods.doc: The counts wp_count_comments reports, for one post or the site. @return array<string, int>

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryRunner
classes.doc:
WP_Comment_Query as the reference runs it (probe wp-comment-query-sql):
the variables filled and handed to pre_get_comments, the meta query's
SQL, comments_pre_query (which may answer), the clauses (the date query
among them) handed to comments_clauses, the request, found_comments_query
when a limited query counts what it found, then the ids, the count, or
the comments through the_comments, threaded or flattened when asked.
Results are not cached between queries (the reference keeps them in the
object cache by last_changed).

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs the query, as WP_Comment_Query::get_comments() does: a count, ids, or comments.

methods.name: request
methods.doc:
The clauses through comments_clauses, kept on the query and written
as its request, and whether the request counts the rows it found.

methods.name: comments
methods.doc:
The comments for the ids in their order, each through get_comment(),
their posts loaded first when asked.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryWhere
classes.doc:
WP_Comment_Query's WHERE pieces and the posts join, in the reference's
order (probe wp-comment-query-sql): the approval statuses (with the
readers whose held comments show), the post, the id lists, the author's
email and url, karma, the types (notes left out unless asked for), the
parent (0 for a threaded or flat query that names none), the user, the
search, the post's own fields, the author lists, then the meta and date
queries.

constants.name: ID_LISTS
constants.value: array (   'comment__in' => '{c}.comment_ID IN',   'comment__not_in' => '{c}.comment_ID NOT IN',   'parent__in' => 'comment_parent IN',   'parent__not_in' => 'comment_parent NOT IN',   'post__in' => 'comment_post_ID IN',   'post__not_in' => 'comment_post_ID NOT IN', )

constants.name: AUTHOR_LISTS
constants.value: array (   'author__in' => 'user_id IN',   'author__not_in' => 'user_id NOT IN',   'post_author__in' => 'post_author IN',   'post_author__not_in' => 'post_author NOT IN', )

methods.name: pieces
methods.doc:
The WHERE pieces (joined with AND by the caller) and the posts join
('' when no post field is asked after).
shapes: @param array{join?: string, where?: string} $meta the meta query's SQL, when it has clauses

params.name: meta
params.doc: the meta query's SQL, when it has clauses

methods.name: approved
methods.doc:
The approval test: each status (all is approved or held, any is no
test), and the held comments of the readers named by email or user id.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The one post asked for. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: types
methods.doc:
The types in (comment stands for itself and the empty type, pings for
pingbacks and trackbacks) and out; notes stay out unless asked for,
and all asks for no test at all.

methods.name: parentAndUser
methods.doc: The parent (top level for a threaded or flat query naming none), then the user. @param array<string, mixed> $qv @return list<string>

methods.name: search
methods.doc: A LIKE test over the author's name, email, url, IP and the content. @param array<string, mixed> $qv @return list<string>

methods.name: posts
methods.doc:
The post's own fields, then the comment and post author lists, and
the posts join when a post column is tested.

methods.name: given
methods.doc: A value the query tests: anything but '', null and false.

methods.name: listOf
methods.doc: An array as given, or a comma (or space) separated string split. @return list<mixed>

methods.name: bare
methods.doc: A meta or date query's SQL without its leading AND.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentThreads
classes.doc:
A threaded or flat comment query's descendants as the reference fills
them (probe wp-comment-query-sql): one more comment query a level, with
the query's own variables but the level's parents, no parent, no limit
and no count; a threaded query hangs each reply under its parent, marks
every comment's children as known and keeps the top level by id, a flat
one lists the top level and then each level in its query's order.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: The query's top-level comments with their descendants filled in.

methods.name: flatten
methods.doc: A comment's children, then each one's own, depth first, as a list.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args get_children()'s arguments, handed down

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Connectors
classes.doc:
The connectors registry: the external services a site talks to (AI
providers, spam filters, cloud services) and how each authenticates.
Rows are normalised on the way in, the way the reference keeps them;
the facade class hands them back to plugin code.

constants.name: MaskCap
constants.doc: The reference stops adding bullets after sixteen, whatever the key's length.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers a connector, or the refusal.

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Forgets a connector; its row, or null.
shapes: @return array<string, mixed>|null the row that was registered, null when there was none

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every connector.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: One connector, or null.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether a connector is registered.

methods.name: registerDefaults
methods.doc:
The reference's three AI providers and Akismet. Activation is
checked through the caller's closure, so the plugin list is read
when asked.

methods.name: mask
methods.doc: Keys of four characters or fewer are shown whole; longer ones keep their last four behind at most sixteen bullets.

methods.name: keySource
methods.doc:
Where a key comes from, in the reference's precedence: the environment,
then a constant, then the stored option; empty values do not count.

extension is corrected (a.png holding a JPEG becomes a.jpg); anything
claiming to be such an image and not being one has no type; any other
type must match what the content is, plain text standing for a few text
types and an office or archive container for the document types; and
the type must be one the site allows.

A file a plugin hands to wp_handle_upload or wp_handle_sideload, taken in
the reference's order (probe upload-filters, contracts/runtime.md
"Uploads"): the action's prefilter, where a plugin sanitizes the file or
refuses it with an error; its overrides; the upload's own errors, an
empty file and, for a form upload, the form and the upload itself; the
type, from the file's content as much as its name
(wp_check_filetype_and_ext), refused unless the site allows it or the
user may upload anything; the uploads folder; a unique, clean name
(wp_unique_filename); pre_move_uploaded_file, where a plugin may move it
itself; the move; and wp_handle_upload over the result.

higher priority during a run takes part in that run, one added at the
current or a lower priority waits for the next; a callback removed
before its turn is skipped; the "all" hook sees every firing with the
hook name first and every argument regardless of its accepted count.

Options as plugin code sees them: PHP values, decoded from the stored
blob by the engine's own reader, cached for the request so a value written
and read again in one request keeps its PHP type (an int stays an int,
false stays false) exactly as the reference shows. A value holding an
object is kept as its stored text and decoded afresh on every read, as
the reference does: a plugin that changes the object it was handed and
saves it must find the stored copy still different, or its change is
never written.

constants.name: GUARDED
constants.doc:
The options the engine keeps for itself: the symbol-gate cache a plugin
could otherwise rewrite to pass its own gate, the recovery strikes, the
cron lock, and the sign-in throttle rows. The facade refuses to write
them; the engine writes them through this class directly.

Writes a new option. add_option has already decided it is new (its
value is still the default); a row that is there anyway is written

already held this value.

methods.doc:
Writes an option row whether or not one exists, as the reference does
for every add: two requests that both find a transient missing and
both add it must not fail on the unique name, so the second write lands
over the first. True when the row was inserted or changed, false when
the same value was already there.

The names of transients whose expiry has passed. The timeout row is the

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PackageDownload
classes.doc:
The publisher's say over its own download. Before fetching an update
package, the reference asks `upgrader_pre_download`: a plugin that hosts
itself answers there, and answering is how it proves the archive is the
one it published. Three answers, which are the reference's:

a file path  the publisher fetched and verified the package itself
a refusal    the publisher rejects this download, with its reason
nothing      nobody vouched for it

The engine asks the same question, and installs a package from outside
the wordpress.org directory only on the first answer. That is stricter
than the reference, which downloads whatever the offer names; here an
archive nobody vouched for is never unpacked over a plugin folder.

methods.name: verified
methods.doc:
The publisher's verified copy of the package, its refusal, or null
when nothing answered.

params.doc: what is being updated, as the reference passes it ('plugin' or 'theme')

The page-list menu a classic theme falls back to when no menu is
assigned to a location. Storefront's header is one of these, so its
markup is what the theme's CSS binds to.

Shapes captured from the reference: the optional home item carries no
class (the attribute is written but left empty), a page item carries
`page_item page-item-{id}` plus `current_page_item` for the page being
viewed, and the whole list is wrapped in the caller's before/after.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PlaceholderTrace
classes.doc:
Records every call into a generated placeholder while a site opts in by
having wp-content/minn-placeholder-trace.log on disk: one line per call
with the symbol, the plugin file that called it, and the request. The
log says which placeholders deserve behaviour; an absent file costs one
stat per request.

methods.name: hit
methods.doc: Logs a placeholder symbol being called, when the trace file exists.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Placeholders
classes.doc:
The printf placeholders plugin code hands wpdb::prepare, filled the way
the reference fills them: a bare %s is escaped and quoted; a numbered
(%1$s), padded (%5s) or precise (%.2f) one is formatted and escaped but
never quoted, so a plugin can name a table with it; %d and %f cast; %i
backticks an identifier; %% is a literal. Numbered placeholders address
the argument list directly while unnumbered ones count from the first
on their own, as vsprintf does. A placeholder with no argument behind it
empties the whole query, as the reference does.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: Fills a query's placeholders from the arguments; null when one has no argument.
shapes: @param callable(string): string $escape the connection's string escape

methods.name: quoted
methods.doc: A bare %s is the one placeholder the reference wraps in quotes.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginRemoval
classes.doc:
Deleting plugins as the reference's delete_plugins does it: each in turn
is uninstalled first when it can be (its uninstall.php, or the callback
it registered), then delete_plugin, its folder (or file) removed,
deleted_plugin, and its installed translations removed with it; the
updates offered for the deleted ones are forgotten. A plugin already
gone counts as deleted. Only what lies inside the plugins folder is
ever removed, and a symlinked folder is unlinked, never followed.

methods.doc: delete_plugins: true, false for none asked, or the error naming those left behind.
shapes: @param array<int, string> $plugins plugin files, relative to the plugins folder

params.name: plugins
params.doc: plugin files, relative to the plugins folder

methods.name: uninstall
methods.doc:
uninstall_plugin: pre_uninstall_plugin, then the plugin's uninstall.php
(WP_UNINSTALL_PLUGIN naming it) or the callback it registered (heard on
uninstall_<file>, with the plugin loaded); either is forgotten once run.

methods.doc: One plugin, uninstalled, removed and announced; whether it is gone. @param array<string, mixed> $translations

methods.name: removeFiles
methods.doc: The plugin's folder, or its file when it has none; false for anything outside the plugins folder.

methods.doc: A folder plugin's installed translations (.po, .mo, .l10n.php, script .json), by locale. @param array<string, mixed> $translations

methods.name: forgetUpdates
methods.doc: The updates offered for plugins that are gone. @param array<int, string> $deleted

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginUpdates
classes.doc:
The update offers the site's own plugins publish. A plugin that hosts
itself, or sells itself, is not in the wordpress.org directory and never
appears in the directory's answer: it publishes its offer by filtering
the update transient WordPress reads, which is the only place anyone
learns of it. The engine asks the same question of the runtime, in the
shape the reference asks it, so a self-hosted plugin is offered its
update here exactly as it would be on WordPress.

The transient carries `checked` (every installed plugin and its version),
and a plugin's updater returns early when that is empty, so the installed
versions are what make the question answerable.

methods.name: supplied
methods.doc:
What the site's plugins offer for themselves, empty when no runtime
is booted or nothing filters the transient.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $installed plugin file => installed version
@return array{plugins: array<string, array<string, mixed>>, no_update: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: fromFiltered
methods.doc:
The filtered transient as the state's two buckets: offers under
`plugins`, plugins that answered "current" under `no_update`, both
as arrays, and only for files this site actually has.
shapes: @return array{plugins: array<string, array<string, mixed>>, no_update: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: bucket
methods.doc: One bucket of the transient, normalised.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Plugins
classes.doc:
Loads the site's plugins into the runtime the way the reference does:
mu-plugins first, then active_plugins in stored order, each file
included once. A plugin loads only when the static symbol read finds
nothing the runtime lacks; otherwise it is reported and skipped so the
site keeps rendering. The lifecycle actions fire between the phases.

Minn Admin loads as code for its adapters (surfaces, licenses,
connectors, custom CSS, the plugin routes the engine has no
controller for), but the engine owns the shell, the front bar, the
sign-in flow, and maintenance: those hooks come off right after the
include so the two never print twice or disagree.
