methods.name: load
methods.doc:
Loads the active plugins as code and fires the boot hooks. Recovery
is armed for exactly this window: a failure here is one every
visitor would hit, so it may be recorded against its extension.

methods.name: loadTheme
methods.doc:
The theme's setup without the plugins: setup_theme, the theme's
functions.php, after_setup_theme, then wp_loaded. The probe runtime
ends its boot with this, so a theme's supports are what a request's
would be and a late declaration is judged as one; it skips init,
whose work the probes compare on their own.

methods.doc: The plugins that loaded.

shapes: @return array<string, array<string, mixed>> plugin file => why it did not load

methods.doc: True when the named plugin file is running as code this request.

methods.name: loadThemeFunctions
methods.doc:
The active theme's functions.php, child first then parent, between
setup_theme and after_setup_theme as the reference loads them. Each
file goes through the same symbol gate as a plugin folder and is
reported under "theme:{slug}" when it cannot load. Templates never
run as PHP; a block theme's functions.php only registers hooks.

methods.name: rememberThemeDomain
methods.doc:
An active theme's own text domain, named in its stylesheet header
(the slug when it names none), reads its folder ("Domain Path", or
"/languages") with files named by locale alone.

methods.name: registerRealpath
methods.doc:
A symlinked plugin folder resolves __FILE__ to its real location; the
map from that location back to the plugins directory keeps
plugin_basename() and plugins_url() truthful (the reference keeps the
same map).

methods.name: isolatedInclude
methods.doc: The include gets a clean local scope, as wp-settings.php gives every plugin file.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostData
classes.doc:
The loop's view of a post, as the reference's generate_postdata and
get_the_content give it (probes the-content, excerpt): the content split
into pages at <!--nextpage--> (the line breaks beside the marker go with
it) and handed to content_pagination, the page the query asks for, and
"more" when the main query shows a single post, a page or a feed; then
the content of that page, cut at the more tag with a more link (or run
on past it when "more" is set), the teaser dropped when asked or marked
<!--noteaser-->.

methods.doc:
id, authordata, currentday, currentmonth, page, pages, multipage,
more, numpages.

methods.doc:
The content get_the_content gives: the asked page, cut at the more tag
unless "more" is set.

What the reference's REST controllers tell plugins about a post they
write, for the engine's own controllers: the same actions in the same
order with the same arguments, fired through the facade's lifecycle
functions so the facade's own writes say the same (contracts/runtime.md
"Writes tell plugins"). Without a booted runtime every method does
nothing, so a write with no plugins loaded is exactly what it was.

A post keeps a category through every save, the default when it has

them, set_object_terms included), quietly without.

The terms a REST body names, set through wp_set_object_terms with

fields), core's own written directly without.

REST upload makes it: wp_generate_attachment_metadata over the stored
file (the sizes cut with the attachment's id, the metadata stored as
each one lands, so an optimiser hooked there finds it), then
wp_update_attachment_metadata. Only for the images the engine sizes,
as without plugins.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostLinks
classes.doc:
Post addresses as the reference's link functions build them (probe
permalinks): a post through pre_post_link (the structure) and post_link;
a page from get_page_uri through _get_page_link and page_link; an
attachment under its parent's address, or its own; a plugin's type by
its address pattern (the permastruct its rewrite registered) through
post_type_link, by its query var without one. Plain (?p=, ?page_id=,
?post_type=) unless its status is public, or private and readable by
whoever asks, or it is a sample: a draft, a scheduled or trashed post, a
revision, a private one a visitor asks for. "Leaving the name" keeps the slug as its placeholder
(%postname%, %pagename%, %{type}%) for an editor to fill in, and
get_sample_permalink shows a draft as it would be published.

What WP_Query does with its posts once it has them, as the reference does
it (probe wp-query-sql): a single post whose status is not public is
dropped unless the reader may see it (a draft its editor may preview, with
the_preview); sticky posts move to the front of the home listing's first
page, the ones it did not find fetched by a nested query; the_posts; and

WP_Query's post type and status clause as the reference writes it (probe
wp-query-sql). Statuses asked for by name: the type clause, then the
statuses (any, less those excluded from search; private kept apart when

replaces everything before it), authors, comment counts, mime types,

(probe revisions): only for a type that supports revisions and while
wp_revisions_to_keep allows any; compared with the latest revision
(wp_save_post_revision_check_for_changes, the revision fields with their
whitespace evened out, wp_save_post_revision_post_has_changed, whose
default also compares the revisioned meta); saved through wp_insert_post
and _wp_put_post_revision (whose default copies the revisioned meta);
then the oldest dropped past the limit, after
wp_save_post_revision_revisions_before_deletion.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostSave
classes.doc:
A REST save's columns through the filters the reference's save runs
before it writes, in its order (probe post-insert-filters,
contracts/runtime.md "Saves plugins can change"): rest_pre_insert_{type}
over the prepared post; every column through its db context
(pre_post_* and *_save_pre, where kses and the custom-CSS strip sit) on
slashed text; wp_insert_post_empty_content, which refuses a post with no
content, title or excerpt; wp_insert_post_parent; for a post that is live,
the slug, made again from the filtered title when the request gave none,
through pre_wp_unique_post_slug, the bad-slug check and
wp_unique_post_slug; and wp_insert_post_data over the row. What a filter
changes is written. Without plugins loaded the columns are as given.

A live post's slug through the reference's three filters:
pre_wp_unique_post_slug may settle it; otherwise it is made free in

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Recovery
classes.doc:
Recovery from a fatal in someone else's code. When a plugin or theme
kills the boot of a request, the file it died in names it; a second
such failure inside ten minutes records it as paused, and the next
request loads without it: the site comes back on its own instead of
staying down until a human reads the log. One failure is only noted:
a pause is a site-wide decision, and a single request can be a
crafted one. Failures after boot (a route, a template) never pause
anything; see Failure::armRecovery().

The paused list is stored where WordPress stores it, in the same shape
(`paused_plugins` keyed by plugin file, `paused_themes` by stylesheet,
each holding type, file, line and message), so a site that ejects back
to WordPress finds the pause it left with. The strikes live in the
engine's own `minn_recovery_strikes` option.

constants.name: WINDOW
constants.doc: Seconds inside which a second boot failure pauses the extension.

methods.name: blame
methods.doc:
The extension a file belongs to: a plugin as the active `folder/file.php`
whose folder holds the file (or the bare file of a single-file plugin),
a theme as its slug. The name is the one the loader checks against the
paused list, so a fatal deep inside a plugin's subfolders pauses the
plugin and not a folder nothing is called by. Anything outside the
plugin and theme folders belongs to nobody, and is never paused: a
fatal in the engine or in core is not a plugin's fault and pausing
something would not fix it. A symlinked plugin reports its real
location; the realpath map (real folder to the folder under plugins/)
brings it home first.
shapes: @param list<string>|null $active the active plugin files; read from the site when omitted

params.name: active
params.doc: the active plugin files; read from the site when omitted

methods.name: pause
methods.doc:
Records an extension as paused. Returns false when it was already
paused, so a caller can tell a fresh failure from a repeat and only
notify once.
shapes: @param array{type: int, file: string, line: int, message: string} $error

params.name: error
params.shape: array{type: int, file: string, line: int, message: string}

methods.name: strike
methods.doc:
Notes a boot failure against an extension. True when it is the
second inside the window, which is when the caller pauses it; the
first is only remembered. Strikes older than the window are dropped
as they are read, so the option never grows.

methods.name: pausedPlugins
methods.doc: The plugins recovery mode has paused.

methods.name: pausedThemes
methods.doc: The themes recovery mode has paused.

methods.name: resume
methods.doc: Lets an extension load again. Returns false when it was not paused.

methods.name: resumeAll
methods.doc: Lets everything load again. Returns how many were released.

methods.name: pluginFile
methods.doc:
The active plugin file a path under plugins/ belongs to: the entry in
the folder the path starts with, the bare file itself for a single-file
plugin, and the folder alone when no active entry claims it.
shapes: @param list<string> $parts the path segments under plugins/

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Runtime
classes.doc:
The WordPress runtime the engine offers plugin code: the procedural
facade under minn/wp-api/ plus the services it delegates to. One per
request; the facade reaches it through these statics.

constructor.doc:
The runtime for one request. Everything about the request itself
comes from the context; the fields below it are the same values,
kept as properties because plugin code reaches for them by name.

constants.name: CONTENT_DONE
constants.doc:
The the_content defaults the engine's own rendering has already done:
blocks, texturize, paragraphs, shortcodes, block hooks, and the image
attributes. What it has not (an attachment's own link, smilies, the
capital P, insecure home addresses) runs with the plugins' own
callbacks.

properties.name: db
properties.doc: The database door this request answers through.

properties.name: site
properties.doc: The site's options.

properties.name: request
properties.doc: The request being answered, absent on the command line.

properties.name: reader
properties.doc: Who reads this request; settled again (identify()) once plugins have said who the user is.

properties.name: capabilities
properties.doc: The capability engine.

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: The minn/ folder: the engine's own files.

properties.name: absPath
properties.doc: The site root with a trailing slash.

properties.name: version
properties.doc: The WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks.

properties.name: seams
properties.doc: The extension seams this request registered, once the front has loaded them.

properties.name: renderState
properties.doc: The counters and collected styles of everything rendered for this request.

properties.name: blockRenderer
properties.doc: The block renderer this request renders through.

methods.name: identify
methods.doc: The request's reader from now on: the user plugin code named through determine_current_user (Runtime\CurrentUser).

methods.name: useSeams
methods.doc: Holds the extension seams this request registered, so nothing static has to.

methods.name: seams
methods.doc: The extension seams, or null before the front has registered any (REST and the CLI never do).

methods.name: renderState
methods.doc: The render state for this request, made on first use: one set of counters for everything rendered.

methods.name: useRenderState
methods.doc: Makes a render state this request's, so a renderer that brought its own is the one the leaves read.

methods.name: blockRenderer
methods.doc: The block renderer for this request, made on first use over this request's own database door.

methods.name: boot
methods.doc:
Makes this request's runtime the one the facade sees and defines the
facade.

Deliberately does NOT start the facade's registries empty. A process
answering a second request would then have a fresh hook table that no
plugin can fill again: plugin files register their hooks as they are
included, and an include happens once per process. Until a plugin's
registrations can be replayed, a second boot inherits the first's
registries on purpose, which is why a worker runtime is not yet
something the engine claims (see contracts/runtime.md).

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The booted runtime; throws when there is none.

methods.name: booted
methods.doc: Whether the runtime is up.

methods.name: hooks
methods.doc: The hook registry.

methods.name: options
methods.doc: The options store.

methods.name: capture
methods.doc:
Runs an action and returns what it printed. Plugin callbacks may open
output buffers of their own during the action (a page post-processor
started in wp_head) or close one they think is theirs (the same plugin
in wp_footer); a sentinel buffer under the capture keeps the output
either way: extra buffers are flushed through their handlers into the
capture, and a capture closed early lands in the sentinel.

methods.name: contentFilter
methods.doc: Content the engine rendered itself, through the_content for everything else hooked there.

methods.name: cache
methods.doc: The object cache.

methods.name: textDomains
methods.doc: The text domains loaded for this request.

methods.name: locales

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ScriptPack
classes.doc:
The site-supplied script pack: the `wp-*` JavaScript packages the engine
does not reimplement, which a few plugins' front ends need (WooCommerce's
block cart and checkout are the reason it exists).

These packages are GPL, so the engine never ships them: the SITE installs
them into its own `wp-content`, the way it installs a language pack, and
the engine registers the handles only when they are actually there. A
site owner adding GPL files to a site that already runs GPL plugins is
not the engine distributing GPL; nothing under `minn/` changes.

The engine's own MIT packages under `minn/assets/wp` always win: the pack
fills the gaps around them, it does not replace them.

term-insert-filters, contracts/runtime.md "Terms plugins can change").
An insert asks pre_insert_term, refuses an empty name or a missing
parent, runs every field through its db filters (sanitize_term), refuses
a name the parent (or, for tags, the taxonomy) already has, makes the
slug unique, hands the row to wp_insert_term_data, writes it (a slug left
empty becomes the term's id), puts it in the taxonomy, lets a plugin
name a duplicate to keep instead, and tells plugins. An update merges
the stored term (slashed, so a backslash in it survives) under the
changes, runs the same filters, asks wp_update_term_parent (where a
parent that would put the term under itself becomes 0), and refuses a
slug a sibling holds.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ThemeSupports
classes.doc:
What a theme supports, as add_theme_support keeps it (probe rest-themes):
a bare feature is true, anything else its arguments. html5 lists add up
(repeats and all), post thumbnails stay on for every type once on, post
formats keep only real formats, the custom logo fills in its defaults at
once (flexible both ways when asked for bare), and the custom header and
background get theirs as WordPress finishes loading, a header with no
width or height made flexible that way. title-tag declared after loading
is refused. A block theme supports thumbnails, responsive embeds, editor
styles, HTML5 markup and feed links before its own setup runs.

registers) say how each is shown in REST: its schema, or the default
when the theme does not support it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ThemeSwitch
classes.doc:
Switching the theme as the reference does it, in two halves. The switch
(switch_theme): the leaving theme keeps its widgets and its menu
locations are remembered, the three theme options move, the switch is
recorded (theme_switched), the arriving theme's mods start with the
classic sidebars, only its mods stay autoloaded, then switch_theme. The
next load, on init (check_theme_switched): after_switch_theme with the
theme that left, whose defaults map the menu locations across
(_wp_menus_changed) and look the widgets over, then the rules flushed
and the record cleared. Deleting a theme fires delete_theme and
deleted_theme around its folder going, and forgets the update check.

that role (with a menu) to the arriving locations that name it.

user_register and the count, profile_update, delete_user and

new account (pre_user_nicename); the email and the URL; the nickname

everything went. A symlinked directory is unlinked, never followed:

reached through one would empty the real source.

methods.name: normalizeEntities
methods.doc:
Every "&" made a reference, in one pass: a known name or a code point
kses accepts stays one (decimal padded to three digits, hex with a
lower-case x), anything else becomes "&".

methods.name: lessThan
methods.doc:
A "<" that reaches the next "<" or the end without a ">" is text: the
run is escaped the way esc_html escapes it (quotes included).

methods.name: escapeHtml
methods.doc: Text escaped for HTML with references kept: invalid UTF-8 gives nothing, quotes become " and '.

methods.name: blockAttributes
methods.doc:
Block markup with every attribute key and string value passed through
the same filter, and the delimiters written back in their canonical
form ("--->" read as "-->"). Markup without a comment is left alone.

methods.name: filter
methods.doc:
The tag pass: each run from "<" to the next ">" (or the end) is a
comment, an inert bogus comment ("</" before a non-letter, "<!"
before a lower-case letter), or an element judged by the policy;
anything else in angle brackets goes. Text between keeps its
references, with stray ones escaped. Run alone (wp_kses_split), a
last "<" with no ">" still reads as a tag; inside sanitize() the
less-than pass has already escaped it.

methods.name: attributeList
methods.doc:
The attributes written inside a tag, read the way kses reads them: a
name, then "=" and a quoted or bare value, or no value at all; junk
between (stray quotes, "=", "/") is skipped; the first of two
same-named attributes wins. Null when a quoted value never closes,
which costs the tag every attribute.
shapes: @return array<string, array{name: string, value: ?string, whole: string}>|null

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Plain text: tags gone, whitespace collapsed, control characters dropped.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: A URL for a stored field: empty when its scheme is not one the reference allows.

methods.name: attributeUrl
methods.doc:
A URL inside markup: whatever stands before the first colon, once
every character reference and percent escape is decoded as deep as it
goes and the invisible characters are dropped, must be an allowed
scheme, or it is cut off and the rest is judged again. The reference
cuts "?q=a:b" to "b" and "javascript:alert(1)//http://" to "//" the
same way. A value with a good scheme is returned as given.

methods.name: pdfObject
methods.doc:
Whether a URL may be an object's data in post content: an http or https
URL on the uploads host and port, no credentials, query or fragment,
whose path ends in ".pdf".

methods.name: style
methods.doc: A style attribute's value with only the listed properties kept.

methods.name: styleHooks
methods.doc:
The runtime's say over style attributes: the property list
(safe_style_css) and each declaration (safecss_filter_attr_allow_css).
The facade sets these as it loads.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: One bracketed run as the tag pass keeps it, or nothing.

methods.name: htmlComment
methods.doc: A comment kept with its body as text: no "--" inside, an empty one dropped.

methods.name: deepDecode
methods.doc: A value with its references and percent escapes decoded until nothing changes, so no encoding hides a scheme.

methods.name: visible
methods.doc: The text with whitespace, control characters, no-break spaces, and replacement characters removed.

methods.name: normalizeText
methods.doc:
Text between tags as the reference stores it: valid references stay
references (decimal ones padded to three digits), invalid ones and
stray ampersands become "&", and a closing bracket is escaped.

methods.name: normalizeAttribute
methods.doc:
An attribute value as the reference stores it: valid references become
their characters, except that the five markup characters stay escaped
(an apostrophe as '); invalid references and stray ampersands
become "&"; raw quotes are escaped.

methods.name: named
methods.doc: What a named reference stands for, or null when the name is not one.

methods.name: codePoint
methods.doc: A numeric reference's code point, or null when it names no character the reference accepts (NUL, controls, surrogates, beyond Unicode).

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc:
The attributes the policy allows, in the order written: a value must
meet its rules, a URI keeps only an allowed scheme, srcset and style are
judged on their own terms. A tag that loses a required attribute keeps
none at all.

methods.name: rendered
methods.doc: One allowed attribute as stored, or null when its value is judged away entirely.

methods.name: srcset
methods.doc: Every candidate must be an absolute URL with a safe scheme, or the attribute goes.

methods.name: css
methods.doc:
The style attribute's declarations kept as written, as the reference
keeps them: a listed property (the list through safe_style_css when
the runtime hooks it; --* lets custom properties through), a value
with no expression, behavior, script, data: or escape, url() only on
image properties; each asked through safecss_filter_attr_allow_css.

methods.name: safeValue
methods.doc: No expression, behavior, script, data: or escape anywhere; url() only on image properties, without parentheses around it.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesEntities
classes.doc:
The named references kses keeps as written: the list captured from the
reference (data/kses.json) plus the five XML ones. Any other name is
stored as "&name;".

methods.name: known
methods.doc: Whether "&name;" is a reference kses leaves alone.

methods.name: allowlist
methods.doc: An allowlist the reference ships, by context ("post" or "data").

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesPolicy
classes.doc:
What one kses pass allows: the tags, each tag's attributes (allowed
plainly or with value rules), whether a tag takes data- attributes,
which attributes hold URIs, and the schemes those URIs may use.

shapes: @param array<string, array<string, mixed>> $tags tag => attribute => true, or a list of value rules
@param array<string, list<string>> $prefixes tag => attribute-name prefixes it accepts (only "data-")

params.name: tags
params.doc: tag => attribute => true, or a list of value rules

methods.name: post
methods.doc: Post content from an author without unfiltered_html: the reference's post allowlist as captured.

methods.name: comment
methods.doc: Comments, profiles and term descriptions: only the attributes each tag lists, nothing global.

methods.name: fromAllowlist
methods.doc:
A caller's own allowlist taken literally: a listed attribute is allowed
whatever it maps to (false included, as the reference only asks whether
the name is there), an array carries value rules, and "data-*" lets the
tag take any data- name. Nothing else is implied.

methods.name: allowsTag
methods.doc: Whether the tag may appear at all.

methods.name: rules
methods.doc:
The rules an attribute carries on a tag: an empty list when it is
allowed plainly, null when it is not allowed.

methods.name: required
methods.doc: The attributes a tag must keep: lose one and the tag keeps none.

methods.name: holdsUri
methods.doc: Whether the attribute holds a URI whose scheme must be judged.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesValues
classes.doc:
The value rules an allowlist attribute may carry, as the reference judges
them: lengths count bytes, bounds need a whole number (up to six digits,
up to six spaces either side), "valueless" compares the attribute's form,
"values" compares without case, and a callback decides for itself. A rule
the reference does not know passes. Where the reference fatals (a values
rule that is not a list, a callback that does not exist) the value fails.

methods.name: satisfies
methods.doc:
Whether a value meets every rule its attribute carries; "required" is
the tag's concern, so it is skipped here.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: One rule against one value; $valueless is "y" for a bare attribute and "n" for one with a value.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Lists
classes.doc:
List shaping behind the facade's array utilities: the multi-field sort
wp_list_sort() promises (loose comparison per field, first difference
wins) and the row-shape conversions wpdb hands back for its OBJECT_K /
ARRAY_A / ARRAY_N output formats.

methods.name: sort
methods.doc: Items sorted by several fields, each ascending or descending.

methods.name: shapeRows
methods.doc:
Rows of stdClass shaped for a wpdb output format: keyed by their first
column (first row wins a duplicate key), associative, or numeric.

methods.name: descendants
methods.signature: descendants(array $items, int $rootId, callable $id, callable $parent, array $visited = array ( )): array
methods.doc:
Every descendant of one root in a flat parent-linked list, preorder
(a child ahead of its own children), the shape _get_term_children and
get_page_children walk. Visited ids guard against a parent cycle.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Locale
classes.doc:
The locale's calendar and number vocabulary as data: the names a site
prints for weekdays, months and meridiems, and how it separates
thousands and decimals.

The names are English here because the engine carries no core
translations yet; the facade runs each one through the translation
filters on the way out, so a catalogue can answer for them later
without this class changing.

methods.name: weekdayInitial
methods.doc: A weekday's one-letter form.

methods.name: abbreviation
methods.doc: A weekday's or month's three-letter form; May is already three letters.

methods.name: monthKey
methods.doc: Months are keyed by their zero-padded number, both ways round.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Markers
classes.doc:
The BEGIN/END marker blocks insert_with_markers() maintains in files like
.htaccess: the captured shape keeps everything outside the markers,
replaces the block inside them, and writes the reference's four-line
do-not-edit preamble ahead of the inserted lines.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Replaces the lines between a marker's begin and end comments in a file.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
The lines between a marker's begin and end comments, every block of it
in order. A line opens or closes a block when it contains the comment
anywhere (case-sensitive); lines that start with "#" are left out, so
the preamble and any nested markers are, while indented comments stay.
Lines split on "\n" only, and a block left open at the end of the file
keeps the empty line after its final newline.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Paths
classes.doc: File-system path and permission spellings.

methods.name: translationDir
methods.doc:
The trailing-slashed directory holding a text domain's {domain}-{locale}.mo:
a custom path first, then the language dir's plugins and themes folders,
then the dir itself for the default domain; false when none has the file.

methods.name: normalize
methods.doc: Forward slashes only, runs collapsed, a stream wrapper kept, a Windows drive letter upper-cased.

methods.name: symbolicMode
methods.doc: The `ls -l` spelling of a mode: type letter, then rwx for owner, group and world with the setuid, setgid and sticky bits folded in.

classes.name: Minn\Support\ScriptTag
classes.doc:
Script elements as the reference builds them (probe script-tags): the
attributes sorted by name, a src or href through esc_url and every other
value escaped (true or null printed bare, false left out); inline code
between newlines, with any "<script" or "</script" that would end or
open an element written with its "s" as a \u escape. Only JavaScript and
JSON can carry that escape: a script of another type whose code holds
such a sequence is not printed at all.

constants.name: ESCAPABLE
constants.doc: The script types inline code is JavaScript or JSON in (lowercase, trimmed; no type at all counts as JavaScript).

constants.name: TAG
constants.doc: A sequence that would open or close a script element inside one.

methods.name: element
methods.doc: The empty element for a script file.

methods.name: inline
methods.doc:
The element for inline code (already between its newlines), or '' when
its type cannot hold the code safely.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: The attributes as markup, each with its leading space.

classes.name: Minn\Support\SearchReplace
classes.doc:
String replace that walks serialized-PHP arrays of scalars without
unserialize, so a domain change in an option blob keeps its lengths.

methods.name: in
methods.doc: A value with one string replaced, and how many times.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: int} replacement and how many times $old occurred

classes.name: Minn\Support\Serialized
classes.doc:
Tolerant readers for the serialized-PHP blobs WordPress stores. Nothing
here executes the blob; each reader scans for the one shape it needs.

constants.name: INVALID
constants.doc: Returned by decode() when the blob is not a serialized value the reader accepts.

properties.name: open
properties.doc: The objects being encoded right now, outermost first, so a loop is seen.

methods.name: stringList
methods.doc: The string values of a serialized string list.

methods.name: serializeStringList
methods.doc: A flat string list in the stored form.

methods.name: field
methods.doc: The first "field";value pair inside a blob: string, int, or float value as a string.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc:
A serialized scalar or array as PHP data, parsed by this reader:
strings, integers, floats, booleans, null, and arrays of those. An
object record becomes a stdClass of its properties, or whatever the
reviver makes of the class name and those properties; nothing here
instantiates anything itself. A blob with trailing bytes or a
malformed shape is INVALID.

methods.name: storedClass
methods.doc: The class an object was stored as, when it came back as a stdClass of its properties.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
PHP's serialize() for the values decode() accepts: null, bool, int,
float, string, arrays of those, and objects written as their class.

methods.name: intList
methods.doc: The integer values of a serialized list such as sticky_posts.

methods.name: readObject
methods.doc:
An object record. The properties land on a plain stdClass; only the
reviver may turn that into something else, and only for a class it
knows. A record it leaves alone keeps its class name and its stored
property names (visibility markers, numbered parts, a private name a
parent class shares) on the side, so encode() writes it back as it
was read instead of as a stdClass.

methods.name: encodeRecord
methods.doc:
A stdClass, or a record read back as one, in PHP's own form: the
stored class name and property names where there are some, property
names as strings otherwise, each value through encode() so a record
nested inside keeps its class too.
shapes: @param array{class: string, keys: array<string, int|string>, hidden: list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}>} $record

params.name: record
params.shape: array{class: string, keys: array<string, int|string>, hidden: list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}>}

methods.name: encodeWrapper
methods.doc: PHP's array wrappers in their own form (flags, storage, members, iterator class), the storage through encode().

methods.name: encodeObject
methods.doc:
Plugin code stores objects (maybe_serialize's contract). A record read
back as a stdClass is written under the class it was stored as; a
stdClass and PHP's array wrappers are written here so a record inside
them keeps its class too; any other object goes through PHP's own
serializer, which runs nothing and matches the reference byte for
byte. Only reading is the hazard, and reads stay on decode().

classes.name: Minn\Support\Time
classes.doc: Human-scale spans: a number of seconds as the largest whole unit it fills, rounded, never below one.

methods.name: span
methods.doc: A number of seconds as its largest whole unit and count.
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: string} count and unit name

classes.name: Minn\Support\Url
classes.doc:
URL shaping the escaping and query helpers share: the character cleanup
esc_url applies, bracket encoding outside the authority, and query
argument merging. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: Spaces encoded, stray characters dropped, ";//" healed, a bare host given http; '' when nothing survives.

methods.name: encodeBrackets
methods.doc: Square brackets after the authority are percent-encoded; the authority itself is left alone. @param array<string, mixed> $parsed

methods.name: withQuery
methods.doc:
The URI with query arguments merged in (false removes one), the
fragment kept, a bare query string treated as such; a URI that is
only a query (or nothing) keeps its leading question mark.
shapes: @param Closure(array): array $encode encodes the existing arguments the way the reference does
@param Closure(array): string $build builds the query string

params.name: encode
params.doc: encodes the existing arguments the way the reference does

methods.name: validateForHttp
methods.doc:
The checks wp_http_validate_url makes on a URL whose protocol already
passed: an http(s) scheme, a host without credentials or a colon, no
private address unless it is this site or allowed, only the safe
ports (80, 443 and 8080 unless the caller's list says otherwise; the
site's own always). Returns the URL, or null when refused.
shapes: @param Closure(string, string): bool $externalAllowed whether a private host may be fetched anyway
@param (Closure(list<int>, string, string): array)|null $safePorts the port list for a URL that names a port

params.name: externalAllowed
params.doc: whether a private host may be fetched anyway

params.name: safePorts
params.doc: the port list for a URL that names a port

methods.name: buildQuery
methods.doc: A query string in the reference's spelling (probe query-args): keys and values as given, nested keys as `a%5Bb%5D`, null left out, booleans as 0/1.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: parse_url that also accepts scheme-relative and path-only URLs; a single component by its PHP_URL_* constant.

methods.name: withScheme
methods.doc: The URL under a scheme, or scheme-and-host stripped for 'relative'; a protocol-relative URL is read as http first.

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc:
A redirect target the site may send a browser to: http(s) only, no
credentials, and a host the caller allows (local paths always pass).
shapes: @param Closure(string): list<string> $allowedHosts the hosts allowed for the target's host

params.name: allowedHosts
params.doc: the hosts allowed for the target's host

classes.name: Minn\Support\Utf8
classes.doc:
Whether bytes are well-formed UTF-8 as the reference judges them: overlong
forms, surrogates, code points past U+10FFFF, stray continuation bytes and
truncated sequences fail; noncharacters, NUL and a byte order mark pass.

methods.name: isValid
methods.doc: True for well-formed UTF-8, including the empty string.

classes.name: Minn\Support\WebServer
classes.doc: What the SERVER_SOFTWARE string says about the web server in front of the site.

methods.name: isApache
methods.doc: Whether the server speaks Apache's module and .htaccess conventions: Apache itself, or LiteSpeed.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ArchiveTitle
classes.doc:
The label and name an archive titles itself with: `Category:` around the
term, `Author:` around the display name, the date formatted for its
granularity. One source of truth for the block path's query-title and
the classic path's get_the_archive_title(), which used to compute the
same labels separately. Search and post-type archives stay with their
callers: their captured shapes differ between the two paths.

methods.name: parts
methods.doc: The archive title's prefix and title for a resolution.
shapes: @return array{string, string} the label (no colon) and the escaped bare name; both empty when the view has none

params.name: dateFormat
params.doc: the site's date_format option, for day archives

methods.name: compose
methods.doc: The reference's prefixed shape: `Category: Uncategorized`.

methods.name: taxonomyLabel
methods.doc: The singular label a plugin registered for its taxonomy, for the archive title prefix.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\BodyClasses
classes.doc:
The body-class list a classic theme's body_class() starts from, in the
reference's order: the query tokens (with the singular and template
tokens spliced in front of the type token), logged-in, the embed and
theme tokens, with the numbered paging tokens re-seated after the embed
token. The body_class filter runs over this list in the facade.

methods.name: classic
methods.doc: The body classes a classic theme's page carries.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\BodyFacts
classes.doc:
The facts about a page that decide the body classes a classic theme's
page carries beyond the view tokens: privacy policy page, a signed-in
reader, a custom logo, responsive embeds, and the Minn bar.

constructor.signature: __construct(bool $privacyPage = false, bool $loggedIn = false, bool $customLogo = false, bool $embedResponsive = true, bool $bar = false)

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicContent
classes.doc:
What a classic theme's the_content() prints: the engine's block pipeline
(render, password gate, the more-tag teaser in listings), the cached
embeds, then the runtime's shortcodes and the_content filters so plugin
code sees the same hook order the reference runs.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: A post's content as the classic loop prints it, with the more link.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active classic theme: the reference's PHP template
loader. The main query stands, template_redirect fires, the hierarchy
picks a PHP file, template_include filters it, and load_template() runs
it as the response body. The theme prints its own document; the engine
contributes the reference's wp_head defaults (title tag, robots, feed
links, REST and oEmbed discovery, canonical, site icon) as hooks the
theme's wp_head() call fires.

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme $theme, ?Minn\Theme\Theme $styleTheme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self
methods.doc: A classic renderer over the database door.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The page for a resolution through the theme's PHP templates.

methods.name: themeClasses
methods.doc: The body-class tokens before plugins filter them (get_body_class filters them). @return list<string>

methods.name: template
methods.doc: The reference's loader order: the first true conditional whose template exists wins, index.php last.

methods.name: registerHead
methods.doc: The piece only the renderer holds: the engine stylesheets. The head defaults registered at setup_theme.

methods.name: registerStyles
methods.doc: The engine's block stylesheet, and the theme.json presets when the theme ships one, where the reference prints its block-library and global styles.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme
classes.doc:
The active classic (PHP-template) theme on disk. A theme is classic when
it ships no block template index; its templates are PHP files the engine
dispatches through the reference's hierarchy and runs via load_template().
The theme's own functions.php loads through the runtime's symbol gate.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The active classic theme, or null under a block theme.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\EmbedRenderer
classes.doc:
A post's embed page (its /embed/ address, or ?embed= on it), the card
another site's iframe shows, as the reference prints it: the main query
stood with the embed asked for, then the embed template (the theme's
own embed-{type}.php or embed.php, else the engine's theme-compat one)
through template_include, with embed_head, embed_content,
embed_content_meta and embed_footer. An address that embeds nothing
gets the 404 card.

methods.name: asked
methods.doc: Whether a request for this resolution asks for its embed page.

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
The embed page, under the status the request's main query settled on;
the body classes the theme's page would carry (the Minn bar's aside).

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FeedHeaders
classes.doc:
The headers a feed is sent with, as the reference's send_headers sends
them (suite feed-hooks): the feed type's content type, and when the site
last changed (its posts, and its comments too for a comments feed) as
Last-Modified with an ETag over it; a reader whose copy carries that
date or tag is told the copy is current.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The headers, and whether the reader's copy is current.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the request's query variables

methods.name: carriesComments
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars whether the feed's last change counts the comments: a comments feed, or a single post's

params.name: vars
params.doc: whether the feed's last change counts the comments: a comments feed, or a single post's

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Folder
classes.doc: A theme folder read from disk: its style.css headers, which folder its templates come from, its screenshot, whether it is a block theme.

shapes: @param array<string, string> $headers keyed by the caller's labels

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A theme folder with its style.css headers.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $labels key => the style.css header label
@param Closure(string, array<string, string>): array<string, string>|null $reader the header reader (the facade's, so header filters apply); the engine's own by default

params.name: reader
params.doc: the header reader (the facade's, so header filters apply); the engine's own by default

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: The folder's path.

methods.name: screenshot
methods.doc: The screenshot file name, or null when the theme has none.

methods.name: isBlockTheme
methods.doc: Whether any of the folders ships a block template index.
shapes: @param list<string> $dirs the stylesheet and template directories

methods.name: filePath
methods.doc: The first of the stylesheet and template directories that holds the file, or the template directory's path.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FrontLifecycle
classes.doc:
WordPress's front-end request steps around the main query, as WP::main
runs them (front lifecycle trace): parse the request (do_parse_request
may take it over; query_vars names the public variables, a plugin's own
read from the query string; request filters the result; parse_request
follows), the main query, the 404 decision (pre_handle_404 first), the
globals, and the headers (wp_headers, the status, send_headers). The
engine has already resolved the URL; these steps tell plugins about it
in the reference's order and let them change what the query asks.

methods.name: parseRequest
methods.doc:
Parses the request: false when a plugin's do_parse_request took the
parse over (the main query then does not run).
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the variables the engine resolved
@param array<string, mixed> $given the query string and form, where a plugin's own variables are read
@param (\Closure(list<string>): array<string, mixed>)|null $parse the reference's parse vars for the public vars, when the request is known

params.name: given
params.doc: the query string and form, where a plugin's own variables are read

params.name: parse
params.doc: the reference's parse vars for the public vars, when the request is known

methods.name: handle404
methods.doc:
The 404 decision: a plugin's pre_handle_404 may make it; otherwise a
request the engine could not resolve is a 404 (the query says so, the
status and no-cache headers follow), as is a page past the end of a
listing (the query found nothing on it); anything else is a 200.

methods.name: sendHeaders
methods.doc:
The headers the reference sends for the request: no caching for a
signed-in reader or a 404, the content type, a pingback address for a
single post that takes pings; then wp_headers, the status an error
variable names, and send_headers.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\GlobalStyles
classes.doc:
theme.json to CSS. Presets become custom properties on :root and their
has-* utility classes; settings.layout sizes, root styles, elements, and
per-block styles become rules; the containers, galleries, and style
variations the page actually rendered get their own stylesheets. The
layout rules themselves (flow, constrained, flex, grid, alignments) are
the engine's own, written to the same class hooks.

params.name: user
params.doc: the site editor's saved global styles, layered over the theme

constants.name: ELEMENT_SELECTORS
constants.value: array (   'link' => 'a:where(:not(.wp-element-button))',   'heading' => 'h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6',   'h1' => 'h1',   'h2' => 'h2',   'h3' => 'h3',   'h4' => 'h4',   'h5' => 'h5',   'h6' => 'h6',   'button' => '.wp-element-button, .wp-block-button__link',   'caption' => '.wp-element-caption, .wp-block-audio figcaption, .wp-block-embed figcaption, .wp-block-gallery figcaption, .wp-block-image figcaption, .wp-block-table figcaption, .wp-block-video figcaption',   'cite' => 'cite', )
constants.doc:
Element selectors in the order the reference prints them, whatever
order theme.json or the saved styles list them in: the heading group
lands before the individual levels, so an h1 line-height beats the
group's. Themes list h1..h6 before heading and would otherwise win.

constants.name: BLOCK_SELECTORS
constants.doc: Blocks whose metadata names a root selector other than .wp-block-{slug}.

constants.name: STYLESHEET_LESS
constants.doc:
The reference prints a core block's theme.json styles only when the
page rendered the block with output (a generated excerpt counts), and
attaches them to the block's own stylesheet; these core blocks have
none, so their styles never reach a page. A block from outside core
has no such stylesheet to wait for, so its styles always print.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: The theme.json (plus site-editor) styles node, under the engine's own defaults.

methods.name: resolvedStyles
methods.doc:
The same node with every `var:preset|…` token resolved to the custom
property it names, which is the shape a caller reading the styles as
data expects (the CSS writer resolves them on the way out instead).

methods.name: css
methods.doc: The global stylesheet from theme.json and the user's styles, as a page prints it: only the core blocks it rendered.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc:
The stylesheet wp_get_global_stylesheet answers (probe editor-styles),
by type: the custom properties, the styles (every block's, rendered or
not), the preset classes; in that order.

methods.name: fontFaces
methods.doc:
The @font-face rules for every family that declares font files, as
the reference prints them in its own style element: family (quoted
when it has a space), style, weight, display, then the sources with
file:./ resolved against the theme that carries the file and the
format named from the extension. Families without files print
nothing.

methods.name: parts
shapes: @return array{variables: string, base: string, presets: string, blocks: array<string, mixed>}

methods.name: structuralRules
methods.doc: The engine's own layout rules on the reference's class hooks; the global-padding rules exist only under root-padding-aware alignments.

methods.name: gapRules
methods.doc: The block-gap rules for a layout scope: "" for the root, or a block's -is-layout- prefix.

methods.name: rootStyles
methods.doc:
Root styles land on body. With root-padding-aware alignments the root
padding is NOT applied to body; it becomes the custom properties the
has-global-padding rules read.

methods.name: blockCustomProperties
methods.doc: Each block's own settings.custom as custom properties on the block's root selector. @param array<string, mixed> $blocks

methods.name: blockStyles
methods.doc:
A block's rules: its root rule, its layout gap rules, then a rule for
each feature its metadata gives a selector of its own (the avatar's
border on its image), its own CSS and its elements (probe
editor-styles).

methods.name: selectorsOf
methods.doc: A core block's selectors from its metadata (data/blocks.json). @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: byFeature
methods.doc:
A block's styles split between its root selector and the features (or
a feature's single properties) its metadata selects elsewhere.
shapes: @return array{0: array<string, mixed>, 1: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: scopedCss
methods.doc:
A block's own CSS under its selector (probe editor-styles), split at
each ampersand: a part with no rule applies to the block itself; a
nested selector that starts with a space is scoped, every comma part
after the block's selector; any other is appended to it; a pseudo
element moves to the end, outside :where().

methods.name: scope
methods.doc: Every comma part of a selector list after every part of the scope.

methods.name: append
methods.doc: Text appended to every comma part of a selector list.

methods.name: variationStyles
methods.doc: Style variations the page rendered, one rule set per numbered instance.

methods.name: declarations
methods.doc:
theme.json style properties to declarations: color, typography, spacing,
border, shadow, dimensions, outline.

methods.name: ordered
methods.doc:
The reference prints declarations in its own fixed property order:
alphabetical, except that the sides of a margin or padding run
top, right, bottom, left.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\HeadLinks
classes.doc:
The links the reference puts in every head: the site and comments
feeds (plus the archive's own feed), the REST discovery link, the
JSON alternate for the queried object, and the site icon set. The
block path prints them as one run; the classic path prints the same
pieces from the reference's wp_head hooks.

methods.name: engineStylesheet
methods.doc: The link to the engine's own block stylesheet.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every head link for a resolution.

methods.name: feedLinks
methods.doc: The site and comments feed links.

methods.name: siteFeeds
methods.doc:
The site's two feed links as feed_links prints them: the posts feed
and the comments feed (each unless its feed_links_show_* filter says
no), titled with the caller's separator and words.

methods.name: extraFeedLink
methods.doc: The feed link a single or an archive adds.

methods.name: restLink
methods.doc: No trailing newline: the reference prints the JSON alternate and the RSD link on the same physical line.

methods.name: jsonAlternate
methods.doc: The wp/v2 alternate link for the resolution.

methods.name: rsdLink
methods.doc: The RSD link.

methods.name: shortlink
methods.doc: Singular views only; posts and pages alike shortlink as ?p={id}, in the reference's single quotes.

methods.name: icons
methods.doc: The site icon links: the 32 and 192 pixel icons, the Apple touch icon, and the tile image.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Hierarchy
classes.doc:
The classic template hierarchy: the candidate file names each template
type tries, most specific first, as the reference resolves them. The
facade's get_{type}_template() functions feed these to get_query_template(),
which locates the first candidate the theme (child, then parent) ships.

methods.name: frontPage
methods.doc: The front page templates.

methods.name: home
methods.doc: The home templates.

methods.name: privacyPolicy
methods.doc: The privacy policy templates.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: The page templates, custom first.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: The single templates, custom first.

methods.name: attachment
methods.doc: The attachment templates by mime type.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: The term archive templates.

methods.name: author
methods.doc: The author archive templates.

methods.name: archive
methods.doc: The post type archive templates.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge
classes.doc:
Stands the main query for a themed page and runs the front-end steps
around it as WP::main does (FrontLifecycle): the request parsed, the main
query through WP_Query (so pre_get_posts and every posts_* filter shape
it), the 404 decision, the globals, the headers, then "wp" and
template_redirect. A listing's posts are the query's; a single post the
query does not find (a preview, a draft its author reads) is the one the
engine resolved. Without the runtime, the engine's own listing.

methods.name: stand
methods.doc:
The page of posts a resolution shows, through the runtime's main query
when it is up; the variables a request adds of its own (a feed's) win.

methods.name: perPage
methods.doc: Posts per page.

methods.name: vars
methods.doc:
The variables the reference's request parse would arrive at: the
resolution's, the posts page by its id, and an unresolved pretty path
as the page path it was taken for.

methods.name: queried
methods.doc:
The main query for these variables: a listing is its posts; any other
page stands on the post the engine resolved when the query has none.

methods.name: seeded
methods.doc: The engine's own page seeded into the query globals, when no query ran or it found nothing to stand on. @param array<string, mixed> $vars

methods.name: objectTypes
shapes: @return list<string> the post types a plugin's taxonomy attaches to

classes.name: Minn\Theme\NotModified
classes.doc:
Raised once a reader's copy of a feed has been found current and the
headers that say so are sent: the reference stops the request there, so
the engine answers with nothing more.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PageRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active block theme: the template the resolution
maps to, rendered against the main query, inside the document shell the
reference emits (skip link, wp-site-blocks, the skip-link target on the
first main element).

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Theme\Templates $templates, Minn\Blocks\Renderer $renderer, Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge $bridge, Minn\Theme\HeadLinks $headLinks, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL)

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self
methods.doc: A page renderer over the database door.

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc:
The reference's body-class tokens: the singular and template tokens
sit in front of the type token ("page", "single"), the custom-logo
and embed tokens follow the core set, the paging tokens come after
those, and the theme (and child theme) tokens close the list; then
the body_class filter.

methods.name: themeClasses
methods.doc: The body-class tokens before plugins filter them (bodyClasses()). @return list<string>

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The page for a resolution, or null when the theme has no template for it.

methods.name: pluginTemplate
methods.doc:
The reference filters template_include under block themes too (the
canvas is the incoming value); a plugin swapping in its own PHP file
takes the whole response over, the CaptainCore Manager shape.

methods.name: skipLinkTarget
methods.doc:
The skip link points at the first <main>: at its own id when the
template gave it one, otherwise at the id the reference injects.
shapes: @return array{string, string} the body, the target id

methods.name: documentTitle
methods.doc: The title after the extensions and, with the runtime up, the reference's document_title filters.

methods.name: head
methods.doc:
The head: title, the discovery links, the engine's stylesheets (inside
wp_head when the runtime is up, where the reference prints a theme's,
after plugin styles), then the extension head (after the stylesheets
either way, as the seam contract says), the fonts, the bar's own.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PatternText
classes.doc:
Block-theme patterns are PHP files whose only code is a handful of
echo-and-escape calls around literal strings. The engine never executes
them: it interprets that small text grammar (string literals, "."
concatenation, the i18n and escaping wrappers, the theme URI helper, and
printf with %s) and leaves anything else out. The header comment block
is dropped, and every byte outside the PHP tags is kept as-is.

constants.name: PASSTHROUGH
constants.doc: Wrappers whose value is their first argument, unchanged.

constants.name: ESCAPING
constants.doc: Wrappers whose value is their first argument with HTML special characters encoded.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: A pattern file's HTML with its PHP interpreted, never executed.

methods.name: expression
methods.doc: A concatenation of terms.

methods.name: escape
methods.doc: Special characters encoded once; entities already present are kept.

methods.name: skipSpace
methods.doc: Whitespace and comments, anywhere a token may follow.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Printed
classes.doc:
Raised once a WordPress handler has printed a whole response (a sitemap,
a stylesheet) or sent a redirect, where the reference exits: the request
ends there and the engine answers with what was printed.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\StylePresets
classes.doc:
The preset side of theme.json: the colour, gradient, font-size,
font-family, spacing, and shadow lists a theme declares over core's
own, as the custom properties on :root and the has-* utility classes
the reference prints for them. Pure: settings in, CSS fragments out.

methods.name: presets
methods.doc: Every preset list the theme declares, over core's own, keyed by kind.

methods.name: presetList
methods.doc:
A preset list as theme.json writes it is a plain list; as the site
editor saves it, it is keyed by origin (default, theme, custom). The
reference prints the origins in that order, so the two shapes flatten
to one list here.

methods.name: fontFamilies
methods.doc: The font family presets in the settings.

methods.name: presetProperties
methods.doc: The presets as custom properties for :root.

methods.name: customProperties
methods.doc:
A settings.custom tree as custom properties: --wp--custom-- and the path
to each value, every key in kebab case, lists by index; empty values
are left out.

methods.name: presetClasses
methods.doc: The has-* utility classes the presets give every colour, gradient, font size, and font family.

methods.name: defaultSlugsFirst
methods.doc:
A theme size that reuses one of core's slugs prints in core's position;
the theme's own slugs follow.

methods.name: spacingPresets
methods.doc:
The default spacing scale (20 to 80) is always present, whatever
defaultSpacingSizes says; a theme size with the same slug replaces the
default in place, and the theme's other sizes follow the scale.

methods.name: fluidFontSize
methods.doc:
A font size with fluid bounds becomes clamp(min, min + ((1vw - v) * f),
max) scaled between a 320px viewport and the theme's wide size, which
is how the reference arrives at 0.196 for a 1rem to 1.125rem size on a
1340px wide layout. A plain size stays as written.

methods.name: fontFormat
methods.doc: The format() a font source is declared with, from its file extension.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\StyleSettings
classes.doc:
The settings and styles nodes as wp/v2/global-styles reports them:
preset lists keyed by the origin that declared them, appearanceTools
spelled out as the flags it stands for, and var:preset tokens resolved
to the custom properties they name. Pure: a node in, a node out.

constants.name: PRESET_PATHS
constants.value: array (   0 =>    array (     0 => 'color',     1 => 'palette',   ),   1 =>    array (     0 => 'color',     1 => 'gradients',   ),   2 =>    array (     0 => 'color',     1 => 'duotone',   ),   3 =>    array (     0 => 'typography',     1 => 'fontSizes',   ),   4 =>    array (     0 => 'typography',     1 => 'fontFamilies',   ),   5 =>    array (     0 => 'spacing',     1 => 'spacingSizes',   ),   6 =>    array (     0 => 'shadow',     1 => 'presets',   ),   7 =>    array (     0 => 'dimensions',     1 => 'aspectRatios',   ),   8 =>    array (     0 => 'dimensions',     1 => 'dimensionSizes',   ), )
constants.doc: Where a settings node keeps preset lists, at its root and under each block.

constants.name: APPEARANCE_TOOLS
constants.value: array (   'background' =>    array (     0 => 'backgroundImage',     1 => 'backgroundSize',     2 => 'gradient',   ),   'border' =>    array (     0 => 'color',     1 => 'radius',     2 => 'style',     3 => 'width',   ),   'color' =>    array (     0 => 'link',     1 => 'heading',     2 => 'button',     3 => 'caption',   ),   'dimensions' =>    array (     0 => 'aspectRatio',     1 => 'height',     2 => 'minHeight',     3 => 'minWidth',     4 => 'width',   ),   'position' =>    array (     0 => 'sticky',   ),   'spacing' =>    array (     0 => 'blockGap',     1 => 'margin',     2 => 'padding',   ),   'typography' =>    array (     0 => 'lineHeight',     1 => 'textColumns',   ), )
constants.doc:
What appearanceTools switches on, group by group in the order the
reference appends the groups it has to add; a group already present
keeps its place and gains the flags at its end.

methods.name: normalize
methods.doc:
A settings node as written (theme.json, a variation, or the site
editor's post) with its presets keyed by origin and appearanceTools
expanded.

params.name: origin
params.doc: theme for a theme's file, custom for the site editor's

methods.name: resolved
methods.doc: Every var:preset|kind|slug token replaced by the custom property it names.

methods.name: withAppearanceTools
methods.doc: The flag itself goes; a flag the node already sets keeps its value.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateHierarchy
classes.doc:
The templates a block theme falls back through for a template slug, as
get_template_hierarchy builds them (probe rest-templates-lookup): the
slug itself, then its family's chain to index. A single entry's slug
reaches single-{type} and single only when the type is registered (and
goes straight to singular when not); a taxonomy's reaches taxonomy-{tax}
and taxonomy only when the taxonomy is; pages, categories, tags and
authors step through their bare name when the slug has more to it. A
prefix names the next step outright. A custom template is a page's.

methods.name: for
methods.signature: for(string $slug, bool $custom, string $prefix, array $types, array $taxonomies): array
methods.doc: A slug's fallback chain, most specific first, ending at index.

methods.name: chain
methods.doc: What follows a slug (or a prefix) down to index.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: The registered name a slug's remainder starts with (the whole of it, or before a hyphen), the longest first. @param list<string> $names

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateIndex
classes.doc:
Every block template and template part the site offers, in the order the
reference lists them: the rows the site editor saved first (newest post
date first), then the theme's own files in the order the directory hands
them back, then whatever a plugin registered. A saved row shadows the
theme file of the same slug and reports has_theme_file so the file can
be restored by deleting the row.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every template of a type: the theme's files with the saved rows over them.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: Null when the id names another theme, or a slug nothing provides.

methods.name: themeSlug
methods.doc: The theme the index reads.

methods.name: hasFile
methods.doc: Whether the theme ships a file for a slug.

methods.name: authorText
methods.doc:
Who the caller is told made this: the theme's own name for anything
that has a file behind it, the plugin for a registered one, the
author's display name for a row a person saved, and the site's name
when nobody is recorded.

methods.name: originalSource
methods.doc: theme when a file backs it, plugin when one registered it, user when someone saved it, else site.

methods.name: isCustom
methods.doc: A slug the reference does not name in its default template types is a custom template.

methods.name: defaults
methods.doc: The default template types.

methods.name: markup
methods.doc:
Markup as a caller of the REST route sees it: patterns spliced in
where the template only named them, then every template-part block
told which theme it belongs to. A record carries the markup as
stored, because that is what get_block_templates() hands a plugin.

methods.name: fileTitle
methods.doc:
A theme file's title: the default template types name the hierarchy
slugs, theme.json names the rest, and a slug neither knows about is
its own title, verbatim rather than prettified.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePartTheme
classes.doc:
A template-part block inside a template says which theme's part it means.
The theme's own files usually leave that out, and the reference fills the
active theme in on the way out, for saved rows as much as for files. It
appends the attribute and leaves every other byte of the markup alone.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Template part blocks with the theme attribute set.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePatterns
classes.doc:
A template can name a pattern instead of carrying its blocks, and the
reference hands the caller the blocks: every "wp:pattern" delimiter is
replaced by the pattern's own markup before a template or part is
served. A slug the theme does not know stays exactly as it is, which is
what tells an editor the pattern went missing rather than the block.

methods.name: expand
methods.doc: Markup with its pattern blocks replaced by the patterns' content.

methods.name: closerAt
methods.doc: The offset past a self-closing delimiter's "/-->", or null when it is not one.

methods.name: stamped
methods.doc:
The pattern's own name rides on the block it opens, so an editor can
still see which pattern a stretch of blocks came from. Only a pattern
that IS one block gets the stamp: several blocks have no single
wrapper to carry the name, and the reference leaves those anonymous.
The stamp goes on the pattern's raw markup, before any pattern nested
inside it is spliced in, so when that one block is itself a pattern
reference the stamp goes away with it.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateRecord
classes.doc:
One block template or template part, whatever it came from: a theme
file, a row the site editor saved, or a template a plugin registered.
The id every caller uses is "<theme>//<slug>" in all three cases.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $theme, string $slug, string $type, string $content, string $title, string $description, string $source, ?string $origin, bool $hasThemeFile, int $author, ?string $modified, ?string $date, int $wpId, string $status = 'publish', ?string $area = NULL, ?string $plugin = NULL)

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The reference's template id: theme//slug.

methods.name: isPart
methods.doc: Whether this is a template part.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateWriter
classes.doc:
Saving and removing block templates. A template the theme ships is never
touched on disk: editing one writes a wp_template row that shadows the
file, and deleting that row is what "reset to the theme version" means.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
Writes the site's own copy of a template, creating the row the first
time. Returns the post id.
shapes: @param array{title?: string, content?: string, description?: string, area?: string} $fields

params.name: fields
params.shape: array{title?: string, content?: string, description?: string, area?: string}

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: Moves a site copy to the trash, which hands the theme's file back.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Deletes a saved template row.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Templates
classes.doc:
Which template renders a resolution, and where its markup comes from:
a wp_template post saved from the site editor (matched by slug and the
theme term) wins over the theme's file. Parts resolve the same way
through wp_template_part.

methods.name: forResolution
methods.doc: The template that renders a resolution, or null.

methods.name: template
methods.doc: A template's markup by slug, saved first.

methods.name: part
methods.doc: A template part's markup by slug, saved first.

methods.name: partSource
methods.doc:
Where a template part comes from: a part saved for the theme (its
post id), the theme's file (its path), or nowhere; with its markup.

methods.name: candidates
methods.doc: The block-theme template hierarchy for each kind of resolution.

methods.name: userStyles
methods.doc:
The site editor's saved global styles for the active theme, when any.
An emptied node is stored as [] and reads as nothing, the way the
reference reads it; a list where a map belongs is dropped the same way.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A page's chosen custom template, from _wp_page_template meta.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc:
Plugins reshape the hierarchy through the reference's
"{type}_template_hierarchy" filters (WooCommerce sends its taxonomies to
archive-product that way); the filter sees PHP file names and hands
back the same, which become slugs again.

methods.name: savedRow
shapes: @return array{ID: int|string, post_content: string}|null the newest published template of a type (and slug) saved for the theme

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Theme
classes.doc:
The active block theme on disk, read as data: theme.json, the templates
and parts directories, and the patterns index. A child theme's files
win and its parent fills in what the child does not define; theme.json
merges the same way, with the child's preset lists replacing the
parent's whole. The engine reads the site's installed theme the way it
reads the site's database; it never runs the theme's PHP.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The active block theme, or null under a classic one.

methods.name: forStyles
methods.doc:
The active theme as styling data (theme.json present), whether or not
it is a block theme; the classic renderer prints its presets where the
reference prints a classic theme's global styles.

methods.name: parentSlug
methods.doc: The theme's own name, and the parent's, for body classes.

methods.name: json
methods.doc: The theme.json with the parent's merged in; with plugins loaded, through wp_theme_json_data_theme.

methods.name: styleFiles
methods.doc:
Every JSON file under styles/, the parent theme's first and each
theme's in path order: block style partials and style variations alike.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
Layered theme.json: maps merge key by key, lists (palettes, font
sizes, template parts) replace as a whole.

methods.name: templateFile
methods.doc: A template file's markup, or null.

methods.name: partFile
methods.doc: A template part file's markup, or null.

methods.name: partPath
methods.doc: The file a template part is read from: this theme's, else its parent's; null when neither has one.

methods.name: name
methods.doc:
The theme's display name, as the stylesheet header states it; a child
theme answers with its own. Falls back to theme.json's title, then the
folder name.

methods.name: fileSlugs
methods.doc:
Every template (or part) slug the theme offers, the child's files
first and the parent's after, each in the order the directory hands
them back: the reference walks these directories unsorted and its
template list carries that order through.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A template title and description the theme declares for a custom template slug.

methods.name: partTitle
methods.doc: The title theme.json gives a template part, when it names one.

methods.name: partArea
methods.doc: The template-part area declared in theme.json (header, footer, or uncategorized).

methods.name: pattern
methods.doc: A pattern's markup, with its PHP text subset interpreted; null when unknown.

methods.name: patternMeta
methods.doc:
A pattern's declared Block Types and Categories, the header fields a
plugin reads to tell (say) a header pattern from any other.

methods.name: patternHeader
methods.doc:
The header fields a pattern declares, as the metadata attribute the
reference writes onto the pattern's first block when it splices the
pattern into a template. A field the header omits is omitted here.
shapes: @return array{patternName: string, name: string, description?: string, categories?: list<string>}|null

methods.name: styleUri
methods.doc: The theme's stylesheet URL when it ships one; a child's own, else nothing (the parent's is not enqueued for it).

methods.name: rawJson
methods.doc: The theme.json as written, the parent's merged in.

methods.name: withStylePartials
methods.doc:
A theme's styles/ folder can hold block style variations: a JSON file
with blockTypes and a slug (else the file name) whose styles become
styles.blocks.{type}.variations.{slug} for each named block type. The
parent's partials load first, the child's over them.

methods.name: safe
methods.doc: A template or part name is a file name, never a path.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeJsonData
classes.doc:
The theme's theme.json as plugins and the theme's own functions may
change it (wp_theme_json_data_theme, a WP_Theme_JSON_Data they update
with presets and settings of their own), as the reference's resolver
hands it to them. Worked out once a request for each set of callbacks,
so a filter added late still counts.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The theme layer through wp_theme_json_data_theme; as written when nothing filters it. @param array<string, mixed> $json

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeStyles
classes.doc:
The active theme's global styles as wp/v2/global-styles/themes/{stylesheet}
reports them: the engine's defaults (captured from the reference under a
theme with no theme.json) with the theme's own settings and styles over
them, and the style variations the theme ships.

params.name: theme
params.doc: null under a theme without theme.json: the defaults alone

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The site's active theme as styling data, whether or not it is a block theme.

methods.name: settings
methods.doc: Settings: presets by origin, appearanceTools expanded, the defaults underneath.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: Styles: the theme's over the defaults, block style partials and section styles in, every var:preset token resolved.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc:
The style variations under styles/: every JSON file there that names
no blockTypes (those are block style partials), the parent theme's
first, in path order, $schema dropped and the nodes normalized the
way the theme's own are.

methods.name: withSectionStyles
methods.doc:
A root styles.variations node names section styles by the slug of
the block style partial that declares them; each lands under every
block type that partial names, the blocks it has to add in name
order, and the root node goes.

methods.name: partials
methods.doc: The block style partials under styles/: slug => the block types each names.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\UserStyles
classes.doc:
The site editor's saved global styles: one wp_global_styles post per
theme, tied to it by the wp_theme term, holding a versioned JSON body
of the settings and styles the editor wrote. Every changed save leaves
a revision behind, as a post's does.

methods.name: idFor
methods.doc: The newest published global-styles post carrying the theme's term, or null.

methods.name: ensure
methods.doc: The theme's post, made the way the reference makes it when there is none yet.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: The post when it is a global-styles post, else null.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc:
What a global-styles body holds; a missing, malformed, or list-shaped
node is empty, as the reference reads it.

methods.name: isBlank
methods.doc: True when the body carries nothing at all under settings or styles, malformed or not.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
Replaces what the caller names (null keeps the stored value), stamps
the modified time, and snapshots a revision when anything changed.

classes.name: Minn\Widgets\WidgetForms
classes.doc:
The core widgets' settings forms, the markup a widget's form() prints and
wp/v2/widgets returns as rendered_form, character for character as the
reference prints it (probe rest-widgets): field ids and names from the
widget's number, values escaped, defaults filled in. The whitespace is
the reference's own and is part of the answer.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: The title field most widgets open with.

methods.name: titleOnly
methods.doc: search, meta, calendar: the title alone.

methods.name: pages
methods.doc: The pages widget: title, sort order, pages to leave out.

methods.name: archives
methods.doc: The archives widget: title, dropdown and counts boxes.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: The categories widget: title, dropdown, counts and hierarchy boxes.

methods.name: recentPosts
methods.doc: The recent posts widget: title, how many, whether to show dates.

methods.name: recentComments
methods.doc: The recent comments widget: title and how many.

methods.name: customHtml
methods.doc: The custom HTML widget: hidden title and content fields its editor syncs.

methods.name: block
methods.doc: The block widget: its block markup in a textarea.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The text widget in its visual mode: hidden fields the editor syncs.

methods.name: tagCloud
methods.doc: The tag cloud: its title, the taxonomies that show a cloud (tags unless one is chosen), and the counts box.

methods.name: navMenu
methods.doc: The navigation menu widget: a note when there are no menus, else the title and the menu to show.

methods.name: rss
methods.doc:
wp_widget_rss_form: the feed's address, title, item count (1 to 20,
10 by default) and the three display boxes, each shown unless the
caller hides it, and ticked when the settings say so (or, saying
nothing, when it is shown).
